## 2.3 Feature Relationships

Every relationship recorded here is visible either in `Hello.java` itself, in the commands documented in `README.md`, or in the artifact dependencies listed in `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md`. No relationship is inferred from a pattern that the repository does not exhibit; in particular there is no service call, message, queue, schema or shared datastore anywhere in the system to relate features through.

### 2.3.1 Feature Dependency Map

The diagram shows **direct** dependencies only, with an arrow pointing from a prerequisite to the feature that depends on it. The complete set, including indirect dependencies, follows in the table below.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph External["External to the repository"]
        JDK["JDK toolchain<br/>javac / java / javadoc"]
        GITHOST["Git and hosting platform<br/>clone, branch, merge"]
        OSPROC["OS process contract<br/>stdout, stderr, exit status"]
        GPL["GPL v3 instrument<br/>FSF, 29 June 2007"]
    end

    subgraph RuntimeGroup["Runtime behaviour — Hello.java"]
        F001["F-001 JVM Entry-Point Contract<br/>lines 6, 15"]
        F002["F-002 Fixed Console Message Emission<br/>line 17"]
        F003["F-003 Deterministic Normal Termination<br/>lines 18-19"]
    end

    subgraph BuildGroup["Build and distribution"]
        F004["F-004 Dependency-Free<br/>JDK-Only Build and Launch"]
        F005["F-005 Source-Only Distribution<br/>via Git Remote"]
    end

    subgraph DocGroup["Documentation and licence"]
        F006["F-006 GPLv3 Licensing<br/>LICENSE"]
        F007["F-007 Operator Guide<br/>README.md"]
        F008["F-008 In-Source Documentation<br/>four comments"]
        F009["F-009 Project-Status Record<br/>blitzy/documentation/"]
    end

    JDK --> F004
    GITHOST --> F005
    GPL --> F006
    F004 --> F001
    F001 --> F002
    F002 --> F003
    F002 --> OSPROC
    F003 --> OSPROC
    F001 --> F008
    F004 --> F008
    F001 --> F007
    F004 --> F007
    F006 --> F007
    F007 --> F009
    F008 --> F009
    F001 --> F005
    F006 --> F005
    F007 --> F005
    F008 --> F005
    F009 --> F005
```

| Feature | Depends on | Nature of the dependency |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-001 | F-004 | The class must be compiled or source-launched before `main` can be invoked |
| F-002 | F-001 | The write at line 17 executes only inside the invoked `main` frame |
| F-003 | F-001, F-002 | The return at line 19 follows the single write; there is no other path to it |
| F-004 | F-001 | The unit F-004 compiles and launches is the class and entry point F-001 declares |
| F-005 | F-001, F-006, F-007, F-008, F-009 | The distribution channel carries exactly these tracked artifacts |
| F-006 | None | Independent of the runtime features it governs; no code or tool reads `LICENSE` |
| F-007 | F-001, F-002, F-003, F-004, F-006 | The guide documents their behaviour, their commands and the licence terms |
| F-008 | F-001, F-002, F-003, F-004 | The comments document those three constructs; `javadoc` from the same toolchain measures their coverage |
| F-009 | F-001 … F-008 | The record reports on the delivery and validation of every other feature |

**Dependency properties worth noting.** The runtime chain F-004 → F-001 → F-002 → F-003 is strictly linear and has no branch: `Hello.java` contains no `if`, `for`, `while` or `switch` statement and no `try`/`catch`, so there is exactly one path through the system. The documentation features form a second layer that depends on the first but is never depended upon by it — nothing in `Hello.java` reads `README.md`, `LICENSE` or anything under `blitzy/documentation/`, so a documentation change cannot alter runtime behaviour. F-006 is the only feature with no prerequisite inside the repository.

### 2.3.2 Integration Points

The system integrates with exactly four things outside itself, consistent with Section 1.2.1.3. Each row below names the features that meet at that seam.

| Integration point | Features involved | Interface and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JDK toolchain | F-004, F-001, F-008 | `javac` compiles the single unit, `java` launches the class or the source file, `javadoc` measures comment coverage. `Project Guide.md` Appendix D records OpenJDK 25.0.3; Appendix F assigns each tool its role |
| Operating-system process contract | F-002, F-003 | stdout receives the greeting, stderr stays empty, exit status is 0 (`Hello.java` lines 16–19; `README.md` line 63) |
| Git and its hosting platform | F-005, F-009 | Clone, branch and the merge of pull request #1 (`2a78292`); `git` also supplies the pre-comment baseline used by the F-008 verification procedures (`Project Guide.md` §9.6, Appendix F) |
| GPL v3 obligations | F-006, F-007, F-005 | Copyleft terms in `LICENSE`, referenced from `README.md` line 77, carried with every conveyed copy |

**Internal seams.** Two integration points are internal to the repository and are validated as such. The **guide-to-toolchain seam** is the requirement that every command in `README.md` execute exactly as written; `Project Guide.md` §2.1 records 2.5 hours of "Guide-to-toolchain seam validation" that executed each documented command in scratch copies of the repository and compared the guide's fenced expected-output block byte-for-byte against real stdout. The **comment-to-code seam** is the requirement that each comment describe the construct it is attached to; `Project Guide.md` §5.1 rows 1–3 validate placement and additions-only status, while §3 notes that comment wording itself "is not executed and prose accuracy is not machine-checkable".

### 2.3.3 Shared Components

| Shared component | Path | Features that share it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The single compilation unit | `Hello.java` (20 lines / 1,073 bytes, blob `3fd76ce`) | F-001, F-002, F-003, F-008 — and F-004 as its build input |
| The `main` method body | `Hello.java` lines 15–19 | F-001 (signature), F-002 (line 17), F-003 (line 19) |
| The output literal | `Hello.java` line 17 | F-002 defines it; F-007 republishes it at `README.md` lines 59–61 as the operator-facing oracle |
| The operator guide | `README.md` (77 lines / 4,053 bytes, blob `3956e03`) | F-007 owns it; F-004 and F-006 are documented through it; F-005 distributes it |
| The licence instrument | `LICENSE` (674 lines / 35,149 bytes, blob `f288702`) | F-006 owns it; F-007 links to it; F-005 conveys it |
| The pre-comment baseline revision | `0726b1d` in Git history | F-008 verification (additions-only and behaviour-parity comparisons); F-005 provides the history that holds it |
| The out-of-tree scratch directory | generated per run by `mktemp -d` | F-004 (build destination), F-008 (`javadoc` output), F-009 (verification scratch space) |

The proportions matter to maintenance: four features share one 1,073-byte file, so any edit to `Hello.java` touches F-001, F-002, F-003 and F-008 simultaneously, and the change-impact rules in Section 2.6.4 are written on that basis.

### 2.3.4 Common Services

There are no common application services in this system. `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix B states the position without qualification: the program "binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call; there is no service, database, broker or cache in this project", and §9.1 adds that there is "no package manager step, no virtual environment, no container, no database, no broker and no bound port". The only shared facilities are therefore external tools and platform contracts:

| Common facility | Provided by | Consumed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compilation, launch and documentation tooling | The JDK on `PATH` (OpenJDK 25.0.3 as recorded) | F-004, F-001, F-008 |
| Standard output, standard error and exit status | The operating-system process contract | F-002, F-003 |
| Version control and baseline retrieval | `git` 2.51.0 | F-005, F-008, F-009 |
| POSIX shell utilities for verification (`grep`, `awk`, `diff`, `tr`, `od`, `cmp`) and `mktemp -d` | The host environment | F-004, F-007, F-008, F-009 |

No shared configuration, secret store or environment variable participates: `Project Guide.md` Appendix E records `JAVA_HOME` as not required and states that "No other variable and no secret is read by any tracked file".

### 2.3.5 Cross-Feature Process Flow

The four operator workflows enumerated in Section 1.3.1.1 (`W-1` … `W-4`) are the only processes in which features interact. The flow below shows how each workflow traverses the feature set; the detailed process decomposition belongs to Section 4 (Process Flowchart) of this specification.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start(["Operator at repository root"]) --> Guide["Read README.md<br/>F-007-RQ-002"]
    Guide --> Choice{"Which documented<br/>launch path?"}
    Choice -->|"W-1 compile in place"| CompileA["javac Hello.java<br/>F-004-RQ-003"]
    Choice -->|"W-2 compile out of tree"| CompileB["javac -d $B Hello.java<br/>F-004-RQ-006"]
    Choice -->|"W-3 single-file launch"| Direct["java Hello.java<br/>F-004-RQ-004 — JDK 11+"]
    CompileA --> Untracked["Untracked Hello.class<br/>F-005-RQ-002 — do not commit"]
    Untracked --> LaunchA["java Hello<br/>F-001-RQ-002"]
    CompileB --> LaunchB["java -cp $B Hello<br/>F-001-RQ-002"]
    LaunchA --> Emit["One write to stdout<br/>F-002-RQ-001, F-002-RQ-002"]
    LaunchB --> Emit
    Direct --> Emit
    Emit --> Term["Normal return, no System.exit<br/>F-003-RQ-001"]
    Term --> Verify["W-4 compare stdout, stderr and exit status<br/>F-002-RQ-004, F-003-RQ-002, F-003-RQ-003"]
```

| Workflow | Features exercised | Requirements verified end to end |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W-1 — compile in place, then run | F-007 → F-004 → F-001 → F-002 → F-003, with F-005 governing the untracked artifact | F-004-RQ-003, F-001-RQ-002, F-002-RQ-001, F-003-RQ-002, F-005-RQ-002 |
| W-2 — compile to a fresh directory outside the checkout, then run | F-007 → F-004 → F-001 → F-002 → F-003 | F-004-RQ-006, F-004-RQ-005, F-001-RQ-002, F-002-RQ-001, F-003-RQ-002 |
| W-3 — launch the source file directly | F-007 → F-004 → F-001 → F-002 → F-003 | F-004-RQ-004, F-002-RQ-004, F-003-RQ-002 |
| W-4 — verify the output contract | F-002 and F-003 against the oracle published by F-007 | F-002-RQ-001, F-002-RQ-002, F-002-RQ-003, F-003-RQ-002, F-003-RQ-003 |

All three launch workflows converge on the same single write and the same normal return, which is why `README.md` line 46 can state that "Both paths produce byte-identical standard output" and why `Project Guide.md` §3 records runtime parity as 6 of 6 checks across both documented paths.


## 2.4 Implementation Considerations

### 2.4.1 Technical Constraints

| Feature | Technical constraint | Source of the constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-001 | The class must stay in the default package, which means code in a named package cannot import it — Section 1.3.2.4 records reuse as a library from packaged code as unsupported. The file name must continue to match the public class | `Hello.java` line 6; `Project Guide.md` §9.8 |
| F-002 | The payload is a compile-time constant with no interpolation, so it cannot be parameterised without changing the published oracle. The trailing separator must remain host-supplied | `Hello.java` line 17; `README.md` line 63 |
| F-003 | Termination must remain by normal return; adding `System.exit`, a loop, a thread or a blocking read would break the single-outcome contract | `Hello.java` line 18; `Project Guide.md` §2.6-class change rules restated in Section 2.6.4 |
| F-004 | No dependency manifest, no `module-info.java` and no `--release` or `--source` setting may be introduced without forfeiting the JDK-only property; the Java language level stays "None declared" | `README.md` line 18; `Project Guide.md` Appendix D |
| F-005 | No `.gitignore` and no `.gitattributes` exist, so build output must be kept out of the tree by command discipline and line endings must be preserved by editor discipline | Verified absence; `README.md` line 30; `Project Guide.md` §5.2 divergence 5 |
| F-006 | `LICENSE` must remain verbatim; a per-file notice cannot be added until a copyright holder and year are recorded, which no tracked file does | `Project Guide.md` §5.2 divergence 5 |
| F-007 | The guide is constrained by its own asserted structure: eight sections in order, the summary first, a 70-word / 8-line summary budget, exactly two relative links and exactly two stable-symbol citations | `Project Guide.md` §5.1 rows 5–11, §9.6 |
| F-008 | Comments may be added but no executable line altered; the implicit default constructor can carry no doc comment, so coverage is capped at 2 of 3 without a structural change | `Project Guide.md` §5.1 row 3, §5.2 divergence 4 |
| F-009 | Verification tooling must not be committed — build, test and CI files are out of scope — so checks run from a scratch directory and nothing re-runs them automatically | `Project Guide.md` §9.6, §1.4 |

Two constraints are repository-wide. First, **`Hello.java` is stored with CRLF on all 20 lines with no `.gitattributes`**, so any editor that normalises line endings rewrites the whole file; `Project Guide.md` §6 carries this as a Medium-severity technical risk, "Open — accepted by design". Second, **there is no automated gate**: no build descriptor, test suite or CI workflow is committed, so as §1.4 puts it, "Nothing re-runs the documentation checks on future changes."

### 2.4.2 Performance Requirements

No performance requirement exists anywhere in the repository. There is no latency, throughput, availability, concurrency or resource target in `Hello.java`, `README.md` or `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md`, no instrumentation or timing code, and Section 1.3.2.4 records using the program as a performance, load or soak benchmark as an unsupported use case. The table records the only quantified properties the repository does state, so that a reader is not left to infer targets that do not exist.

| Feature | Quantified property recorded in the repository | Where recorded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-001 | One method frame, one statement, no loop or branch | `Hello.java` lines 15–19 (five executable lines in the file) |
| F-002 | 16-character literal; 17 bytes of stdout where the separator is LF; exactly one write | `README.md` line 63; `Project Guide.md` §4 |
| F-003 | Exit status 0; empty stderr | `README.md` line 63; `Project Guide.md` §9.7 |
| F-004 | Zero compiler diagnostics, including under `-Xlint:all -Werror`; one compilation unit; zero dependencies to resolve | `Project Guide.md` §3, Appendix A |
| F-005 | 5 tracked files, 925,008 tracked bytes, zero tags, zero tracked binaries | `git ls-files`, `git tag`; `Project Guide.md` Appendix C |
| F-007 | 77 lines; 8 sections; 55-word summary against a 70-word budget | `Project Guide.md` §5.1 rows 6 and 9 |
| F-008 | 15 added lines, 0 removed; at most 1 `javadoc` warning; coverage 2 of 3 documentable members | `Project Guide.md` §3, §5.1 row 3 |
| F-009 | 49 of 49 checks passed; 11 open items; 32.0 of 38.0 hours | `Project Guide.md` §1.2, §1.4, §3 |

### 2.4.3 Scalability Considerations

Scalability in the conventional sense does not apply: the system is a single-process, single-threaded program that writes one line and exits, with no listener, no request path and no state. What does scale — and what the repository's own records treat as the real concern — is the **documentation-to-code ratio and the verification burden**.

| Feature | Scalability consideration |
| --- | --- |
| F-001 … F-003 | Fixed cost by construction. One compilation unit, one entry point, one statement; no queue, pool, cache or connection exists to size. Every run is independent because no state persists between runs |
| F-004 | Build cost is one `javac` invocation with nothing to resolve; there is no incremental-build or caching concern because there is no second compilation unit. Adding one would immediately create the build-ordering and manifest concerns the project currently has none of |
| F-005 | The tracked footprint is dominated by documentation: 884,733 of 925,008 bytes are the two files under `blitzy/documentation/`, against 1,073 bytes of source. Clone size therefore grows with each documentation generation round, not with the program |
| F-007, F-009 | Verification effort grows with documented claims, not with code: 37 acceptance assertions plus 12 toolchain checks already cover a 20-line source file and a 77-line guide, and `Project Guide.md` §1.4 records that nothing re-runs them |
| F-008 | Comment coverage is capped at 2 of 3 documentable members; the coverage ratio cannot improve without adding a declared constructor, so the metric does not scale with further comment work |

### 2.4.4 Security Implications

`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §6 states the baseline: the program "reads no input, dereferences no argument, opens no resource, binds no port, makes no network call and has no dependency manifest, so there is no injection surface, no supply-chain exposure, no authentication or authorisation surface and no data-at-rest concern", and §1.5 records that no credential, key, network egress, environment variable or secret is used anywhere. The implications that do exist are therefore confined to the build and repository-hygiene surface.

| Feature | Security implication | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| F-001 | `args` is never dereferenced, so hostile arguments cannot influence behaviour; `Project Guide.md` §4 records runs with "shell and injection payloads" producing identical output | No exposure |
| F-002 | The output literal is a constant with no interpolation, so there is no format-string or output-injection vector; stdout is the only sink written | No exposure |
| F-003 | No resource is opened, so nothing can leak on exit; there is no error path that could disclose internal state through stderr | No exposure |
| F-004 | The compiler output destination is the one real consideration: a fixed, predictable path "can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it" (`README.md` line 30). The documented command generates a unique owner-readable-only directory with `mktemp -d` | `Mitigated` per `Project Guide.md` §6 |
| F-005 | With no `.gitignore`, an in-place compile leaves an untracked class file that could be committed by accident; the control is documentation plus the instruction "Do not commit the class file either way". Commit signing is recorded as deferred infrastructure | `Open`, Low severity (§6) |
| F-006 | The absent per-file copyright and warranty notice is a licensing-compliance gap rather than a technical vulnerability; it awaits a recorded rights holder | `Open`, Owner decision (§1.4) |
| F-007, F-009 | Documented commands must stay safe by construction, since an operator will paste them verbatim; §6 identifies the reintroduction of a predictable compiler-output path in a future edit as the concrete risk, mitigated by stating the rationale beside the command | `Mitigated` (§6) |
| F-008 | Comments are not executed and carry no security weight; the only related concern is that they must not be allowed to drift from the code they describe |  No exposure |

There is no authentication, authorisation, encryption, secret-management or audit requirement anywhere in this system, and none is asserted here.

### 2.4.5 Maintenance Requirements

| Feature | Maintenance requirement |
| --- | --- |
| F-001 | Preserve the signature, the default package and the non-dereference of `args`; any change to the class's member set contradicts the class Javadoc at lines 1–5 and the contract Section 1.3.1.1 records |
| F-002 | Any edit to the literal must be propagated to the fenced expected-output block at `README.md` lines 59–61, or the published oracle and the program diverge |
| F-003 | Keep the method free of `System.exit`, loops, threads and blocking reads so that the single-outcome contract continues to hold |
| F-004 | Re-run `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` after any source edit — it is the project's only static-analysis surface. Confirm the JDK 11 floor on a real JDK 11 runtime or soften the claim (`Project Guide.md` §1.6, 1.0 h, Medium) |
| F-005 | Publish the branch and merge the change so the documentation reaches the default branch (§1.6, 0.5 h, High); keep the tracked set free of build output; edit `Hello.java` in byte mode and re-run the line-ending census afterwards |
| F-006 | Leave `LICENSE` verbatim; decide the per-file notice question, which requires naming a copyright holder and year (§1.6, part of the 2.0-hour hygiene item) |
| F-007 | Correct the Project Layout claim at line 67 so it matches the five-file tree — Section 1.3.2.2 notes this is not covered by any recorded item; decide the citation-coverage question, amending the two-reference budget and its check first (§1.6, 1.0 h, Medium); review the rendered guide on the hosting platform (§1.6, 0.5 h, Medium) |
| F-008 | Always pass the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` as the comment-census baseline, or four checks fail vacuously against a correct tree (§1.6, 1.0 h, High); re-emit CRLF on every added line; expect exactly one `javadoc` warning and treat a second as a regression |
| F-009 | Keep the record's figures reconciled and its stale claims corrected — Appendix C repeats the same flatness error as `README.md` line 67; decide whether to adopt an automated gate, currently `Deferred` / Owner decision (§1.4) |

**Aggregate maintenance position.** `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §1.4 records **11 open items** with "No defect is open in the delivered code", and §2.2 itemises **6.0 remaining hours** across six tasks — two High (verification baseline, branch publication), three Medium (citation coverage, JDK 11 confirmation, rendered-guide review) and one Low (the four hygiene decisions). Six of the eleven items are explicitly "Owner decision", and §2.3 records confidence in the remaining estimates as medium "because four of the six items are decisions whose scope the owner sets rather than fixed units of work".

| A-7 | The prior committed register is the correct provenance for identifiers F-001 … F-007 | `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` §2.1 and §2.6.3 define that register and anchor it at commit `0726b1d` |

### 2.6.4 Change-Impact Rules

These rules follow from the dependencies in Section 2.3.1 and are stated so that a reviewer can tell from a diff alone which acceptance criteria must be re-executed.

# 3. Technology Stack

## 3.1 Programming Languages

The language surface of this repository is exhaustively enumerable rather than representative. `git ls-files` returns five tracked paths, and a worktree-wide search across twenty source-file extensions — `.java`, `.py`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.kt`, `.swift`, `.m`, `.mm`, `.go`, `.rs`, `.rb`, `.c`, `.cpp`, `.h`, `.cs`, `.sh`, `.sql`, `.css`, `.html` — returns exactly one file: `./Hello.java`. The tracked extension census is one `.java`, three `.md` and one extension-less file (`LICENSE`).

**One language compiles. Two more appear only as content.** Java is the sole implementation language; Markdown and plain text carry the documentation and the licence, and POSIX shell appears only as copy-and-paste commands inside fenced blocks in `README.md`, never as a tracked script.

### 3.1.1 Language Inventory by Component

| Component | Language | Version / dialect | Artifact | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Executable program | **Java** | Language level **"None declared"** — no `--release` or `--source` setting exists anywhere in the repository (`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix D) | `Hello.java` — 20 lines, 1,073 bytes, 5 code lines, 15 comment lines, 0 tabs | The entire executable surface of the system |
| In-source API documentation | **Javadoc doc-comment syntax** | Validated by `javadoc -Xdoclint:all` (Appendix F) | `Hello.java` lines 1–5 and 7–14 | Class and entry-point documentation using the `{@code}` inline tag and the `@param args` block tag |
| Operator guide, project record, specification | **Markdown** | GitHub Flavored Markdown over CommonMark — "Determined by the hosting platform; no generator or renderer is part of the project" (Appendix D) | `README.md` (77 lines, 4,053 bytes, 4 fenced blocks, 2 tables, 2 relative links); `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` (476 lines, 45,009 bytes); `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` (839,724 bytes) | Human-readable documentation; read by no code or tool in the repository |
| Licence instrument | **Plain text** | None | `LICENSE` — 674 lines, 35,149 bytes | Verbatim GNU General Public License, Version 3, 29 June 2007 |
| Documented operator commands | **POSIX shell** | `bash`-tagged fenced blocks at `README.md` lines 26–28, 36–38 and 42–44, plus a `text`-tagged expected-output block at lines 59–61 | Content of `README.md` only | Commands an operator types; **no `.sh` file is tracked and no script is executed by the project** |

### 3.1.2 Java as the Sole Implementation Language

The whole program is `Hello.java`, and its language footprint is deliberately minimal:

| Construct | Location | Language generation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public class Hello` in the default package — no `package` statement | line 6 | JDK 1.0 |
| `public static void main(String[] args)` | line 15 | JDK 1.0 |
| `System.out.println(String)` | line 17 | JDK 1.0 |

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
    System.out.println("Hello from Java!");
}
```

No construct above the original language level appears anywhere in the file. A direct reading confirms the absence of generics, annotations, lambdas or method references, `var` local-variable inference, records, sealed types, text blocks, enhanced `switch`, `try`/`catch`, loops, conditionals, fields, explicit constructors and object instantiation. There is no `module-info.java`, so the class is not part of a named module.

**Why this matters for versioning.** Because the source uses only JDK 1.0-era constructs, it is compilable at every Java language level, which is precisely what supports `README.md` line 20's statement that the compile-then-run path "carries no such floor and works on considerably older releases." `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §9.1 records that this path was "exercised at release targets 11, 17 and 21."

The single **JDK 11 floor** that the repository does state is therefore **not a language-level floor at all** — it is a *launcher-capability* floor. `README.md` line 20 attaches it only to the direct source launch: "The direct source launch `java Hello.java` shown under Run is single-file source-code launch, which needs JDK 11 or later." <cite index="5-3,5-5">JEP 330, Launch Single-File Source-Code Programs, was introduced in the JDK 11 release; it allows a Java source file to be executed directly by the launcher, with the source compiled in memory and executed without producing a .class file on disk</cite> — which is exactly the "leaves no class file behind" behaviour `README.md` line 40 documents. <cite index="1-30,1-31">Under that JEP the class executed is the first top-level class found in the source file, and it must contain a declaration of the standard `public static void main(String[])` method</cite>; `Hello.java` lines 6 and 15 satisfy both conditions.

`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §1.6 records confirming this floor on a real JDK 11 runtime as an open Medium-priority item (1.0 hour), because only OpenJDK 25.0.3 was available when the project's own validation was run.

### 3.1.3 Languages Present Only as Content

Three languages appear in the tree without being part of the build or the runtime, and each is documented here so that a reader does not mistake content for tooling:

- **Markdown.** No generator, renderer, static-site tool or linter for Markdown is configured; `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix D records the dialect as determined by the hosting platform. The rendered appearance has never been verified — reviewing the rendered guide is a recorded open item (§1.6, 0.5 hour, Medium).
- **POSIX shell.** Every shell fragment in the repository is documentation. `README.md` line 30 embeds `B="$(mktemp -d)" && javac -d "$B" Hello.java` in prose, and `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §9.2, §9.4 and §9.6 embed further command blocks. No `.sh` file has ever been tracked in any of the 14 commits, and nothing in the repository invokes a shell.
- **Plain text.** `LICENSE` is legal text with no executable content.

### 3.1.4 Selection Criteria and Justification

The language choice follows directly from what the artifact is for, and every criterion below is traceable to a statement in the tree rather than to a general preference.

| Criterion | How Java satisfies it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The artifact must prove a Java toolchain works** | The program is the smallest unit that still exercises `javac`, class loading, `main` resolution and a write to standard output. Any other language would fail the purpose | `Hello.java`; Section 1.2.1.1's "canonical reference program" positioning |
| **A JDK alone must build and run it** | `java.lang` is imported implicitly, so no resolution step exists. The class Javadoc states the property outright: "imports nothing outside `java.lang`, so a JDK alone builds and runs it" | `Hello.java` lines 2–4; verified: zero `import` statements |
| **Zero dependency and zero supply-chain surface** | The only types referenced are `String` and `System`, both from `java.lang`; no manifest exists in which a dependency could be declared | `Hello.java` lines 15, 17; `README.md` line 18 |
| **Shortest possible launch command** | The default package lets the JVM resolve the class by the bare name `Hello`, with no classpath root, directory layout or module path to establish first. The class Javadoc records this as the reason | `Hello.java` line 4; `README.md` line 12 |
| **Portability preferred over a pinned, reproducible build** | The language level is left undeclared so the unit compiles on any JDK. `README.md` line 18: the repository "pins no Java version" and carries no file "in which a version could be recorded" | `README.md` line 18; Appendix D |
| **Two interchangeable launch paths for different audiences** | Compile-then-run works on older releases; single-file source launch (JDK 11+) leaves no artifact. Both are pure-Java paths needing no extra runtime | `README.md` lines 20, 40, 46 |

### 3.1.5 Language-Level Constraints and Dependencies

| Constraint | Consequence | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **No `--release` or `--source` setting may be introduced** | The Java language level must stay "None declared"; introducing one, or a `module-info.java`, would forfeit the JDK-only property recorded as constraint F-004 | Appendix D; Section 2.4.1 F-004 |
| **The file name must continue to match the public class** | `Hello.java` must hold `public class Hello`; breaking the correspondence yields `error: class Hello is public, should be declared in a file named Hello.java`, a failure mode recorded in `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §9.8 | `Hello.java` line 6; §9.8 |
| **The default package is a reuse boundary, not just a style** | Code in a named package cannot import a default-package class, so reuse of `Hello` as a library is an unsupported use case | Section 1.3.2.4; `Hello.java` line 4 |
| **Only the implicit `java.lang` import may be relied on** | Adding the first third-party or JDK-module import would introduce a resolution step and invalidate the dependency-free property | `Hello.java` lines 2–4 |
| **Source encoding is fixed by construction, not by configuration** | `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE` each contain **zero bytes at or above `0x80`** (verified directly), so any ASCII-superset source encoding decodes the file identically. No `-encoding` option is required, and none is recorded anywhere | Direct byte census; `Hello.java` line 17 (ASCII literal) |
| **Stored line endings are unmanaged** | `Hello.java` carries CRLF on **20 of 20 lines** while `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `Project Guide.md` are LF-only. There is no `.gitattributes`, and `git check-attr text eol -- Hello.java` reports both attributes "unspecified" with `core.autocrlf` and `core.eol` unset, so an editor that normalises endings would rewrite every line of the source | Direct census via `od`; `git check-attr`; Section 2.4.1 |
| **The output literal is a compile-time constant** | `"Hello from Java!"` has no interpolation, so the payload cannot be parameterised without changing the published oracle at `README.md` lines 59–61 | `Hello.java` line 17; Section 2.4.1 F-002 |

**Language-level security note.** The language surface removes whole vulnerability classes by construction rather than by control: `args` is never dereferenced (it occurs only on line 11 as a `@param` tag and line 15 as the signature, never on an executable line), the sole output is a constant with no format string, and no `try`, `catch`, `throw`, `new`, `System.in`, `Scanner` or `Thread` construct exists. Section 2.4.4 records the consequence — no injection surface, no supply-chain exposure, no authentication or authorisation surface and no data-at-rest concern.


## 3.2 Frameworks & Libraries

**No framework is used by this system, and exactly one library is — the portion of the Java Class Library that the language imports implicitly.** This is not an omission to be corrected but the property the artifact exists to demonstrate: `Hello.java` lines 2–4 state that the program "imports nothing outside `java.lang`, so a JDK alone builds and runs it," and `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix F closes with "No linter, formatter, documentation generator, build tool or test framework is configured in the repository, and none is introduced by this change."

### 3.2.1 Framework Inventory — A Verified Null Result

A framework dependency in a Java project must be declared in a manifest, vendored as an archive, or named in an `import`. All three channels were checked directly and all three are empty.

| Channel by which a framework could enter | Verification performed | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A build or dependency manifest | Existence test at the repository root for `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `build.xml`, `ivy.xml`, `Makefile`, `makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `requirements.txt`, `Pipfile`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `mvnw`, `.mvn/`, `gradle/` | **All 27 absent.** `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §9.3 states it directly: "None. There is no `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `Makefile`, `package.json` or lock file of any kind, and nothing is downloaded at build time" |
| A vendored archive or compiled artifact | Recursive search of the worktree for `*.jar`, `*.class`, `*.war`, `*.ear`, `*.zip`, `*.so`, `*.dll`, `*.exe`, `*.tar*` | **Zero matches.** No library is bundled and no compiled output is committed |
| An `import` statement or module requirement | `grep` for `^\s*(import\|package)` in `Hello.java`; existence test for `module-info.java` | **No `import`, no `package`, no `module-info.java`.** The only types named in the source are `String` and `System` |
| Historical introduction since removed | `git log --all --name-only` over all 14 commits across every branch | Only five files have **ever** been tracked. No manifest, lockfile or archive has existed at any point in the history |

Consequently there is no web framework, no dependency-injection container, no ORM, no HTTP client, no serialisation library, no logging framework, no test framework, no assertion library and no mocking library in this system. Section 1.3.2.1 records the same absences from the requirements side.

### 3.2.2 The Java Class Library — the Only Library Dependency

The single library dependency is the JDK's own class library, reached without an `import` because `java.lang` is imported implicitly by the language.

| API used | Declaring package | How it is reached | Line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `System.out` — the initialised standard-output stream | `java.lang` | Named directly; implicitly imported | 17 |
| `println(String)` | `java.io` (`PrintStream`, the declared type of `System.out`) | Resolved through `System.out`; **the type is never named in the source**, so no `import` is required | 17 |
| `String` — the element type of the entry-point parameter array and the type of the output literal | `java.lang` | Named directly; implicitly imported | 15, 17 |

This is the architecturally significant detail behind the zero-import claim: `println` is a `java.io.PrintStream` method, but because the source only ever names the *field* `System.out` and never the field's type, `java.lang` remains the only package the file must import. The class Javadoc's wording — "imports nothing outside `java.lang`" — is therefore exact.

The class library is **required but not vendored**. Section 2.6.2 K-7 states the boundary: "The requirement set is scoped to the repository, not to the JDK it runs on," so the JDK and its class library are an external dependency of the system rather than a component of it.

### 3.2.3 Compatibility Requirements

Because nothing is declared, compatibility is determined entirely by what the two documented workflows ask of the toolchain.

| Workflow | Minimum toolchain capability | Version floor | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `javac Hello.java` → `java Hello` (compile-then-run) | A `javac` that accepts JDK 1.0-era constructs and a JVM that resolves a default-package class by bare name | **None stated.** Documented as working on "considerably older releases"; exercised at release targets **11, 17 and 21** | `README.md` line 20; `Project Guide.md` §9.1 |
| `B="$(mktemp -d)" && javac -d "$B" Hello.java` → `java -cp "$B" Hello` (out-of-tree compile) | The same, plus `javac -d` and `java -cp`, both long-standing options | None stated | `README.md` line 30; Appendix A |
| `java Hello.java` (single-file source launch) | A launcher implementing source-file mode | **JDK 11 or later** | `README.md` lines 20, 40; <cite index="3-1">JEP 330, added in JDK 11</cite> |
| `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` (static-analysis gate) | `javac` with the `-Xlint` and `-Werror` options | None stated; run on OpenJDK 25.0.3 | Appendix A; Appendix F |
| `javadoc -Xdoclint:all` / `javadoc -d "$B/jd" -quiet` (comment-coverage check) | `javadoc` with `-Xdoclint` | None stated; run on OpenJDK 25.0.3 | Appendix A; Appendix F |

**Recorded toolchain version.** `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix D records **OpenJDK 25.0.3** for `java`, `javac` and `javadoc`, and §9 states that "Every command below was executed against this repository on a Linux host with OpenJDK 25.0.3." <cite index="12-3">Java SE 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25 are the LTS releases</cite>, and <cite index="13-22">Java 25 was released in 2025 as the current LTS under a two-year LTS cadence</cite> — so the recorded toolchain is an update of the current long-term-support line, and the three exercised compile-then-run targets (11, 17, 21) are themselves all LTS releases spanning the range from the single-file-launch floor to the LTS immediately preceding the recorded version.

**The one compatibility gap.** No JDK 11 runtime was available when the project's own validation ran, so the JDK 11 floor is asserted from the feature's documented availability rather than observed. `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §1.6 carries "Confirm the 'JDK 11 or later' floor on a real JDK 11 runtime, or soften the claim" as an open Medium-priority 1.0-hour item, and Section 2.1's F-004 status records the same partial. This specification's own environment reproduces the constraint: `command -v java javac javadoc` returns nothing and `JAVA_HOME` is unset, so no version claim here was re-derived by execution.

### 3.2.4 Justification for the No-Framework Position

| Justification | Supporting evidence |
| --- | --- |
| **A framework would defeat the artifact's purpose.** The value of the program is that it isolates the toolchain: if `javac` and `java` succeed, the toolchain works. Any framework would make a failure ambiguous between the toolchain and the dependency | Section 1.2.2.3's "zero external dependencies, zero configuration" approach; `Hello.java` lines 2–4 |
| **It eliminates the supply-chain attack surface entirely rather than managing it.** With no manifest there is nothing to resolve, pin, scan or update, and no transitive graph | `Project Guide.md` §6 records "no supply-chain exposure"; §9.3 "None"; §1.5 "no credential, key, network egress, environment variable or secret is used by anything in this project" |
| **Build cost is one `javac` invocation with nothing to download.** Section 2.4.3 records that there is no incremental-build or caching concern because there is no second compilation unit | `Project Guide.md` §9.3; Section 2.4.3 |
| **A framework could not be added without breaking a stated constraint.** Constraint F-004 forbids introducing a dependency manifest, and Section 2.6.4 records that "Adding a first third-party import or a second compilation unit" invalidates F-004-RQ-001/002 and F-005-RQ-001 | Section 2.4.1 F-004; Section 2.6.4 |
| **The functionality needs nothing more.** One write to one sink, no input, no state, no error path — the standard library covers the whole requirement with a single method call | `Hello.java` lines 16–18 |

### 3.2.5 Conventions and Standards Relied On in Place of Libraries

Two external *conventions* substitute for what a library or framework would otherwise supply. Neither is code, and neither is vendored.

| Standard | What it governs | Where it enters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Javadoc doc-comment conventions** (cited in `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §2.1 as the authoring standard) | Comment form and placement: class block at column 0, member block indented four spaces with `@param args` and no `@return`, both line comments at eight spaces (`Project Guide.md` §5.1 row 2) | `Hello.java` lines 1–5, 7–14, 16, 18 |
| **GitHub Flavored Markdown over CommonMark** | Rendering of the three Markdown documents; "no generator or renderer is part of the project" | `README.md`, `blitzy/documentation/*.md`; Appendix D |

One consequence of relying on the Javadoc convention rather than a tool-enforced rule is recorded and accepted: `javadoc` emits exactly one warning, `Hello.java:6: warning: use of default constructor, which does not provide a comment`. As `Project Guide.md` §5.2 explains, "a default constructor can carry no doc comment, and declaring one is a structural change the comment-only constraint forbids," which caps documentable-member coverage at 2 of 3. `Project Guide.md` §9.6 instructs that a second warning be treated as a regression.


## 3.3 Open Source Dependencies

**The system declares no open-source dependency and resolves nothing at build time.** `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §9.3 answers dependency installation in one word — "None." — and adds that "nothing is downloaded at build time." `README.md` line 18 states the same from the operator's side: the repository "has no dependency manifest, so nothing has to be resolved or downloaded before building."

This sub-section therefore documents two distinct things that a reader must not conflate: the **empty declared-dependency set**, and the **open-source software the system consumes from the host** without declaring it.

### 3.3.1 Declared Third-Party Dependencies

| Dimension | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| Declared dependencies | **Zero.** No manifest exists in which one could be declared (see Section 3.2.1 for the 27 existence tests performed) |
| Lockfiles | **None.** No `package-lock.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Pipfile.lock` or Gradle/Maven lock artifact exists, and none has ever been tracked in the 14-commit history |
| Vendored archives | **None.** A recursive search for `*.jar`, `*.war`, `*.ear`, `*.zip`, `*.so`, `*.dll` and `*.exe` returns zero matches |
| Transitive graph | **Not applicable.** With no direct dependency there is no transitive closure to resolve, pin or audit |
| Imports | **Zero `import` statements** in `Hello.java`; only `java.lang` is reached, implicitly |

### 3.3.2 Package Registries and Artifact Coordinates

| Dimension | Finding | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package registries consumed | **None.** No Maven Central, npm, PyPI or other registry is referenced, configured or reachable from any tracked file. `Project Guide.md` §9.1 records "No package manager step, no virtual environment, no container, no database, no broker and no bound port" | `Project Guide.md` §9.1, §9.3 |
| Repository/mirror configuration | **None.** No `settings.xml`, `.npmrc`, `pip.conf` or equivalent exists | Direct existence tests |
| Published coordinates for this artifact | **None declared anywhere.** There is no group ID, artifact ID or version coordinate, so the program is never published to, nor consumed from, an artifact repository | Section 2.1's F-005; Section 1.3.2.3 |
| Distribution channel | **Git clone only.** `git ls-files` returns five source and documentation files with no packaged artifact among them; `git tag` returns **zero tags across 14 commits**, so there is no release line | Direct verification |
| Release versioning | **None.** Section 2.6.3 records that requirement versions must be anchored to commit SHAs "because no tags exist" | Section 2.6.3 |

### 3.3.3 Open-Source Software Consumed from the Host

These components are genuinely open-source and genuinely required, but they are **host-supplied tooling, not entries in a dependency graph**. None is vendored, version-pinned or resolved by the project. Versions are those the repository records or that were observed directly in the environment used to produce this specification.

| Component | Version recorded / observed | How it is consumed | Source of the version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OpenJDK** — `java`, `javac`, `javadoc` | **25.0.3** (recorded); compile-then-run also exercised at release targets **11, 17, 21** | Invoked from `PATH`. `javac` compiles the single unit; `java` launches the class or the source file; `javadoc` measures comment coverage | `Project Guide.md` Appendix D, §9.1, §9 preamble |
| **Java Class Library** (`java.lang`, and `java.io.PrintStream` reached through `System.out`) | Ships with the JDK above | Implicitly imported; the only code dependency of `Hello.java` | `Hello.java` lines 2–4, 15, 17 |
| **Git** | **2.51.0** recorded in Appendix D as the version used for the project's verification run; **2.43.0** observed in this specification's environment | Clone, branch, merge, and the pre-comment baseline comparisons in the verification steps | Appendix D; `git --version` |
| **GNU coreutils and text utilities** — `grep`, `awk`, `diff`, `tr`, `od`, `cmp`, `iconv` | Not pinned or recorded | Assert the guide's structure and both files' stored byte format "directly against the source, so verification needs no renderer and no extra runtime" | Appendix F; §9.1 |

The JDK is explicitly **not vendored**: `README.md` line 18 makes a JDK the sole prerequisite, and Section 1.3.2.4 records "Running without a JDK on the host" as an unsupported use case. `JAVA_HOME` is not part of this dependency surface — Appendix E records it as "Not used by anything in this project; the `PATH` binaries are sufficient."
