### 3.3.5 Supply-Chain Security Implications

The empty dependency set removes the dominant class of supply-chain risk outright. `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §6 states the baseline: the program "has no dependency manifest, so there is no injection surface, no supply-chain exposure, no authentication or authorisation surface and no data-at-rest concern."

| Control that a dependency-bearing project would need | Status here | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dependency pinning / lockfile | **Not applicable** | Nothing is resolved; nothing to pin |
| Vulnerability scanning (SCA) of third-party components | **Not applicable to application dependencies** | No third-party component is present. Runtime CVE exposure is entirely a property of the host's JDK build, which the repository neither pins nor distributes |
| Software Bill of Materials | **Absent, and not required by any declared component** | The complete component list is the five tracked files plus the host JDK |
| Registry authentication / credential handling | **Not applicable** | No registry is contacted. `Project Guide.md` §1.5: "no credential, key, network egress, environment variable or secret is used by anything in this project" |
| Build-time network egress | **None** | "nothing is downloaded at build time" (§9.3) |
| Commit signing / provenance of the source itself | **Not enforced — the residual supply-chain control that is genuinely absent.** `git log --all --pretty='%G?'` shows **mixed** status: the 10 intermediate commits authored by `Blitzy Agent` are unsigned (`N`), while the three original `rjhonsi` commits and the `blitzy-qa[bot]` merge carry signatures that cannot be verified here for want of a public key (`E`). `Project Guide.md` §1.4 records commit-signing infrastructure as `Deferred` / Owner decision | `git log`; §1.4; Section 2.4.4 F-005 |
| Accidental commit of build output | **Controlled by documentation only.** With no `.gitignore`, an in-place `javac Hello.java` leaves an untracked `Hello.class`; the only control is `README.md` line 30's instruction "Do not commit the class file either way" plus the `mktemp -d` alternative. Recorded as `Open`, Low severity | `README.md` line 30; §6 |
| Compiler output destination | **Mitigated by design.** `mktemp -d` "returns a uniquely named one readable only by its owner, whereas a fixed, predictable destination can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it" | `README.md` line 30; §6 |

**Repository object store, for completeness.** `git count-objects -vH` reports 37 objects in a single 302.84 KiB pack with no loose or garbage objects — and no binary among the tracked blobs, so a clone conveys only text.


## 3.4 Third-Party Services

**Exactly one third-party service participates in this system: the Git hosting platform that holds the remote refs.** It serves the source-distribution channel and the Markdown rendering; it is not reached by the program at runtime. `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix B is categorical about everything else: "Not applicable. The program binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call; there is no service, database, broker or cache in this project."

### 3.4.1 Service Inventory

| Category | Present? | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git hosting platform | **Yes** | The only third-party service — see Section 3.4.2 |
| External APIs / outbound integrations | No | No network call is made by any tracked file; the only HTTPS URLs in the tracked tree are the licence-text references in `LICENSE` (`<https://fsf.org/>` at line 4 and `<https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>` at lines 648, 667 and 674) |
| Inbound API surface, ports, listeners | No | Appendix B: no port bound, no listener started |
| Authentication / identity providers | No | No credential, key, token or secrets file exists in any tracked file (verified by pattern search) |
| Monitoring, metrics, tracing, log aggregation | No | No logging framework and no diagnostic output; stderr is deliberately empty |
| Cloud services (compute, storage, messaging, IaC) | No | No cloud SDK, credential, endpoint, region or infrastructure descriptor exists anywhere in the tree |
| Message brokers, caches, queues | No | Appendix B |
| CI / build services | No | No CI descriptor of any kind; see Section 3.6 |
| Email, notification, payment, analytics services | No | No such reference exists in any tracked file |

### 3.4.2 The Git Hosting Platform — the Only Third-Party Service

| Attribute | Observed value | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform | **GitHub.** The clone's `origin` remote resolves to `github.com/rjhonsi/BlitzyRepo2_Java.git` for both fetch and push | `git remote -v` |
| Protocol | HTTPS | The `origin` URL scheme |
| Remote refs held | **Six**: `origin/HEAD` → `origin/main`, `origin/main`, `origin/jr_java1`, `origin/jr_java2`, `origin/jr_java3`, and `origin/blitzy-6d6c8680-f3ef-4055-9d11-0fc35e375843` | `git branch -a` |
| Pull-request workflow | `HEAD` is `2a78292` "Merge pull request #1", authored by `blitzy-qa[bot]` on 2026-09-22 — the platform's merge facility is part of the delivery path | `git log -1` |
| Branch state | `git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD` reports `0 11` — `main` is an ancestor of `jr_java1` and **11 commits behind** it, so the documentation delivery is not yet on the default branch | Direct verification |
| Markdown rendering | The platform determines the dialect — "GitHub Flavored Markdown over CommonMark … no generator or renderer is part of the project" — and `README.md`'s two relative links (`[Hello.java](Hello.java)` at line 71 and `[LICENSE](LICENSE)` at line 77) resolve through it | Appendix D; `README.md` |
| Access control | Whatever the platform enforces. The repository defines no roles, accounts or permissions of its own | Section 1.3.1.2 |
| Runtime coupling | **None.** The program never contacts the platform; the service participates only in distribution and presentation | Appendix B |

**Recorded dependencies on the platform.** `Project Guide.md` §1.6 carries two open items that are properties of this service rather than of the code: publishing the branch and merging it so the change reaches `main` (High, 0.5 hour), and reviewing the rendered guide on the hosting platform — emphasis, tables, fences and links — which has never been verified (Medium, 0.5 hour).

### 3.4.3 Authentication Services

**The application performs no authentication of any kind.** There is no credential handling, privilege check or identity concept in `Hello.java`; `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §1.5 records that "no credential, key, network egress, environment variable or secret is used by anything in this project," and Appendix E records that no environment variable and no secret is read by any tracked file. No identity provider, OAuth client, token, session or API-key construct exists.

Authentication exists **only around the distribution channel**, and only outside the tracked tree. Two findings are worth recording precisely because they are the system's entire credential surface:

| Finding | Detail | Security consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No secret is conveyed by a clone | A pattern search across all tracked files for token, key and credential forms (`ghs_`, `ghp_`, `x-access-token`, `AKIA`, PEM key headers, `secret`, `api_key`, `password`) matches **only documentation prose and the GPL text itself** — never an actual value | Cloning the repository transfers no credential material |
| The only credential observed is untracked and local | The clone reaches the remote over HTTPS using a **short-lived token-bearing remote URL held in the clone's own `.git/config`**. `git ls-files --error-unmatch .git/config` fails with "did not match any file(s) known to git", confirming the file is outside the tracked tree | The token is an artifact of the checkout environment, not of the repository. It is never committed and is not part of the system's distributable content |

The absence of an authentication surface is structural, not configured: because the program reads no input and dereferences no argument, there is no channel through which a principal could be asserted.

### 3.4.4 Monitoring and Observability Tools

**None is present, and none is referenced.** Section 1.3.2.1 records the exclusion, and direct inspection confirms the mechanism: there is no logging framework, no `logback.xml` or `log4j2.xml`, no metrics client, no tracing instrumentation and no APM agent configuration anywhere in the tree.

The program's entire observable surface is the operating-system process contract, and it is fully specified by three invariants at `README.md` line 63:

| Signal | Value | Consequence for observability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard output | `Hello from Java!` plus one platform line separator | The only telemetry the system emits — and it is a constant, so a wrapper compares rather than parses |
| Standard error | Empty by design | There is no diagnostic channel to collect; `Project Guide.md` §6 notes there is no error path that could disclose internal state through stderr |
| Exit status | `0`, by normal return from `main` with no `System.exit` | A caller can distinguish a real environment failure from normal operation with no interpretation |

`Project Guide.md` §9.7 records the observed form of this contract directly: `java Hello; echo "exit=$?"` prints the greeting followed by `exit=0`. No latency, throughput, availability or resource measurement exists anywhere in the repository, and Section 2.4.2 records the absence of performance requirements rather than substituting targets.

### 3.4.5 Cloud Services

**No cloud service is used, configured or referenced.** Verified by direct existence tests at the repository root: no `main.tf`, `variables.tf` or `terraform/` directory; no `serverless.yml`, `template.yaml` or `cloudformation.yaml`; no `k8s/`, `kubernetes/`, `helm/` or `Chart.yaml`. No cloud SDK appears in `Hello.java` — the file has zero `import` statements — and no region, endpoint, account identifier or cloud credential appears in any tracked file. A full-history check (`git log --all --name-only`) confirms no such descriptor has ever been tracked in any of the 14 commits.

Section 1.3.2.4 records "Deploying it as a service" as an unsupported use case, because "No listener, no port, no packaging, and no deployment descriptor exist."

### 3.4.6 Integration Requirements and Residual Third-Party Risk

Because the service inventory is a single entry, the integration requirements are correspondingly small — and stating them precisely is more useful than a generalised integration model.

| Integration requirement | Where it is enforced |
| --- | --- |
| The remote must hold the branch refs and accept the merge that moves `main` forward | The hosting platform; recorded as an open High-priority item in `Project Guide.md` §1.6 |
| The platform's Markdown renderer must present the three Markdown documents correctly, including `README.md`'s two relative links, four fenced blocks and two tables | The hosting platform; rendered appearance never verified (§1.6) |
| A JDK must be present on the host at build and launch time | The operator's environment; not vendored and not pinned (`README.md` line 18) |
| The launching shell must connect standard output and observe the exit status | The operating-system process contract (`README.md` line 63) |

The residual third-party risk is therefore concentrated in exactly two places, neither of which the repository controls: **the hosting platform's own access control**, and **the unpinned JDK build the operator installs** (see Section 3.3.5). There is no outbound egress beyond the single constant line on standard output, no inbound surface, no secret to rotate and no vendor availability the program depends on at runtime.


## 3.5 Databases & Storage

**No database, cache or storage service is part of this system.** `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix B states it without qualification: "there is no service, database, broker or cache in this project," and §9.1 repeats it among the prerequisites — "no database, no broker and no bound port." The program keeps no state within a run and none between runs.

What *is* worth documenting is the storage the system genuinely relies on, which is not a data tier at all: the **Git object store** that holds the source durably, and the **filesystem destinations** the compiler writes to.

### 3.5.1 Database Inventory

| Tier | Present? | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary database | **None** | Appendix B; `Hello.java` has zero `import` statements, so no JDBC, JPA or driver type can be referenced |
| Secondary / replica / analytical store | **None** | Appendix B |
| Embedded or file-backed database | **None** | No `*.db`, `*.sqlite`, `*.mv.db` or equivalent exists; the worktree contains only the five tracked text files plus the untracked authoring artifact |
| Schema, migration or seed assets | **None** | No `*.sql` file exists anywhere in the worktree; no migration directory exists |
| Connection configuration | **Nowhere to put one.** No `application.properties`, `application.yml`, `config.yml`, `config.yaml`, `.env` or `.env.example` file exists, and Appendix E records that no environment variable is read by any tracked file | Direct existence tests |
| ORM / data-access layer | **None** | No manifest in which one could be declared (Section 3.2.1); no `import` in the source |

### 3.5.2 Data Persistence Strategy — Statelessness by Construction

The persistence strategy is the deliberate absence of persistence, and it is a static property of the source rather than a configuration choice.

| Property | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| No state within a run | `Hello.java` declares **no field**, creates **no instance**, and holds no static mutable state — the class Javadoc at lines 2–3 states "it has no field, creates no instance" |
| No state between runs | `README.md` line 12: the program "reads no input, opens no resource and keeps no state." Every run is therefore independent, and Section 2.4.3 records that there is no queue, pool, cache or connection to size |
| No read path | No `System.in`, `Scanner`, file read or resource load exists; `args` is never dereferenced |
| No write path other than stdout | The line comment at `Hello.java` line 16 fixes this as a design property: "Sole output: one write to standard output … no other sink is written" |
| Nothing to leak on exit | Because no resource is opened, Section 2.4.4 records that nothing can leak on termination |

### 3.5.3 Caching Solutions

**None.** No cache library, cache configuration or in-process cache construct exists — there is no manifest in which a cache dependency could be declared, no field in which a cached value could be held, and no second invocation within a process to serve from a cache. Appendix B lists the cache among the components that do not exist.

The one caching-adjacent statement the repository does make is about *build* caching, and it is a statement of absence: Section 2.4.3 records that "there is no incremental-build or caching concern because there is no second compilation unit."

### 3.5.4 Storage Services Actually Used

Three storage surfaces exist. None is a managed service; each is a property of the host or of Git.

| Surface | What it stores | Durability and scope | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Git object store** — the system's only durable store | The five tracked files as content-addressed blobs | **37 objects in a single 302.84 KiB pack**, no loose objects and no garbage. No binary blob is present, so a clone conveys only text. Replicated to the hosting remote across six refs | `git count-objects -vH`; `git ls-files` |
| **Working-tree checkout** | The five tracked files plus one untracked artifact (`tech_spec.md`, the specification-authoring file, which is not part of the system) | Local and ephemeral | `ls -la`; `git ls-files` |
| **Compiler output destination** | `Hello.class`, the transient build artifact | Either beside the source (in-place compile) or in a per-run `mktemp -d` directory outside the checkout. **Never committed** — zero `*.class` blobs are tracked and none has ever been tracked in the 14-commit history | `README.md` line 30; full-history check |

**The compiler output destination is the one storage decision with a security rationale**, and the repository states it explicitly. `README.md` line 30 recommends `B="$(mktemp -d)" && javac -d "$B" Hello.java` followed by `java -cp "$B" Hello`, because `mktemp -d` "returns a uniquely named one readable only by its owner, whereas a fixed, predictable destination can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it." `Project Guide.md` §6 records this as `Mitigated`, and §6 identifies the reintroduction of a predictable output path in a future edit as the concrete residual risk.

**The absence of an ignore rule is the corresponding hygiene gap.** There is no `.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude` holds no active pattern, and `git check-ignore -v Hello.class` matches no rule at all — so an in-place compile leaves an untracked class file with nothing to stop it being committed by accident. The only control is documentation: `README.md` line 30's "Do not commit the class file either way," reinforced by `Project Guide.md` §9.4's `rm -f Hello.class && git status --short`. Section 2.4.4 records this as `Open`, Low severity.

### 3.5.5 Data Domains and Measured Volumes

| Data element | Form | Volume | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The greeting payload | Compile-time `String` constant `"Hello from Java!"` — the **only** data element in the system | 16 ASCII characters; **17 bytes** of standard output where the separator is LF, **18 bytes** where it is CRLF | `Hello.java` line 17; `README.md` line 63 |
| The line separator | Derived at runtime from the host, appended by `println` | 1–2 bytes | `README.md` line 63 |
| Tracked repository content | Five text files | **925,008 bytes total** — of which **884,733 bytes (95.6%)** are the two Markdown documents under `blitzy/documentation/` and only **1,073 bytes** are source | Direct measurement |

There is no schema, record, file format, serialisation or data-at-rest representation. Section 1.3.1.2 records the same: one data element and one derived value, with no data at rest or in transit. Section 2.4.3 identifies the one dimension that actually grows — "Clone size therefore grows with each documentation generation round, not with the program."

### 3.5.6 Storage-Related Security and Operational Implications

| Concern | Position | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data-at-rest encryption, masking, tokenisation | **Not applicable.** `Project Guide.md` §6 records that the program has "no data-at-rest concern"; there is no stored record to protect and no key material anywhere in the tree | §6 |
| Backup, retention, recovery objectives | **None recorded, and none asserted here.** The durable store is the Git object store replicated to the remote; no backup policy, retention rule or recovery target exists in any tracked file | Direct inspection |
| Migration and versioning of data | **Not applicable.** No schema exists to migrate. Section 2.6.3 records that even *requirement* versions must be anchored to commit SHAs, because zero tags exist | Section 2.6.3 |
| Connection pooling, transaction management, consistency | **Not applicable.** No connection, transaction or consistency construct exists | Appendix B |
| Sensitive content entering the immutable store | **Unguarded.** Git objects are content-addressed and effectively immutable once pushed, and with no `.gitignore`, no active `.git/info/exclude` pattern and no secret-scanning or pre-commit configuration, nothing in the repository would prevent a future commit from persisting unintended content. Today the store is clean: a pattern search across all tracked files finds no credential, key or token value | `git check-ignore`; tracked-file pattern search |
| Stored byte format | **Unmanaged and load-bearing.** `Hello.java` is CRLF on all 20 lines while the other tracked text files are LF-only, with no `.gitattributes` and `core.autocrlf`/`core.eol` unset — so the stored form is part of what is distributed, and normalising it would rewrite every line and change the file's content digest | `od`; `git check-attr`; `Project Guide.md` §5.2 |


## 3.6 Development & Deployment

The development and deployment surface is the JDK toolchain plus Git, invoked by hand. There is **no build system, no containerisation, no CI/CD and no deployment mechanism** — each verified by direct existence tests rather than inferred — and `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix F states the position for tooling generally: "No linter, formatter, documentation generator, build tool or test framework is configured in the repository, and none is introduced by this change."

### 3.6.1 Development Tools

`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix F enumerates the developer tools and the role each plays; the table below reproduces those roles with the versions recorded in Appendix D.

| Tool | Version recorded | Role in this project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `javac` | OpenJDK **25.0.3** | Compiles the single source file. `-Xlint:all -Werror` "is the project's static-analysis surface, as no linter is configured" |
| `java` | OpenJDK **25.0.3** | Launches the compiled class, or the source file directly in single-file source mode |
| `javadoc` | OpenJDK **25.0.3** | Measures comment coverage; `-Xdoclint:all` validates doc-comment syntax and tag usage. "Its HTML output is never committed" |
| `git` | **2.51.0** recorded; **2.43.0** observed in this specification's environment | Clone, branch, merge, and supplies "the pre-comment revision used as the baseline for behaviour and comment-census comparisons" |
| GNU `grep`, `awk`, `diff`, `tr`, `od`, `cmp`, `iconv` | Not pinned | "Assert the guide's structure and both files' stored byte format directly against the source, so verification needs no renderer and no extra runtime" |
| `mktemp -d` | Not pinned | "Generates the per-run build and scratch directories, keeping class output out of the checkout" |

**Environment setup is empty by design.** `Project Guide.md` §9.2 opens with "Nothing to configure. No environment variable or secret is read by any tracked file," and records that `JAVA_HOME` "is not required, because the compiler and launcher are on `PATH`" — offering a derive-it-from-`PATH` snippet only for the case where an operator's own tool demands the variable.

**No editor or IDE configuration is present.** Existence tests confirm the absence of `.editorconfig`, `.vscode/`, `.idea/` and `.devcontainer/`. This matters for one specific reason rather than as a style observation: `Hello.java` is stored CRLF on all 20 lines with no `.gitattributes` and with `core.autocrlf`/`core.eol` unset, so line-ending preservation depends entirely on editor discipline. `Project Guide.md` §6 carries this as a Medium-severity technical risk, "Open — accepted by design."

### 3.6.2 Build System

**There is no build system.** The compiler is invoked directly, and the "build" is a single `javac` call with nothing to resolve. `Project Guide.md` §9.3 is the authoritative statement: "None. There is no `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `Makefile`, `package.json` or lock file of any kind, and nothing is downloaded at build time."

| Descriptor category | Existence test result |
| --- | --- |
| Maven | `pom.xml`, `mvnw`, `.mvn/` — **all absent** |
| Gradle | `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle`, `settings.gradle.kts`, `gradlew`, `gradlew.bat`, `gradle/` — **all absent** |
| Ant / Ivy / Make / CMake | `build.xml`, `ivy.xml`, `Makefile`, `makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt` — **all absent** |
| Java module system | `module-info.java` — **absent**; no `--release` or `--source` setting anywhere (Appendix D) |
| Toolchain version files | `.java-version`, `.sdkmanrc`, `.tool-versions` — **all absent** |

A full-history check (`git log --all --name-only` across all 14 commits and every branch) confirms that no such descriptor has **ever** been tracked.

#### 3.6.2.1 The Two Documented Build Paths

```bash
javac Hello.java                              # Path A — in place
B="$(mktemp -d)"; javac -Xlint:all -d "$B" Hello.java   # Path B — recommended
```

| Path | Command | Outcome | Why it exists |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A — in place** | `javac Hello.java` | Exit 0, no diagnostics, `Hello.class` beside the source | Shortest form. Leaves an untracked artifact because there is no `.gitignore` |
| **B — out of tree (recommended)** | `B="$(mktemp -d)" && javac -d "$B" Hello.java`, then `java -cp "$B" Hello` | Exit 0, no diagnostics, working tree unchanged | Keeps the checkout clean and avoids a predictable, pre-creatable or symlink-redirectable output path (`README.md` line 30) |

`Project Guide.md` §9.4 records the expected result for both as "exit status 0 and no output at all," adds that "`-Xlint:all` is clean, and so is `-Werror`," and supplies the Path A cleanup `rm -f Hello.class && git status --short`.

**Build characteristics.** One compilation unit, zero dependency resolution, zero network egress, no packaging step and no artifact to publish. Section 2.4.3 notes that adding a second compilation unit "would immediately create the build-ordering and manifest concerns the project currently has none of."

### 3.6.3 Quality Gates, Static Analysis and Testing

| Gate | Command | Recorded result | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compiler diagnostics | `javac Hello.java` | Exit 0, no diagnostics | Passing (`Project Guide.md` §3) |
| Strictest static check | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror -d "$B" Hello.java` | Exit 0, empty error stream — **the project's entire static-analysis surface**, "as no linter is configured" | Passing (Appendix A, Appendix F) |
| Comment coverage and doc-comment syntax | `javadoc -d "$B/jd" -quiet Hello.java`; `javadoc -Xdoclint:all` | Exit 0 with **exactly one** warning — `Hello.java:6: warning: use of default constructor, which does not provide a comment` — accepted by design; coverage 2 of 3 documentable members | Passing with one accepted warning (Appendix A, §9.6) |
| Acceptance and toolchain checks | Run from a scratch directory outside the checkout | **49 of 49 passed** — 37 assertions plus 12 toolchain checks | Passing (§3) |
| Automated unit / integration tests | — | **No committed test suite.** §3 records that "The repository carries no committed test suite, and adding one is outside this change's scope" | Absent by declared scope |

**No linter, formatter or code-quality tool is configured.** Existence tests confirm the absence of `checkstyle.xml`, `spotbugs.xml`, `pmd.xml` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. The compiler's own `-Xlint:all -Werror` is the substitute, which is why `Project Guide.md` §1.6's maintenance guidance is to re-run it after any source edit.

**The structural gap.** Nothing re-runs any of these gates. `Project Guide.md` §1.4 states it plainly — "Nothing re-runs the documentation checks on future changes" — and §9.6 explains why the tooling is not committed: "build, test and CI files are out of scope for this repository," so checks run from a scratch directory and their only durable record is `Project Guide.md` §3 and §4. Section 2.6.2 K-3 carries the same constraint, and adopting an automated gate is recorded as `Deferred` / Owner decision.

### 3.6.4 Containerization

**Not used.** Direct existence tests at the repository root return absent for `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dev`, `.dockerignore`, `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml` and `compose.yml`, and no such file has ever been tracked in the history. No orchestration or infrastructure-as-code descriptor exists either — no `k8s/`, `kubernetes/`, `helm/`, `Chart.yaml`, `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `terraform/`, `serverless.yml`, `template.yaml` or `cloudformation.yaml`.

`Project Guide.md` §9.1 lists the container among the prerequisites that do not apply: "No package manager step, no virtual environment, no container, no database, no broker and no bound port."

### 3.6.5 CI/CD

**No continuous-integration or delivery pipeline exists.** Existence tests return absent for `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.travis.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` and `.drone.yml`; the full-history check confirms none has ever been tracked. `README.md` line 18 records the same absence from the version-pinning angle — the repository carries no "CI descriptor … in which a version could be recorded."

| Consequence of having no pipeline | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| The 49 recorded checks were run manually and are not repeatable automatically | `Project Guide.md` §1.4, §3 |
| Verification tooling must **not** be committed, by declared scope | §9.6; Section 2.4.1 F-009 |
| The documentation checks will not re-run on future changes | §1.4 |
| Adopting an automated gate is an open Owner decision, not a planned task | §1.4 |
| Any change to `Hello.java` requires a manual `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` re-run | Section 2.4.5 F-004 |

The only automation-adjacent facility in use is the hosting platform's pull-request merge, visible as `HEAD` = `2a78292` "Merge pull request #1" — a human/bot workflow step, not a pipeline.

### 3.6.6 Deployment, Packaging and Distribution

**There is no deployment.** The program is consumed as source from a clone and built locally; nothing is packaged, published or installed.

| Dimension | Position | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Packaging | **None.** No jar, war or archive is produced or committed; zero binary blobs are tracked | Recursive archive search; `git ls-files` |
| Published artifact / coordinates | **None declared anywhere**, so the program is never consumed as a dependency | Section 2.1 F-005; Section 3.3.2 |
| Release line | **None.** `git tag` returns **zero tags across 14 commits**; requirement versions are anchored to commit SHAs instead | `git tag`; Section 2.6.3 |
| Distribution channel | **Git clone over HTTPS from the hosting remote**, carrying five text files totalling 925,008 bytes | `git remote -v`; `git ls-files` |
| Deployment descriptor | **None**, and Section 1.3.2.4 records "Deploying it as a service" as unsupported | Section 1.3.2.4 |
| Runtime environments | Any host with a JDK on `PATH` and a POSIX shell. No environment-specific configuration exists to differentiate dev, test and production | Appendix E; §9.2 |

#### 3.6.6.1 The Three Documented Launch Forms

| Form | Command | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| From the out-of-tree build directory | `java -cp "$B" Hello` | Pairs with build Path B |
| From the repository root after an in-place compile | `java Hello` | Pairs with build Path A; the bare class name works because the class is in the default package |
| Direct source launch | `java Hello.java` | **Requires JDK 11 or later**; leaves no class file behind |

`README.md` line 46 records that "Both paths produce byte-identical standard output," and `Project Guide.md` §9.5 records all three forms as exercised. The launch outcome is invariant: `Hello from Java!` plus one platform line separator on stdout, empty stderr, exit status 0.

#### 3.6.6.2 Outstanding Delivery State

The delivery is **not yet reachable on the default branch**. `git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD` reports `0 11`: `main` is an ancestor of `jr_java1` and 11 commits behind it, so every documentation artifact added since `0726b1d` is absent from `main`. `Project Guide.md` §1.6 records "Publish the branch and merge the change" as a **High**-priority 0.5-hour item, and Section 2.6.4 notes that pushing and merging closes requirement F-005-RQ-005.


## 3.7 Stack Integration, Compatibility and Constraints

The components documented above integrate through four interfaces and nothing else: the JDK toolchain, the operating-system process contract, Git with its hosting platform, and the GPL v3 obligations attached to the covered work (Section 1.2.1.3). This sub-section states those integration contracts precisely, records the compatibility position, and assesses the default technology stack against what the repository actually contains.

### 3.7.1 Component Integration Map

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Dev["Maintainer / Operator<br/>POSIX shell at repository root"]

    subgraph SCM["Version Control and Hosting"]
        GitCLI["git 2.51.0 recorded<br/>clone, branch, merge, baseline diff"]
        Remote["GitHub origin remote over HTTPS<br/>6 refs, main 11 commits behind"]
        Render["GitHub Flavored Markdown renderer<br/>presentation only"]
    end

    subgraph Repo["Repository, 5 tracked files, 925,008 bytes"]
        Src["Hello.java<br/>Java, default package<br/>20 CRLF lines, 1,073 bytes"]
        Readme["README.md<br/>77 LF lines, operator guide"]
        Lic["LICENSE<br/>GPL v3 verbatim"]
        Docs["blitzy/documentation/<br/>884,733 bytes of Markdown"]
    end

    subgraph Toolchain["JDK Toolchain, OpenJDK 25.0.3, host supplied, never vendored"]
        Javac["javac<br/>compile plus -Xlint:all -Werror gate"]
        Java["java<br/>class launch or JEP 330 source launch"]
        Javadoc["javadoc<br/>-Xdoclint:all coverage check"]
    end

    subgraph Lib["Only code dependency"]
        Lang["java.lang, implicitly imported<br/>String and System.out"]
    end

    subgraph Proc["Operating system process contract"]
        Stdout["stdout: Hello from Java! plus separator"]
        Stderr["stderr: empty"]
        Exit["exit status 0 by normal return"]
    end

    Dev --> GitCLI
    GitCLI -->|"fetch and push"| Remote
    Remote -.-> Render
    GitCLI --> Src
    GitCLI --> Docs
    Readme -.->|"instructs"| Dev
    Docs -.->|"records toolchain versions"| Javac
    Lic -.->|"governs redistribution"| Src
    Dev --> Javac
    Dev --> Java
    Src --> Javac
    Javac -->|"Hello.class into a mktemp -d directory"| Java
    Src -.->|"JDK 11 plus, leaves no class file"| Java
    Src --> Javadoc
    Lang --> Java
    Java --> Stdout
    Java --> Stderr
    Java --> Exit
```

### 3.7.2 Integration Requirements Between Components

| Interface | Requirement on each side | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`Hello.java` → `javac`** | The file name must match the public class; the unit must compile with no `--release` or `--source` setting and no dependency to resolve. `javac` must accept JDK 1.0-era constructs | Exit 0 with no diagnostics, including under `-Xlint:all -Werror` (`Project Guide.md` §3, §9.4) |
| **`javac` → `java`** | The class output directory must be on the classpath at launch: `java -cp "$B" Hello` for Path B, or the repository root for Path A | `Project Guide.md` Appendix A records both forms as exercised |
| **`Hello.java` → `java` (direct)** | The launcher must implement source-file mode, and the first top-level class must declare the standard `main` signature — satisfied at lines 6 and 15 | (cite index="1-30,1-31">JEP 330 requires the first top-level class in the file to declare `public static void main(String[])`</cite>; `README.md` line 40 |
| **`java` → `java.lang`** | The JVM must supply an initialised `System.out`. No other package is required, and no module path is configured | `Hello.java` line 17; zero `import` statements |
| **`java` → operating system** | The launching shell must connect standard output and observe the exit status. Standard error must remain empty; termination is by normal return, never `System.exit` | `README.md` line 63; `Project Guide.md` §9.7 records `exit=0` |
| **`Hello.java` → `javadoc`** | Doc comments must follow the placement conventions in `Project Guide.md` §5.1 row 2; exactly one warning is expected and a second is to be treated as a regression | `Project Guide.md` §9.6 |
| **Working tree → `git`** | Build output must be kept out of the tree by command discipline, since no `.gitignore` exists; `Hello.java`'s CRLF bytes must survive edits, since no `.gitattributes` exists | `git status --short` expected to print nothing (§9.2, §9.4) |
| **`git` → hosting platform** | The remote must hold the branch refs and accept the merge that advances `main`; the platform's renderer presents the Markdown and resolves `README.md`'s two relative links | `git remote -v`; `git branch -a`; Appendix D |
| **`README.md` → `Hello.java`** | The fenced expected-output block at lines 59–61 is the published oracle and must match the literal at line 17; citations are by stable symbol, not line number, because comments shift lines | `Project Guide.md` §4, Appendix G |
| **`LICENSE` → the covered work** | `LICENSE` must remain verbatim, and a modified covered work must carry a dated modification notice — present at `README.md` line 5 | `Project Guide.md` §1.3, §5.1 row 8 |

### 3.7.3 Version Compatibility and Pinning Position

The repository's deliberate position is **portability over reproducibility**: versions are *recorded*, never *enforced*.

| Dimension | Position | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Java version pin | **None.** `README.md` line 18: the repository "pins no Java version" and carries no `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `.java-version`, `.sdkmanrc`, CI descriptor or `module-info.java` "in which a version could be recorded" | `README.md` line 18 |
| Java language level | **"None declared."** No `--release` or `--source` setting exists anywhere | Appendix D |
| Toolchain version used | OpenJDK **25.0.3** for `java`, `javac` and `javadoc`; `git` **2.51.0** | Appendix D, §9.1 |
| Verified compatibility range | Compile-then-run exercised at release targets **11, 17 and 21**; single-file source launch documented as **JDK 11+** but **not confirmed on a JDK 11 runtime** | §9.1; §1.6 open item |
| External context | (cite index="12-3">Java SE 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25 are the LTS releases</cite>; (cite index="11-7">Java 25 LTS was released on 16 September 2025</cite>. The recorded toolchain is therefore an update of the current LTS line, and the three exercised targets are all LTS releases | [web] Oracle Java SE Support Roadmap; Java version history |
| Reproducibility consequence | A build is reproducible in *behaviour* but not in *toolchain*: two operators on different JDKs both get `Hello from Java!` and exit 0, but nothing records or constrains which JDK either used | Synthesis of the rows above |

**Security implication of not pinning.** Because the JDK is host-supplied and unpinned, runtime CVE exposure is entirely a property of the operator's chosen JDK build and is neither recorded nor constrained by the repository. This is the residual technology risk identified in Section 3.4.6, and it is the trade the project accepts in exchange for compiling on any JDK. (cite index="14-1">Java 25 is the current LTS with Java 21 and Java 17 still supported across distributions</cite>, so an operator following the documented workflow on a current LTS remains on a patched line — but nothing in the repository enforces that.

### 3.7.4 Default Technology Stack — Applicability Assessment

A default technology stack is available as a fallback for greenfield work. **None of its elements is present in this repository**, and adopting any of them would contradict the stated constraint that a JDK alone builds and runs the program (`Hello.java` lines 2–4; constraint F-004). Each row below records the verification actually performed, so that the absence is evidenced rather than assumed.

| Default element | Present? | Verification performed | Why it does not apply |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AWS (cloud platform) | No | No cloud SDK import, credential, region or endpoint in any tracked file; no IaC descriptor | Nothing is deployed; the program binds no port and makes no network call (Appendix B) |
| Docker (containerisation) | No | `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dev`, `.dockerignore`, `docker-compose.yml`/`.yaml`, `compose.yml` — all absent, and never tracked in 14 commits | §9.1 records "no container" among the non-prerequisites |
| Terraform (IaC) | No | `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `terraform/` — all absent | There is no infrastructure to describe |
| GitHub Actions (CI/CD) | No | `.github/` absent. The hosting platform *is* GitHub, but no workflow exists | Build, test and CI files are out of scope by declaration (§9.6); "Nothing re-runs the documentation checks" (§1.4) |
| Python (language) / Flask (framework) | No | Worktree search across 20 source extensions returns only `./Hello.java`; no `requirements.txt`, `Pipfile`, `pyproject.toml` or `setup.py` | Java is the implementation language; there is no HTTP surface for a web framework to serve |
| Auth0 (authentication) | No | No credential, token, key or secrets file in any tracked file; Appendix E records no environment variable is read | The program reads no input, so no principal can be asserted (Section 3.4.3) |
| MongoDB (database) | No | Appendix B: "there is no service, database, broker or cache in this project"; no connection configuration file exists anywhere | The program keeps no state within or between runs (Section 3.5.2) |
| Langchain (AI framework) | No | Zero `import` statements; no dependency manifest in which it could be declared | No model, prompt or inference path exists |
| React / React-Native / TypeScript / TailwindCSS | No | No `package.json`, lockfile or `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.jsx`/`.css` file anywhere in the worktree | Console output only; Section 1.3.2.1 records "no UI, hosted page, or port" |
| Swift / Kotlin / Objective-C / ElectronJS (native and desktop) | No | Worktree search for `.swift`, `.kt`, `.m`, `.mm` and `.js` returns nothing | There is no client application; the deliverable is one JVM process that writes one line |

### 3.7.5 Constraints Governing Future Stack Changes

Stack changes are not merely discouraged here; each one invalidates specific recorded requirements. The rules below are the technology-relevant subset of Section 2.6.4's change-impact rules, restated so that a reviewer can tell from a diff alone what must be re-verified.

| Proposed stack change | What it invalidates | Deeper consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add a build manifest, wrapper, test suite or CI descriptor | F-004-RQ-001, F-005-RQ-001, and the §1.4 "no automated gate" item | Forfeits the JDK-only property that constraint F-004 protects and changes the tracked-file census |
| Add a first third-party import or a second compilation unit | F-004-RQ-001, F-004-RQ-002, F-005-RQ-001 | Introduces dependency resolution, a supply-chain surface, and the build-ordering concerns Section 2.4.3 notes the project currently has none of |
| Add a `package` declaration or a `module-info.java` | F-001-RQ-002, F-001-RQ-004, F-004-RQ-002, F-004-RQ-004 | The bare-name launch `java Hello` stops working, invalidating every documented command |
| Introduce a `--release` or `--source` setting | Constraint F-004; Appendix D's "None declared" language level | Converts an any-JDK source file into a version-targeted build |
| Commit compiled output or a packaged artifact | F-005-RQ-002 | Ends the source-only distribution property; the tracked tree would carry its first binary |
| Adopt tags or releases | F-005-RQ-003 and the SHA-anchoring rule in Section 2.6.3 | Requirement versioning would move from commit SHAs to tags |
| Add `.gitattributes`, or normalise `Hello.java` to LF | F-005-RQ-004, F-008-RQ-005 | Rewrites all 20 lines and changes the file's content digest (`Project Guide.md` §5.2) |
| Add `.gitignore` | Closes the Low-severity hygiene item in §6; an Owner decision in §1.4 | Removes the reliance on documentation alone to keep `Hello.class` uncommitted |
| Reintroduce a fixed compiler-output path in place of `mktemp -d` | The mitigation recorded against F-004 in §6 | Restores the predictable-path exposure `README.md` line 30 explains |

- [web] Wikipedia, *Java version history* — confirmed the Java 25 LTS release date of 16 September 2025.
- [web] *Java Version and LTS Timeline* (hidekazu-konishi.com) — confirmed the two-year LTS cadence adopted from September 2021.
- [web] HeroDevs, *Java 8, 11, 17 EOL Dates by OpenJDK Vendor* — confirmed that Java 25 is the current LTS with Java 21 and Java 17 still supported across distributions, supporting the unpinned-JDK risk note in Section 3.7.3.


# 4. Process Flowchart

## 4.1 System Workflows

The system documented here is a single-statement console program. `Hello.java` contains exactly five executable lines — the class declaration at line 6, the entry-point signature at line 15, one `System.out.println("Hello from Java!")` at line 17, and the two closing braces at lines 19 and 20 — and a fixed-string census of the file returns **zero** occurrences of `if (`, `for (`, `while (`, `switch (`, `try {`, `catch`, `throw`, `new ` and `System.exit(`, with exactly one `println(`. There is therefore precisely one path through the running program, containing no decision point and no error branch. Section 2.3.1 records the same property of the feature chain: `F-004 → F-001 → F-002 → F-003` is "strictly linear and has no branch."

Every decision diamond, error state and recovery path in this section consequently belongs to the **operator and toolchain workflow that surrounds the program**, not to the program itself. Those workflows are real, documented and verified: `README.md` publishes them as executable literals, and `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §9 records each command as having been executed on a Linux host with OpenJDK 25.0.3.

### 4.1.1 Workflow Inventory, Actors and Conventions

**Workflow identifiers.** Section 1.3.1.1 already enumerates the four primary operator workflows as `W-1` … `W-4`, and Section 2.3.5 states that these "are the only processes in which features interact" and delegates their detailed decomposition to this section. This section preserves those identifiers unchanged and additionally names the three maintenance procedures that `Project Guide.md` documents but Section 1.3.1.1 does not enumerate; those three are introduced here as `M-1` … `M-3`.

| ID | Workflow | Trigger | Terminal state | Primary evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W-1 | Compile in place, then run | Operator at the repository root | Greeting on stdout, exit status 0, untracked `Hello.class` present or removed | `README.md` lines 27, 37 |
| W-2 | Compile to a fresh directory outside the checkout, then run | Operator who must keep the working tree clean | Greeting on stdout, exit status 0, working tree unchanged | `README.md` line 30 |
| W-3 | Launch the source file directly | Operator on JDK 11 or later wanting no artifact | Greeting on stdout, exit status 0, no class file created | `README.md` lines 40–44 |
| W-4 | Verify the output contract | Any of W-1 … W-3 has produced output | Observed stdout, stderr and exit status compared against the published oracle | `README.md` lines 57–63 |
| M-1 | Comment-only source edit with behaviour-parity verification | Maintainer edits `Hello.java` | Additions-only diff proven against the pre-comment revision, byte-identical runtime behaviour | `Project Guide.md` §9.6 |
| M-2 | Quality-gate run | Any source or guide change | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` clean, exactly one accepted `javadoc` warning, acceptance suite passing | `Project Guide.md` §3, §9.6 |
| M-3 | Publish and merge the delivery | Maintainer with an unpublished branch | `main` no longer behind the working branch | `Project Guide.md` §1.6 |

**Actors and systems.** The repository defines no roles, accounts or permissions of its own — Section 1.3.1.2 records that "user group" here means audience, not an access-control construct. The participants in every flow below are therefore either humans or external facilities.

| Actor or system | Role in the workflows | Inside the system boundary? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operator / learner | Types the documented commands; reads and compares the output | No — a human touchpoint |
| Maintainer | Edits `Hello.java`, runs the gates, publishes the branch | No — a human touchpoint |
| Repository owner | Holds the deferred decisions recorded in `Project Guide.md` §1.4 | No — a human touchpoint |
| POSIX shell | Invokes the toolchain, supplies `mktemp -d`, observes exit status | No — host environment |
| JDK toolchain (`javac`, `java`, `javadoc`) | Compiles, launches and measures comment coverage | No — required but not vendored (Section 1.3.1.2) |
| JVM process from `Hello.java` | Performs the one statement of work | **Yes** — this *is* the executable system |
| OS process contract | Carries stdout, stderr and the exit status | No — the consuming contract |
| Filesystem | Holds the source, and any `Hello.class` or scratch directory | No — `Hello.class` is explicitly outside the boundary |
| `git` and the hosting platform | Clone, branch, pull-request merge, baseline retrieval | No |

**Diagram conventions used throughout Section 4.** Subgraphs act as swim lanes, one per actor or system. Stadium nodes mark start and end points, diamonds mark decision points, and plain rectangles mark process steps. Where a step verifies a contract, the governing requirement identifier from Section 2.2 is written into the node label so each flow step is traceable to its acceptance criterion.

### 4.1.2 Core Business Processes

There is no business process in the commercial sense anywhere in this repository. There is no customer, order, transaction, approval, ledger or workflow engine: Section 1.3.2.1 records that persistence and data services, network services, user interfaces, authentication, configuration management and logging are all absent, each confirmed by direct existence test. The "core business processes" of this system are the developer and operator processes through which the artifact is built, launched, verified and maintained.

#### 4.1.2.1 High-Level System Workflow

The following diagram is the single end-to-end view of the system: an operator obtains the source through Git, reads the guide, drives the JDK toolchain, and observes the process contract. The `System boundary` lane contains the only steps that execute repository code.

```mermaid

    end

    end

    OP1 --> G1
    G1 --> G2
    G2 --> OP2
    OP2 --> OP3
    OP3 -->|"W-1 or W-2"| T1
    OP3 -->|"W-3 single-file launch"| T2
```
