#### 4.1.2.2 W-1 — Compile in Place, Then Run

`W-1` is the shortest documented path and the only one that leaves an artifact inside the checkout. Because the repository carries no `.gitignore`, that artifact appears as untracked content, which is why the flow ends in a hygiene decision rather than simply at the greeting.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W1S(["Start: POSIX shell at the repository root"]) --> W1A{"javac and java<br/>on PATH?"}
    W1A -->|"No"| W1AE["Prerequisite unmet: a JDK is the<br/>sole requirement and is not vendored<br/>Section 1.3.2.4"]
    W1AE --> W1S
    W1A -->|"Yes"| W1B["Run javac Hello.java<br/>one compilation unit, nothing downloaded<br/>F-004-RQ-003"]
    W1B --> W1C{"Exit status 0 and<br/>no diagnostics?"}
    W1C -->|"No: file name does not<br/>match the public class"| W1CE["error: class Hello is public,<br/>should be declared in a file<br/>named Hello.java"]
    W1CE --> W1CR["Recovery: restore the unit as<br/>Hello.java, then recompile<br/>Project Guide 9.8 row 2"]
    W1CR --> W1B
    W1C -->|"Yes"| W1D["Hello.class written beside the source<br/>untracked and unignored<br/>F-005-RQ-002"]
    W1D --> W1E["Run java Hello<br/>bare name, default package<br/>F-001-RQ-002"]
    W1E --> W1F{"Main class<br/>resolved?"}
    W1F -->|"No"| W1FE["Could not find or load<br/>main class Hello"]
    W1FE --> W1FR["Recovery: compile first, or launch<br/>with java -cp build-dir Hello<br/>Project Guide 9.8 row 1"]
    W1FR --> W1E
    W1F -->|"Yes"| W1G["stdout receives the greeting,<br/>stderr stays empty, status 0"]
    W1G --> W1H["Hand off to W-4<br/>output-contract verification"]
    W1H --> W1I{"Must the working<br/>tree stay clean?"}
    W1I -->|"Yes"| W1J["rm -f Hello.class,<br/>then git status --short<br/>expect no output"]
    W1I -->|"No"| W1K["Leave the artifact in place,<br/>but never commit it"]
    W1J --> W1Z(["End: greeting emitted, tree clean"])
    W1K --> W1Z
```

#### 4.1.2.3 W-2 — Compile Outside the Checkout, Then Run

`W-2` is the path `README.md` line 30 recommends. Its distinguishing step is the generation of the output directory: the guide requires a freshly generated, owner-readable-only directory because "a fixed, predictable destination can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it." Section 2.2.5 records the reintroduction of a predictable path as a Security-category concern, currently `Mitigated`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W2S(["Start: working tree must remain clean"]) --> W2A["Generate the build destination<br/>with mktemp -d, assigned to B<br/>unique, owner-readable only"]
    W2A --> W2B{"Directory created<br/>and quoted in use?"}
    W2B -->|"No"| W2BE["Do not substitute a fixed path:<br/>a predictable destination is<br/>pre-creatable and symlink-redirectable"]
    W2BE --> W2A
    W2B -->|"Yes"| W2C["Run javac -Xlint:all -d B Hello.java<br/>F-004-RQ-006, F-004-RQ-005"]
    W2C --> W2D{"Exit 0 with an<br/>empty error stream?"}
    W2D -->|"No"| W2DE["Diagnostic raised. No instance is<br/>recorded at HEAD: -Xlint:all and<br/>-Werror are both clean"]
    W2DE --> W2Z2(["End: escalate, owner decision"])
    W2D -->|"Yes"| W2E["Hello.class written into B<br/>checkout untouched"]
    W2E --> W2F["Run java -cp B Hello<br/>F-001-RQ-002"]
    W2F --> W2G["stdout receives the greeting,<br/>stderr empty, status 0"]
    W2G --> W2H["Hand off to W-4"]
    W2H --> W2I["git status --short<br/>expect no output"]
    W2I --> W2J["rm -rf B to discard<br/>the per-run directory"]
    W2J --> W2Z(["End: greeting emitted,<br/>zero footprint in the checkout"])
```

#### 4.1.2.4 W-3 — Single-File Source Launch

`W-3` compiles nothing durably and leaves no artifact. It is the only workflow in the system with a stated version floor, and that floor is also the only **open** verification item among the launch paths: `Project Guide.md` §4 marks the claim "⚠ Partial" because the JDK 11 floor "has not been run on a JDK 11 runtime; only JDK 25 was available."

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W3S(["Start: operator wants no build artifact"]) --> W3A{"Runtime is<br/>JDK 11 or later?"}
    W3A -->|"Unknown"| W3AQ["Check java -version<br/>no version is pinned in the repository"]
    W3AQ --> W3A
    W3A -->|"No"| W3AE["Single-file source launch unavailable<br/>Section 1.3.2.4 records this<br/>as unsupported"]
    W3AE --> W3AF["Fallback: use W-1 or W-2.<br/>Compile-then-run states no floor and<br/>was exercised at targets 11, 17 and 21"]
    W3AF --> W3Z2(["End: greeting emitted<br/>via the fallback path"])
    W3A -->|"Yes"| W3B["Run java Hello.java<br/>F-004-RQ-004"]
    W3B --> W3C{"Launch<br/>succeeded?"}
    W3C -->|"No"| W3AE
    W3C -->|"Yes"| W3D["In-memory compilation and launch:<br/>no class file is created"]
    W3D --> W3E["stdout receives the greeting,<br/>byte-identical to W-1 and W-2<br/>F-002-RQ-004"]
    W3E --> W3F["Hand off to W-4"]
    W3F --> W3G["git status --short<br/>expect no output, nothing to clean"]
    W3G --> W3Z(["End: greeting emitted,<br/>no artifact produced"])
```

#### 4.1.2.5 W-4 — Output-Contract Verification

`W-4` is the acceptance procedure every launch path terminates in. Its oracle is published inside the repository: the fenced block at `README.md` lines 59–61, which `Project Guide.md` §4 records as comparing "byte-identical to real standard output." The contract deliberately fixes the literal and its single trailing separator rather than a byte count, because the separator is host-defined.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W4S(["Start: a launch path has produced output"]) --> W4A["Capture stdout, stderr<br/>and the exit status"]
    W4A --> W4B{"stdout equals the literal<br/>Hello from Java! followed by<br/>exactly one separator?"}
    W4B -->|"No"| W4BE["Contract breach of F-002-RQ-001<br/>or F-002-RQ-002"]
    W4B -->|"Yes"| W4C{"stderr<br/>empty?"}
    W4C -->|"No"| W4CE["Contract breach of F-002-RQ-003<br/>or F-003-RQ-003: no diagnostic<br/>output is ever expected"]
    W4C -->|"Yes"| W4D{"Exit status<br/>equals 0?"}
    W4D -->|"No"| W4DE["Contract breach of F-003-RQ-002.<br/>Section 1.3.2.4: a non-zero status is<br/>not a supported program state"]
    W4D -->|"Yes"| W4E{"Output unchanged with<br/>no, many and hostile<br/>arguments?"}
    W4E -->|"No"| W4EE["Contract breach of F-001-RQ-003<br/>or F-002-RQ-004"]
    W4E -->|"Yes"| W4F["Optional: compare both launch<br/>paths for byte equality<br/>C-6, F-002-RQ-004"]
    W4F --> W4Z(["End: contract satisfied,<br/>oracle and observation agree"])
    W4BE --> W4X["Re-check the launch form and the<br/>toolchain version, then re-run.<br/>No automated gate exists to re-test"]
    W4CE --> W4X
    W4DE --> W4X
    W4EE --> W4X
    W4X --> W4Z2(["End: unresolved,<br/>escalate to the owner"])
```

#### 4.1.2.6 In-Process Execution Flow

This is the detailed process flow for the three runtime features `F-001`, `F-002` and `F-003` — the only flow in Section 4 whose steps execute repository code. It is noteworthy for what it lacks: **zero decision diamonds and zero error branches**, because the source contains no conditional, loop or exception construct, and `args` appears only on line 11 (the Javadoc `@param` tag) and line 15 (the signature), never on an executable line.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P0(["Process start: JVM created<br/>by the launcher"]) --> P1["Load class Hello from the classpath<br/>bare name resolves because there is<br/>no package statement"]
    P1 --> P2["Resolve public static void main<br/>the class's only member<br/>F-001-RQ-001, F-001-RQ-005"]
    P2 --> P3["Invoke main once with the<br/>argument array; the array is<br/>never dereferenced, F-001-RQ-003"]
    P3 --> P4["Execute line 17: a single write<br/>to System.out, the only sink<br/>referenced in the source<br/>F-002-RQ-003, F-002-RQ-005"]
    P4 --> P5["Reach the closing brace of main<br/>at line 19 and return; no System.exit<br/>F-003-RQ-001"]
    P5 --> P6["JVM shuts down of its own accord<br/>no shutdown hook, no finaliser"]
    P6 --> P7(["Process end: stdout carries the<br/>greeting, stderr empty, status 0<br/>F-003-RQ-002, F-003-RQ-003"])
```

#### 4.1.2.7 Maintenance Processes M-1 to M-3

Three further processes are documented in `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` but are not launch workflows. `M-1` is the most procedurally involved process in the repository, and it carries the system's one genuinely counter-intuitive decision point: the comment census must be given the **pre-comment revision `0726b1d`** as its baseline, because at the current commit the diff is empty and "the census degenerates to zero," failing four checks against a correct tree.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M1S(["Start: maintainer intends a<br/>comment-only edit to Hello.java"]) --> M1A["Edit in byte mode, re-emitting CRLF<br/>on every added line<br/>F-008-RQ-005"]
    M1A --> M1B{"Baseline revision<br/>supplied to the census?"}
    M1B -->|"No, current commit used"| M1BE["Census reports all-zero blocks and<br/>four checks fail vacuously against<br/>a correct tree"]
    M1BE --> M1BR["Recovery: re-run with the<br/>pre-comment revision 0726b1d"]
    M1BR --> M1B
    M1B -->|"Yes, 0726b1d"| M1C["Export the baseline with git show<br/>into a scratch directory,<br/>named Hello.java"]
    M1C --> M1D["Compile both revisions and compare<br/>captured stdout and stderr with cmp"]
    M1D --> M1E{"Behaviour<br/>byte-identical?"}
    M1E -->|"No"| M1EE["The edit was not comment-only:<br/>revert and re-apply<br/>F-008-RQ-003"]
    M1EE --> M1A
    M1E -->|"Yes"| M1F{"Diff is<br/>additions-only?"}
    M1F -->|"No"| M1EE
    M1F -->|"Yes"| M1G["Run the line-ending, ASCII and<br/>tab censuses: CRLF on every line,<br/>zero non-ASCII, zero tabs"]
    M1G --> M1H["Hand off to M-2 quality gates"]
    M1H --> M1I["Discard every scratch directory,<br/>then confirm git status --short<br/>prints nothing"]
    M1I --> M1Z(["End: behaviour preserved,<br/>checkout clean"])
```

`M-2` runs the gates enumerated in Section 3.6.3 — `javac` diagnostics, `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` as the project's entire static-analysis surface, `javadoc` comment coverage, and the acceptance suite recorded at 49 of 49 checks passed. Two properties shape its flow. First, the suite must be run from a scratch directory outside the checkout, because "build, test and CI files are out of scope for this repository." Second, exactly one `javadoc` warning is a **passing** outcome, not a failure: the implicit default constructor at `Hello.java:6` can carry no doc comment, so coverage stands at 2 of 3 documentable members by design.

`M-3` is the publication process, and it is the one workflow in the repository whose terminal state has not yet been reached. `git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD` reports `0	11`: `main` is an ancestor of the working branch `jr_java1` and 11 commits behind it, so the entire documentation delivery is absent from the default branch. Completing `M-3` closes requirement `F-005-RQ-005`.

#### 4.1.2.8 Decision Point Register

Every decision point in the system, with the rule that resolves it and where that rule is written down:

| # | Decision point | Workflow | Resolution rule | Source of the rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D-1 | Is a JDK on `PATH`? | W-1, W-2, W-3 | A JDK is the sole prerequisite and is not vendored; running without one is unsupported | `README.md` line 18; Section 1.3.2.4 |
| D-2 | Which launch path? | W-1 … W-3 | All three are documented and produce byte-identical stdout; W-2 is the guide's recommendation | `README.md` lines 27–46 |
| D-3 | Is the runtime JDK 11 or later? | W-3 | Required for the single-file source launch; otherwise fall back to compile-then-run, which states no floor | `README.md` line 20 |
| D-4 | Did `javac` exit 0 with no diagnostics? | W-1, W-2, M-2 | Zero diagnostics is the acceptance threshold, including under `-Werror` | `Project Guide.md` §9.4; `F-004-RQ-005` |
| D-5 | Was the main class resolved? | W-1, W-2 | Compile first, or pass `-cp`; the bare name is correct because the class is in the default package | `Project Guide.md` §9.8 row 1 |
| D-6 | Is the build destination freshly generated and quoted? | W-2 | Must be produced by `mktemp -d`; a fixed, predictable path is pre-creatable and symlink-redirectable | `README.md` line 30 |
| D-7 | Does observed output match the published oracle? | W-4 | Literal plus exactly one host separator on stdout, empty stderr, exit status 0 | `README.md` lines 57–63 |
| D-8 | Must the working tree stay clean? | W-1, W-2 | The class file must never be committed; there is no ignore rule to catch it | `README.md` line 30; `F-005-RQ-002` |
| D-9 | Which revision is the census baseline? | M-1 | The pre-comment revision `0726b1d`, never the current commit | `Project Guide.md` §5.2 divergence 2, §9.8 row 4 |
| D-10 | Is one `javadoc` warning acceptable? | M-2 | Yes — exactly one, for the implicit default constructor, is expected by design | `Project Guide.md` §9.8 row 6; `F-008-RQ-004` |
| D-11 | Is the delivery reachable on `main`? | M-3 | `git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD` must report `0 0`; it currently reports `0 11` | `F-005-RQ-005`; Section 3.6.6.2 |

### 4.1.3 Integration Workflows

Section 1.3.1.1 fixes the integration surface exactly: "In scope are precisely the four interfaces in §1.2.1.3 … Nothing else is integrated." Those four are the JDK toolchain, the operating-system process contract, Git with its hosting platform, and the GPL v3 obligations attached to the covered work. Section 2.3.2 assigns features to each seam and adds two internal seams that are validated as such.

#### 4.1.3.1 Data Flow Between Systems

The system moves four kinds of data and no more: one source file, one optional class file, one line of standard output, and the tracked documentation set. There is no schema, record, file format, serialisation or data at rest — Section 1.3.1.2 records exactly one data element in the system, the compile-time constant on `Hello.java` line 17, plus one runtime-derived value, the host line separator.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph HostFS["Host filesystem"]
        SRC["Hello.java<br/>1073 bytes, CRLF x20, pure ASCII<br/>blob 3fd76ce"]
        CLS["Hello.class<br/>untracked artifact, or absent<br/>outside the system boundary"]
        SCRATCH["Per-run scratch directory<br/>from mktemp -d<br/>build output and javadoc HTML"]
    end

    subgraph JDKTools["JDK toolchain, OpenJDK 25.0.3"]
        JC["javac<br/>zero dependency resolution,<br/>zero network egress"]
        JV["java<br/>class launch or single-file launch"]
        JD["javadoc<br/>comment-coverage measurement"]
    end

    subgraph Runtime["System boundary"]
        PROC["JVM process from Hello.java<br/>one statement of work"]
    end

    subgraph ProcContract["OS process contract"]
        SOUT["stdout: 16-character literal<br/>plus one platform separator"]
        SERR["stderr: empty by design"]
        STAT["exit status: 0"]
    end

    subgraph GitLane["Git and hosting platform"]
        REPO["5 tracked blobs<br/>925008 bytes, 14 commits, 0 tags"]
        BASE["Pre-comment revision 0726b1d<br/>baseline for parity comparisons"]
    end

    REPO --> SRC
    BASE --> JC
    SRC --> JC
    SRC --> JV
    SRC --> JD
    JC --> CLS
    JC --> SCRATCH
    JD --> SCRATCH
    CLS --> JV
    SCRATCH --> JV
    JV --> PROC
    PROC --> SOUT
    PROC --> SERR
    PROC --> STAT
    SRC --> REPO
```

Two flows in that picture are deliberately one-directional. Nothing in `Hello.java` reads `README.md`, `LICENSE` or anything under `blitzy/documentation/`, so documentation data never reaches the runtime; Section 2.3.1 states the consequence — "a documentation change cannot alter runtime behaviour." And no build output ever flows back into the tracked set: `git ls-files` contains no `.class`, `.jar`, `.war` or `.zip` entry, and `README.md` line 30 instructs "Do not commit the class file either way."

#### 4.1.3.2 API Interactions

**There is no application programming interface in this system.** No HTTP, RPC or file-based interface exists; no port is bound, no listener is started and no network call is made. Section 1.3.2.3 additionally excludes service registries, artifact repositories, package managers, brokers, caches, databases, identity providers and secret stores, and records that `JAVA_HOME` "is explicitly not an integration point." Section 1.3.2.4 records that `Hello` cannot even be reused as a library, because a class in the default package cannot be imported by code in a named package.

What exists instead are three invocation contracts, and these are the whole of the system's interface surface:

| Invocation contract | Caller | Callee | Payload in | Payload out |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JVM entry-point contract | The JVM launcher | `Hello.main` | `String[] args`, accepted and never read | None; the method returns `void` |
| Compiler command line | POSIX shell | `javac` | The path `Hello.java`, optionally `-d <dir>` and `-Xlint:all -Werror` | Exit status, diagnostics on stderr, a class file |
| Launcher command line | POSIX shell | `java` | A class name with optional `-cp <dir>`, or the source path | Exit status, the greeting on stdout |

#### 4.1.3.3 Event Processing Flows

**No event processing exists.** There is no message broker, queue, topic, event bus, listener, callback or scheduler anywhere in the repository — `Project Guide.md` Appendix B states that the program "binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call; there is no service, database, broker or cache in this project." Section 1.3.2.1 additionally records the absence of concurrency: `main` is single-threaded, with no thread, executor or synchronisation construct, which a source census confirms (`Thread` and `Scanner` return zero matches).

The only occurrences that behave like events are lifecycle transitions observed by external parties, and they are strictly sequential:

| Occurrence | Raised by | Observed by | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Process start | The JVM launcher | The invoking shell | Implicit; the class is loaded and `main` invoked once |
| Single stdout write | `Hello.java` line 17 | The OS process contract | The one unit of work in the system |
| Normal return from `main` | `Hello.java` line 19 | The JVM | Triggers shutdown; no hook, finaliser or handler is registered |
| Process exit | The JVM | The invoking shell | Status 0 with empty stderr, the program's only outcome |
| Commit / pull-request merge | Maintainer, hosting platform | Downstream clones | `HEAD` = `2a78292`, "Merge pull request #1" — a human or bot step, not a pipeline |

#### 4.1.3.4 Batch Processing Sequences

**No batch processing exists.** There is no scheduler, cron entry, job runner or CI pipeline: Section 3.6.5 records existence tests returning absent for `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.travis.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml` and `.drone.yml`, with a full-history check confirming none has ever been tracked. Nothing re-runs any check automatically.

The nearest analogue in the repository is the **manually invoked verification batch** of `M-2`: a fixed sequence of independent assertions run in one pass from a scratch directory outside the checkout, recorded at 49 of 49 passing — 37 acceptance assertions plus 12 direct toolchain checks. It is a batch only in the sense of being a bulk, all-at-once, non-interactive sequence; it has no scheduler, no queue, no partitioning and no restart semantics, and its only durable record is `Project Guide.md` §3 and §4. A second bulk sequence is the cross-release compilation check, which exercises `javac` at release targets 11, 17 and 21 in one pass.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    BS(["Trigger: maintainer decides to verify<br/>no schedule, no pipeline, no gate"]) --> B1["Provision a scratch directory<br/>with mktemp -d, outside the checkout"]
    B1 --> B2["Paste the acceptance suite there;<br/>it is never committed, because build,<br/>test and CI files are out of scope"]
    B2 --> B3["Supply the four invocation arguments,<br/>including the pre-comment baseline"]
    B3 --> B4["Pass 1: compilation and static<br/>diagnostics, including -Xlint:all -Werror"]
    B4 --> B5["Pass 2: runtime parity across both<br/>documented launch paths"]
    B5 --> B6["Pass 3: comment placement<br/>and block census"]
    B6 --> B7["Pass 4: stored byte format,<br/>line endings, encoding, tabs"]
    B7 --> B8["Pass 5: javadoc coverage<br/>one accepted warning"]
    B8 --> B9["Pass 6: guide structure, literals,<br/>links and citation census"]
    B9 --> B10["Pass 7: cross-release compilation<br/>at targets 11, 17 and 21"]
    B10 --> B11{"All assertions<br/>passed?"}
    B11 -->|"No"| B12["Consult the recovery table:<br/>most failures trace to the census<br/>baseline, not to the tree"]
    B12 --> B3
    B11 -->|"Yes"| B13["Record the outcome in the project<br/>guide; no other durable record exists"]
    B13 --> B14["Discard every scratch directory,<br/>then confirm git status --short<br/>prints nothing"]
    B14 --> BZ(["End: 49 of 49 checks recorded"])
```

#### 4.1.3.5 Integration Sequence Diagrams

The first sequence shows `W-2`, the recommended build-and-launch path, with each participant in its own lane. It is the clearest view of where the system boundary is crossed: only the `java` lane's internal step executes repository code.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor OPR as Operator
    participant SH as POSIX shell
    participant MK as mktemp -d
    participant JC as javac 25.0.3
    participant FS as Filesystem
    participant JV as java, JVM process
    participant OS as OS process contract

    OPR->>SH: assign B from mktemp -d
    SH->>MK: request a per-run directory
    MK-->>SH: unique path, readable only by its owner
    OPR->>SH: javac -Xlint:all -d B Hello.java
    SH->>JC: compile one unit
    JC->>FS: read Hello.java, 1073 bytes, CRLF on 20 lines
    Note over JC: Zero imports, zero dependency resolution,<br/>zero network egress
    JC->>FS: write Hello.class into B
    JC-->>SH: exit 0, no diagnostics, empty stderr
    OPR->>SH: java -cp B Hello
    SH->>JV: launch class Hello by bare name
    JV->>FS: load Hello.class from B
    JV->>JV: invoke main, execute the single println
    JV->>OS: write the greeting plus one separator to stdout
    JV->>OS: return normally, no System.exit, status 0
    OS-->>OPR: greeting on stdout, empty stderr, status 0
    OPR->>SH: rm -rf B, then git status --short
    SH-->>OPR: no output, checkout unchanged
```

The second sequence shows the Git and hosting-platform integration, which is how the artifact reaches an operator at all. Its final state is the open item `F-005-RQ-005`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor MNT as Maintainer
    participant WT as Local working tree
    participant GIT as git
    participant HOST as Git hosting platform
    actor OPR as Downstream operator

    MNT->>WT: apply a comment-only edit to Hello.java
    MNT->>GIT: git status --short
    GIT-->>MNT: no output expected, no ignore rule exists
    MNT->>GIT: commit on branch jr_java1
    GIT->>HOST: push the branch
    MNT->>HOST: open a pull request
    HOST->>HOST: merge pull request 1, HEAD becomes 2a78292
    Note over HOST: main remains an ancestor, 11 commits behind HEAD.<br/>F-005-RQ-005 is open until the delivery reaches main
    OPR->>HOST: git clone
    HOST-->>OPR: 5 tracked text files, 925008 bytes, 0 tags
    OPR->>WT: build and run per W-1, W-2 or W-3
    Note over OPR,WT: GPL v3 obligations travel with every conveyed copy,<br/>with the dated modification notice at README.md line 5
```

The third sequence shows the **guide-to-toolchain seam** of Section 2.3.2 — the internal integration that makes the documentation trustworthy. Every command printed in `README.md` must execute exactly as written, and the guide's fenced expected-output block must compare byte-for-byte against real standard output.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor VAL as Validator
    participant GUIDE as README.md
    participant CLONE as Scratch copy of the repository
    participant TOOL as JDK toolchain
    participant ORACLE as Fenced expected-output block

    VAL->>GUIDE: extract every documented command literal
    GUIDE-->>VAL: javac Hello.java, the mktemp -d variant,<br/>java Hello, java Hello.java
    VAL->>CLONE: run each literal exactly as written
    CLONE->>TOOL: invoke javac, then java
    TOOL-->>CLONE: exit 0, greeting on stdout, empty stderr
    VAL->>ORACLE: read README.md lines 59 to 61
    ORACLE-->>VAL: the published expected output
    VAL->>VAL: compare captured stdout with the oracle byte for byte
    Note over VAL: Recorded result: byte-identical, and the<br/>untracked-artifact claim confirmed in a throwaway clone
```


## 4.2 Flowchart Requirements

This sub-section states, for each workflow drawn in Section 4.1, which mandatory flowchart elements it contains and which it cannot contain because the corresponding construct does not exist in the repository. It then enumerates the validation rules that govern each step.

### 4.2.1 Workflow Element Coverage

| Workflow | Start point | End point / states | Process steps | Decision diamonds | Error states | Recovery paths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| W-1 (§4.1.2.2) | Shell at the repository root | One: greeting emitted, tree clean or artifact knowingly retained | 12 | 4 — `D-1`, `D-4`, `D-5`, `D-8` | 3 — prerequisite unmet, file-name mismatch, main class not found | Re-run the compile or launch after the documented fix; delete the artifact |
| W-2 (§4.1.2.3) | Clean checkout that must remain clean | Two: zero-footprint success, or escalation on an unrecorded diagnostic | 9 | 2 — `D-6`, `D-4` | 2 — fixed-path substitution, compiler diagnostic | Regenerate the directory with `mktemp -d`; escalate a diagnostic to the owner |
| W-3 (§4.1.2.4) | Operator wanting no build artifact | Two: no-artifact success, or success via the fallback path | 6 | 2 — `D-3`, plus the launch-result check | 1 — version floor unmet, which also covers launch failure | Fall back to W-1 or W-2, which state no version floor |
| W-4 (§4.1.2.5) | Output produced by any launch path | Two: contract satisfied, or unresolved and escalated | 3 plus 4 breach nodes | 4 — `D-7` decomposed into stdout, stderr, status and argument checks | 4 — one per breached requirement | Re-check the launch form and toolchain version, then re-run |
| In-process (§4.1.2.6) | JVM created by the launcher | One: greeting on stdout, empty stderr, status 0 | 6 | **0** | **0** | Not applicable — no failure path exists in the source |
| M-1 (§4.1.2.7) | Maintainer intends a comment-only edit | One: behaviour preserved, checkout clean | 8 | 3 — `D-9`, parity check, additions-only check | 2 — wrong census baseline, edit not comment-only | Re-run with revision `0726b1d`; revert and re-apply the edit |
| M-2 (§4.1.3.4) | Maintainer decides to verify | One: 49 of 49 checks recorded | 12 | 1 — all-assertions-passed | 1 — assertion failure, most often the baseline rather than the tree | Correct the invocation argument and re-run the pass |
| M-3 (§4.1.2.7) | Maintainer with an unpublished branch | **Not yet reached** — `main` is 11 commits behind `HEAD` | Push, open pull request, merge | 1 — `D-11` | 1 — delivery unreachable on the default branch | Push and merge; closes `F-005-RQ-005` |

**Why the in-process flow has no decision or error element.** This is the single most important structural fact about the system's process model, and it is verified statically rather than assumed. A fixed-string census of `Hello.java` returns zero matches for `if (`, `for (`, `while (`, `switch (`, `try {`, `catch`, `throw`, `new ` and `System.exit(`; a comment-stripped word census returns zero for the same constructs; `System.err` and `System.in` return zero; and `args` never appears on an executable line. Section 1.3.2.1 lists "Explicit error handling" among the explicitly excluded capabilities, verified as "No `try`/`catch`, no thrown exception, no error branch anywhere in `Hello.java`."

### 4.2.2 System Boundaries and User Touchpoints

**Boundary crossings per workflow.** Section 1.3.1.2 places inside the boundary "the JVM process launched from `Hello.java` and the tracked files that describe and license it," and places outside it the JDK, the host operating system, Git with its hosting platform, and any `Hello.class` produced by a build.

| Workflow | Boundaries crossed, in order |
| --- | --- |
| W-1 | Operator → shell → `javac` → filesystem → `java` → **system boundary** → OS process contract → operator |
| W-2 | Operator → shell → `mktemp` → `javac` → scratch filesystem → `java` → **system boundary** → OS process contract → operator |
| W-3 | Operator → shell → `java` (compile and launch in one step, no filesystem artifact) → **system boundary** → OS process contract → operator |
| W-4 | OS process contract → operator → `README.md` oracle → operator |
| M-1 | Maintainer → editor → filesystem → `git` → `javac` → `java` → comparison utilities → maintainer |
| M-2 | Maintainer → scratch filesystem → `javac`, `java`, `javadoc`, GNU utilities → maintainer |
| M-3 | Maintainer → `git` → hosting platform → downstream clone |

**User touchpoint register.** The system has no user interface of any kind — Section 1.3.2.1 records "Console output only; no UI, hosted page, or port." Every touchpoint is therefore a shell interaction or a document read.

| Touchpoint | Medium | Workflow | Governing requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reading the operator guide | `README.md`, eight sections at lines 3, 10, 16, 22, 32, 55, 65, 75 | All | `F-007-RQ-001`, `F-007-RQbe-002` superseded by `F-007-RQ-002` |
| Typing a build command | Shell | W-1, W-2 | `F-004-RQ-003`, `F-004-RQ-006` |
| Typing a launch command | Shell | W-1, W-2, W-3 | `F-001-RQ-002`, `F-004-RQ-004` |
| Supplying command-line arguments | Shell | W-1, W-2, W-3 | `F-001-RQ-003` — accepted and never read |
| Reading the greeting | stdout | All | `F-002-RQ-001`, `F-002-RQ-002` |
| Observing the exit status | Shell status variable | W-4 | `F-003-RQ-002` |
| Comparing against the published oracle | `README.md` lines 59–61 | W-4 | `F-002-RQ-004` |
| Reading the licence terms | `LICENSE`, linked from `README.md` line 77 | Redistribution | `F-006-RQ-002` |
| Reading the in-source comments | `Hello.java` lines 1–5, 7–14, 16, 18 | Maintenance | `F-008-RQ-001` |
| Consulting the troubleshooting table | `Project Guide.md` §9.8, seven rows | Error recovery | `F-009-RQ-001` |

### 4.2.3 Timing and SLA Considerations

**No service-level agreement, performance target or timing constraint is recorded anywhere in this repository.** This is an observed absence, not an omission from this document. Section 2.2.1 states that "The repository declares no requirements document, no service-level objective and no performance target — there is no build descriptor, test suite or CI configuration in which one could be recorded," and the "Performance criteria" row of every one of the nine feature specifications in Section 2.2 reads "None is recorded." Section 1.3.2.4 records "Using the program as a performance, load, or soak benchmark" as an unsupported use case, because "no measurement, instrumentation, or timing exists; no such target is recorded anywhere."

Consequently no flow in Section 4.1 carries a timing annotation, a timeout, a deadline, a retry interval or a backoff schedule — none of those constructs exists to document. What the repository does quantify is structural rather than temporal:

| Quantified property | Recorded value | Where it is fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compiler diagnostics | Zero, including under `-Xlint:all -Werror` | `Project Guide.md` §9.4; `F-004-RQ-005` |
| `javadoc` warnings | Exactly one, accepted by design | `Project Guide.md` §9.6; `F-008-RQ-004` |
| Units of work per process run | One statement, executed exactly once | `F-002-RQ-005` |
| Threads of control | One; no thread, executor or synchronisation construct | Section 1.3.1.2; `F-003-RQ-004` |
| Standard-output size | The 16-character literal plus one host separator — 17 bytes on a host whose separator is LF | `README.md` line 63; `Project Guide.md` §4 |
| Acceptance checks | 49 executed, 49 passed, 0 failed | `Project Guide.md` §3 |
| Remaining project effort | 6.0 hours across six deferred items | `Project Guide.md` §2.2 |

The only *bound* that can be stated about a run is therefore structural: the in-process flow of §4.1.2.6 traverses one method frame containing one statement, with no loop, branch or blocking call, and `F-003-RQ-004` requires that "no non-terminating or blocking path can be taken." Whether a given run completes quickly is a property of the host and the JDK, neither of which this repository pins.

### 4.2.4 Validation Rules

#### 4.2.4.1 Business Rules at Each Step

Every rule below is a contract already stated in Section 2.2's "Business rules" rows or in the repository's own documents; none is invented here. The table maps each rule to the flow step it governs.

| Flow step | Business rule | Consequence of breach | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Class resolution (§4.1.2.6 P1) | The class must stay in the default package so the bare name launches it | The documented launch command stops working; `Project Guide.md` §9.8 row 1 applies | `F-001-RQ-002` |
| Entry-point invocation (P2) | `main` must remain the class's only member | Contradicts the class Javadoc at lines 1–5 that Sections 1.2.2.2 and 1.3.1.1 rely on | `F-001-RQ-005` |
| Argument handling (P3) | `args` must never be dereferenced; validating it would itself breach the contract | Argument insensitivity `C-5` is lost | `F-001-RQ-003` |
| The single write (P4) | The literal is the system's contract and may not change; the separator must stay host-supplied, never hard-coded | Invalidates `README.md` lines 57–63 and the acceptance oracle | `F-002-RQ-001`, `F-002-RQ-002` |
| Termination (P5) | Exit status 0 with an empty error stream is the program's only outcome | A non-zero status is not a supported program state (Section 1.3.2.4) | `F-003-RQ-001`, `F-003-RQ-002` |
| Build invocation (W-1, W-2) | The JDK-only property is load-bearing; introducing any manifest or third-party import forfeits it. No Java version may be pinned without an owner decision | `F-004-RQ-001` fails; the zero-supply-chain position is lost | `F-004-RQ-001` |
| Build destination (W-2, `D-6`) | The destination must be a freshly generated, owner-readable-only directory | Reintroduces the pre-creatable, symlink-redirectable path classed as a Security risk | `F-004-RQ-006` |
| Artifact disposal (W-1, `D-8`) | Build output must never be committed; no `.gitignore` exists to catch it | `F-005-RQ-002` fails; a binary enters a source-only distribution | `README.md` line 30 |
| Tracked-set composition | The tracked set defines the system boundary; adding a build, test or CI file changes both `F-005-RQ-001` and `F-004-RQ-001` | The system boundary of Section 1.3.1.2 shifts | `F-005-RQ-001` |
| Guide content (W-4) | Every documented command must be executable exactly as written, and the change summary must remain the first content block in the documented eight-section order | The guide-to-toolchain seam of Section 2.3.2 breaks | `F-007-RQ-001`, `F-007-RQ-002` |
| Source edit (M-1) | The edit must stay comment-only; the single `println`, the ignored `args` and the `System.exit`-free termination must survive any change | Behaviour preservation, a critical success factor per Section 1.2.3.2, is lost | `F-008-RQ-003` |
| Census invocation (M-1, `D-9`) | The baseline must be the pre-comment revision, or four checks fail vacuously against a correct tree | A correct tree is misreported as broken | `Project Guide.md` §5.2 divergence 2 |
| Verification artefacts (M-2) | Verification files must stay out of the tracked set, since build, test and CI files are out of scope | `F-005-RQ-001` fails | `Project Guide.md` §9.6 |
| Licence text (compliance) | The GPL v3 text is verbatim and may not be edited | `F-006-RQ-004` fails; the licence instrument is no longer the published one | `F-006-RQ-001`, `F-006-RQ-004` |

#### 4.2.4.2 Data Validation Requirements

The program validates nothing at run time, and does so deliberately: no input is read, so there is nothing to validate, and Section 2.2.2 records that validating `args` "would itself breach `F-001-RQ-003`." All data validation in this system is therefore performed by the toolchain and by the verification procedures, against the artifacts rather than against runtime values.

| Validation surface | Rule and threshold | Applied in | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compiler diagnostics | Zero diagnostics under `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` — the project's entire static-analysis surface, as no linter is configured | W-1, W-2, M-2 | `F-004-RQ-005` |
| Doc-comment syntax and coverage | Valid under `javadoc -Xdoclint:all`, with the implicit default-constructor warning the only accepted one; coverage 2 of 3 members | M-2 | `F-008-RQ-004` |
| Output byte comparison | Captured stdout must equal the fenced block at `README.md` lines 59–61 byte for byte | W-4 | `F-002-RQ-001` |
| Stream and status assertions | stderr empty; exit status 0; both compared byte-identical against a build of the pre-comment source | W-4, M-1 | `F-003-RQ-002`, `F-003-RQ-003` |
| Launch-path equivalence | `java Hello` and `java Hello.java` must yield identical stdout, as must runs with no, many and hostile arguments | W-4 | `F-002-RQ-004` |
| Additions-only diff | 15 added, 0 removed against revision `0726b1d`, with the five original code lines byte-identical | M-1 | `F-008-RQ-003` |
| Comment block census | `added=15`, `/**`=2, `*/`=2, `//`=2, with indentation and placement assertions | M-1 | `F-008-RQ-001`, `F-008-RQ-002` |
| Stored byte format | `Hello.java`: CR on 20 of 20 lines, zero non-ASCII bytes, zero tabs. `README.md`: zero CR bytes, newline-terminated | M-1, M-2 | `F-008-RQ-005`, `F-005-RQ-004` |
| Guide structure | Eight `##` headings in the documented order; summary body within 70 words and 8 lines — measured at 55 and 3; emphasis confined to one entry per changed file | M-2 | `F-007-RQ-001`, `F-007-RQ-003` |
| Link and citation census | Exactly two relative links, both resolving on disk; citations by stable symbol with zero line-number locators | M-2 | `F-007-RQ-004`, `F-007-RQ-005` |
| Working-tree cleanliness | `git status --short` must print nothing | W-1, W-2, M-1, M-2 | `F-005-RQ-002` |
| Tracked-set composition | `git ls-files` must contain no `.class`, `.jar`, `.war` or `.zip` entry | M-3 | `F-005-RQ-002` |

One validation surface is explicitly declared out of reach rather than merely unimplemented: `Project Guide.md` §3 lists the rendered appearance of the guide among its "Not Covered" areas, and notes that comment wording "is not executed and prose accuracy is not machine-checkable." The guide's structure was asserted against its Markdown source, never against a rendered page.

#### 4.2.4.3 Authorization Checkpoints

**The program has no authorization checkpoint, and no authentication or authorization surface exists to place one on.** `Project Guide.md` §6 states it without qualification: the program "reads no input, dereferences no argument, opens no resource, binds no port, makes no network call and has no dependency manifest, so there is no injection surface, no supply-chain exposure, no authentication or authorisation surface and no data-at-rest concern." Section 1.3.1.2 adds that the system "defines no roles, accounts, or permissions of its own," and Section 1.3.2.1 records the absence of authentication, authorization and secrets — "No credential, key, environment variable, or secret read by any tracked file."

Three access controls nonetheless bear on the workflows, and all three are properties of the host or the hosting platform rather than of the system:

| Checkpoint | Enforced by | Workflow step | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Filesystem ownership of the build destination | The host, through `mktemp -d`, which "returns a uniquely named one readable only by its owner" | W-2, step `D-6` — the only security-motivated control in any documented command | `README.md` line 30 |
| Pull-request merge | The Git hosting platform | M-3 — visible as `HEAD` = `2a78292`, "Merge pull request #1"; a human or bot step, not a pipeline | Section 3.6.5 |
| Clone access to the remote | The Git hosting platform's own controls | W-1 … W-3 precondition; no credential is required by anything in the project | `F-005-RQ-003` |

Two related controls are recorded as absent rather than passing: the repository carries no `CODEOWNERS` file, so no in-repository review rule governs a change, and commit signing is recorded as deferred infrastructure.

#### 4.2.4.4 Regulatory and Licence Compliance Checks

**No regulatory regime is named anywhere in this repository**, and no data-protection, financial or safety obligation can attach to it: there is exactly one data element in the system — a compile-time ASCII string constant — with no input surface, no persistence surface, no network surface and no personal data of any kind (Sections 1.3.1.2 and 1.3.2.1).

The one binding compliance instrument is the licence. `LICENSE` holds the verbatim GNU General Public License, Version 3, 29 June 2007, and because the covered work was modified, the guide carries a dated modification notice. The gate below is the compliance checkpoint that `M-3` must pass before a copy is conveyed.


## 4.3 Technical Implementation

### 4.3.1 State Management

The program itself holds no state. `Hello.java` declares no field, no explicit constructor and creates no instance — its class Javadoc at lines 1–5 records the property directly ("it has no field, creates no instance"), a census of the file returns zero matches for `new `, and `README.md` line 12 states that the program "reads no input, opens no resource and keeps no state." Section 1.3.1.2 gives the boundary consequence: the persistence surface is "None — no state kept between or within runs."

Three things nonetheless transition through states across the workflows of Section 4.1, and all three sit *outside* the program: the operating-system process, the build artifact, and the repository delivery itself.

#### 4.3.1.1 State Transitions — Process Lifecycle

This is the state machine the in-process flow of §4.1.2.6 traverses. Every transition is unconditional except the one that leaves `Starting`, and that branch is a property of the classpath rather than of the program.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "No process exists" as NotRunning
    state "JVM starting, launcher invoked" as Starting
    state "Class Hello resolved by bare name" as Resolved
    state "main frame entered" as MainEntered
    state "Single write to standard output completed" as Emitted
    state "Control returned from main" as Returned
    state "JVM shut down" as Terminated
    state "Launch failed, main class not found" as LaunchFailed

    [*] --> NotRunning
    NotRunning --> Starting : java Hello, java -cp B Hello, or java Hello.java
    Starting --> Resolved : no package statement, so the bare name resolves
    Starting --> LaunchFailed : no compiled class on the classpath
    Resolved --> MainEntered : public static void main invoked exactly once
    MainEntered --> Emitted : line 17 executed exactly once, F-002-RQ-005
    Emitted --> Returned : closing brace at line 19, no System.exit call
    Returned --> Terminated : JVM shuts down of its own accord
    Terminated --> [*] : greeting on stdout, stderr empty, exit status 0
    LaunchFailed --> [*] : platform diagnostic on stderr, non-zero status
    note right of MainEntered
        No field, no instance, no retained state.
        The argument array is accepted and never dereferenced.
        No shutdown hook and no finaliser is registered.
    end note
```

#### 4.3.1.2 State Transitions — Build Artifact Lifecycle

`Hello.class` is the only artifact any workflow produces, and Section 1.3.1.2 places it explicitly outside the system boundary as "an untracked artifact the guide explicitly instructs must not be committed." Its lifecycle is the reason `W-1` ends in a hygiene decision and `W-2` exists at all.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "Absent, clean checkout" as Absent
    state "Present in the checkout, untracked and unignored" as UntrackedInTree
    state "Present in a per-run scratch directory" as OutOfTree
    state "Never materialised" as NeverMade
    state "Committed in error, prohibited" as Committed
    state "Discarded with the scratch directory" as Discarded

    [*] --> Absent
    Absent --> UntrackedInTree : javac Hello.java, build Path A
    Absent --> OutOfTree : javac -d B Hello.java, build Path B
    Absent --> NeverMade : java Hello.java, single-file source launch
    UntrackedInTree --> Absent : rm -f Hello.class
    UntrackedInTree --> Committed : staged and committed, breaching F-005-RQ-002
    Committed --> Absent : revert and remove from the tracked set
    OutOfTree --> Discarded : rm -rf the per-run directory
    NeverMade --> [*]
    Discarded --> [*]
    Absent --> [*]
    note right of UntrackedInTree
        Reachable only because no .gitignore exists.
        Proven by compiling inside a throwaway clone.
        README.md line 30 instructs that it must never be committed.
    end note
```

#### 4.3.1.3 State Transitions — Repository Delivery State

The delivery has its own state machine, and it is the one state machine in this system whose terminal state has **not** been reached. Because `git tag` returns zero tags across 14 commits, each state is identified by a commit SHA rather than a version.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    state "Undocumented, three tracked files" as Undocumented
    state "Source commented and operator guide written" as Documented
    state "Specification documents added" as Specified
    state "Merged on the working branch, ahead of main" as AheadUnpublished
    state "Reachable on the default branch" as Published

    [*] --> Undocumented : revision 0726b1d, README.md 41 bytes on one line
    Undocumented --> Documented : commits 3c3af75 through ce8e85c
    Documented --> Specified : the blitzy documentation commits
    Specified --> AheadUnpublished : merge of pull request 1, HEAD 2a78292
    AheadUnpublished --> Published : push and merge to main, closing F-005-RQ-005
    Published --> [*]
    note right of AheadUnpublished
        Current state. main is an ancestor of branch
        jr_java1 and 11 commits behind it, so the whole
        documentation delivery is absent from main.
    end note
```

#### 4.3.1.4 Data Persistence Points

There is no database, no file written by the program, and no state that survives a run. Every persistence point in the system belongs to the toolchain or to Git.

| Persistence point | Written by | Durability | Tracked? | Workflow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Hello.java` | The maintainer's editor | Permanent; blob `3fd76ce`, 1,073 bytes, CRLF on all 20 lines | Yes | M-1 |
| `Hello.class` beside the source | `javac`, build Path A | Until deleted; untracked and unignored | No — must never be committed | W-1 |
| `Hello.class` in a scratch directory | `javac`, build Path B | Until the per-run directory is removed | No | W-2 |
| `javadoc` HTML output | `javadoc` | Until the scratch directory is removed; "never committed" | No | M-2 |
| Baseline export of the pre-comment source | `git show` into a scratch path named `Hello.java` | Until the scratch directory is removed | No | M-1 |
| Git object store | `git commit`, the hosting platform's merge | Permanent; five blobs, 14 commits, zero tags | Yes | M-3 |
| The verification outcome record | The maintainer, into `Project Guide.md` §3 and §4 | Permanent, and the **only** durable record, since nothing re-runs the checks | Yes | M-2 |

Nothing is persisted at run time: the single `println` writes to a stream, not to storage, and `System.` appears in the source only on line 17 (the call) and line 18 (a comment), with zero references to a file, socket or other stream.

#### 4.3.1.5 Caching Requirements

**No cache exists and none is required.** `Project Guide.md` Appendix B states that there is "no service, database, broker or cache in this project," and §9.1 adds that there is "no package manager step, no virtual environment, no container, no database, no broker and no bound port." Three specific caching layers that a Java project would ordinarily have are absent for structural reasons rather than by configuration choice:

| Cache that would ordinarily exist | Why it is absent here |
| --- | --- |
| Dependency / artifact cache | Nothing is resolved or downloaded at build time; there is no manifest and no lock file of any kind, and the build performs zero network egress |
| Build or incremental-compilation cache | There is no build system to hold one — `javac` is invoked directly on a single compilation unit of 1,073 bytes |
| Application-level cache | There is no state to cache: one compile-time string constant and one runtime-derived line separator are the whole data domain |

The per-run scratch directory is the deliberate *opposite* of a cache. `mktemp -d` generates a fresh directory on every invocation and the workflows remove it afterwards, which is what makes each build destination unique and owner-readable-only; reusing a fixed, predictable location is the condition `README.md` line 30 warns against.

#### 4.3.1.6 Transaction Boundaries

The system has no transactional resource — no database, message broker or distributed participant — so there is no commit protocol, no two-phase coordination and no rollback log. What the workflows do have are per-invocation boundaries, each re-runnable from unchanged inputs:

| Boundary | Unit | Atomicity property observed | Undo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The single write | `Hello.java` line 17 | Exactly one write per process run; no loop or conditional can repeat or skip it (`F-002-RQ-005`) | None — and none is needed; nothing is persisted |
| A `javac` invocation | One compilation unit | Terminates either at exit 0 with no diagnostics, or with a diagnostic on stderr; recorded outcome at `HEAD` is exit 0 for both build paths | `rm -f Hello.class`, or discard the scratch directory |
| A `java` invocation | One process | Produces the complete payload and exit status 0, or fails to resolve the main class and produces neither | None required; the run leaves nothing behind |
| A source edit | `Hello.java` | Verified as all-or-nothing by an additions-only diff against `0726b1d` — 15 added, 0 removed (`F-008-RQ-003`) | Revert and re-apply in byte mode |
| A commit or merge | The Git object store | The unit of durable change; requirement versions are anchored to commit SHAs because no tags exist | `git revert`; the branch state is itself recoverable |

One boundary gap is worth stating because it is the source of the repository's recurring hygiene hazard: **`W-1` is two invocations, not one.** An operator who compiles and then stops has left `Hello.class` in the checkout with no run having occurred, in the `UntrackedInTree` state of §4.1.3.2 — and with no `.gitignore` to catch it, that is precisely the accidental-commit risk the guide mitigates by documenting build Path B and the `rm -f` cleanup.

### 4.3.2 Error Handling

#### 4.3.2.1 In-Program Error Handling

**`Hello.java` contains no error handling of any kind, and this is a specified property rather than an oversight.** Section 1.3.2.1 lists "Explicit error handling" among the explicitly excluded capabilities, verified as "No `try`/`catch`, no thrown exception, no error branch anywhere in `Hello.java`." Static census of the file confirms zero matches for `try {`, `catch`, `throw`, `new `, `System.exit(` and `System.err`, and the source contains no query of the output stream's error state — so the program performs no error detection whatsoever.

`Project Guide.md` §6 explains why whole categories of failure cannot arise: the program "reads no input, dereferences no argument, opens no resource, binds no port, makes no network call and has no dependency manifest, so there is no injection surface, no supply-chain exposure, no authentication or authorisation surface and no data-at-rest concern." Section 2.2.4 records the resulting invariant: the termination path "is unconditional because there is no error path to take." The program's only outcome is empty stderr and exit status 0.

All error handling in this system therefore lives in the surrounding workflow, and the repository documents it in one authoritative place: the seven-row troubleshooting table at `Project Guide.md` §9.8.

#### 4.3.2.2 Error Catalogue

| # | Error state | Stage | Cause | Recovery | Automated? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E-1 | `Could not find or load main class Hello` | Launch | No compiled class on the classpath, or the wrong working directory | Compile first, or launch with `java -cp <build dir> Hello`; the bare name is correct because the class is in the default package | No |
| E-2 | `error: class Hello is public, should be declared in a file named Hello.java` | Compile | The source was exported under another name — common when writing a baseline revision to a scratch file | Export into a directory as `Hello.java` | No |
| E-3 | `Hello.class` appears in `git status` | Repository hygiene | There is no ignore rule in this repository | Delete it, or compile to a directory outside the checkout with `-d` | No |
| E-4 | `block census wrong: /**=0 */=0 //=0` | Verification | The census was given the current commit as its baseline, where the comments are already committed | Re-run with the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` as the baseline | No |
| E-5 | Mixed line endings, or `final terminator not CRLF` | Verification | An editor normalised `Hello.java` to LF on save | Restore the file and re-apply the edit in byte mode, re-emitting CRLF on every line including added ones | No |
| E-6 | `javadoc` reports one warning | Verification | Expected: the implicit default constructor can carry no doc comment | No action; documenting it would require declaring a constructor, which is out of scope | Not an error |
| E-7 | The direct source launch fails on an older JDK | Launch | Single-file source launch needs JDK 11 or later | Use the compile-then-run path, which has no such floor | No |

Two of these are not program faults at all but consequences of deliberate repository decisions. `E-3` exists because no `.gitignore` was added — a hygiene item deferred by owner decision. `E-5` exists because `Hello.java` is stored CRLF on all 20 lines with no `.gitattributes` and with `core.autocrlf` and `core.eol` unset, so line-ending preservation depends entirely on editor discipline; Section 3.6.1 records this as a Medium-severity technical risk, "Open — accepted by design."

#### 4.3.2.4 Retry Mechanisms

**No automated retry mechanism exists**, and no construct capable of implementing one is present: there is no loop in the source, no scheduler, no job runner and no CI pipeline. Retry in this system means an operator re-running a command by hand, and that is safe because every documented command is deterministic in its inputs and outputs:

| Property that makes manual re-run safe | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| The payload is a compile-time constant; nothing at run time can alter it | Section 2.2.3; `Hello.java` line 17 |
| Output is identical across both launch paths and under any argument list, including hostile arguments | `F-002-RQ-004`; `Project Guide.md` §4 |
| Re-running `javac` re-derives the same class file from the same 1,073-byte unit, with zero dependency resolution | Section 3.6.2 |
| `mktemp -d` yields a **new** directory on each run, so a repeated `W-2` never collides with a previous attempt | `README.md` line 30 |
| Nothing is persisted by the program, so no partial state can be left behind to poison a second attempt | Section 1.3.1.2 |

The one re-run that must change an argument rather than simply repeat is `E-4`: re-running the comment census unchanged reproduces the same vacuous failure, because the defect is in the invocation, not the tree. The correct retry supplies revision `0726b1d` as the baseline.

#### 4.3.2.5 Fallback Processes

Four fallbacks are documented, and each is a substitution of one documented path for another rather than a degraded mode:

| Trigger | Fallback | Requirement relationship |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single-file source launch unavailable — JDK earlier than 11 | Compile-then-run (`W-1` or `W-2`), which states no version floor and was exercised at release targets 11, 17 and 21 | `F-004-RQ-004` falls back to `F-004-RQ-003` |
| The working tree must stay clean, or a predictable output path is unacceptable | Build Path B — compile with `-d` into a freshly generated `mktemp -d` directory and launch with `-cp` | `F-004-RQ-006` substitutes for `F-004-RQ-003` |
| Path A already ran and left an artifact | `rm -f Hello.class`, then confirm with `git status --short` | Restores `F-005-RQ-002` |
| The comment census reports all-zero blocks | Re-invoke with the pre-comment revision as the baseline | Restores the intent of `F-008-RQ-003` |

Two fallbacks that a system of this kind might be expected to have do **not** exist, and their absence is recorded rather than inferred: there is no fallback toolchain, because a JDK is the sole prerequisite and is not vendored in the repository; and there is no fallback verification gate, because `Project Guide.md` §1.4 states that "Nothing re-runs the documentation checks on future changes."

#### 4.3.2.6 Error Notification Flows

**There is no notification channel.** Section 1.3.2.1 records the absence of logging, metrics, tracing and monitoring — "No logging framework and no diagnostic output — stderr is deliberately empty" — and Section 1.3.2.3 excludes external monitoring and log aggregation. With no CI pipeline there is also no build notification, no failing-check email and no status badge.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph ProgramLane["The program — inside the boundary"]
        PG1["Hello.java writes one line<br/>to standard output"]
        PG2["stderr deliberately left empty,<br/>F-003-RQ-003"]
        PG3["Exit status 0 always,<br/>F-003-RQ-002"]
    end

    subgraph ToolLane2["The toolchain — outside the boundary"]
        TL1["javac writes its own diagnostics<br/>to stderr; zero at HEAD"]
        TL2["java writes launch failures<br/>to stderr"]
        TL3["javadoc writes one accepted<br/>warning to stderr"]
    end

    subgraph HumanLane["Human channels — the only ones that exist"]
        HL1["Operator reads the terminal"]
        HL2["Troubleshooting table,<br/>Project Guide 9.8, seven rows"]
        HL3["Verification outcome recorded in<br/>Project Guide 3 and 4 — the only<br/>durable record of any check"]
        HL4["Pull request and owner decision<br/>for items that cannot be fixed locally"]
    end

    subgraph AbsentLane["Channels verified absent"]
        AB1["No logging framework,<br/>no metrics, no tracing"]
        AB2["No CI pipeline, so no build<br/>notification and no gate"]
        AB3["No alerting, paging<br/>or log aggregation"]
    end

    PG1 --> HL1
    PG2 --> HL1
    PG3 --> HL1
    TL1 --> HL1
    TL2 --> HL1
    TL3 --> HL1
    HL1 --> HL2
    HL2 --> HL3
    HL3 --> HL4
    AB1 --- AB2
    AB2 --- AB3
```

The practical consequence is stated in Section 3.6.3: the 49 recorded checks were run manually, are not automatically repeatable, and "their only durable record is `Project Guide.md` §3 and §4." Any change to `Hello.java` requires a manual `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` re-run, because nothing will do it on the maintainer's behalf.

#### 4.3.2.7 Recovery Procedures

Recovery in this system is command-level and idempotent. The procedures below are the complete set the repository documents.

| Procedure | Command sequence | Restores | Workflow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Remove an in-tree build artifact | `rm -f Hello.class`, then `git status --short` expecting no output | A clean working tree; `F-005-RQ-002` | W-1 |
| Discard per-run scratch space | `rm -rf` the build, baseline and suite directories, then `git status --short` | Zero footprint outside and inside the checkout | W-2, M-1, M-2 |
| Re-establish a launchable class | Recompile, or relaunch with `java -cp <build dir> Hello` | `F-001-RQ-002`; resolves `E-1` | W-1, W-2 |
| Restore the compilable unit | Export or rename the source to `Hello.java` so the file name matches the public class | `F-001-RQ-004`; resolves `E-2` | M-1 |
| Restore stored byte format | Restore the file and re-apply the edit in byte mode, re-emitting CRLF on every line, then re-run the line-ending census | `F-008-RQ-005`, `F-005-RQ-004`; resolves `E-5` | M-1 |
| Re-establish a valid census | Re-invoke the suite with revision `0726b1d` as the baseline argument | The additions-only intent of `F-008-RQ-003`; resolves `E-4` | M-1, M-2 |
| Prove behaviour was preserved | Build both revisions into separate directories, capture stdout and stderr from each, and compare with `cmp` | `F-008-RQ-003`; the recorded result is byte-identical behaviour | M-1 |
| Make the delivery reachable | Push the branch and merge, until `git rev-list --left-right --count main...HEAD` reports `0 0` | `F-005-RQ-005`; the only open recovery in the system | M-3 |

No recovery procedure in this table requires a backup, a snapshot or a restore point, because the program persists nothing and the source is recoverable from Git history — which is also what supplies the `0726b1d` baseline that two of the procedures depend on.

Two requirements are not reachable by any workflow in this section, and the reason is recorded rather than inferred. `F-006-RQ-005`, the per-file copyright header, is an artifact property with no procedural step — it is satisfied by editing `Hello.java`, not by running anything, and it remains an open owner decision. `F-007-RQ-006`, the layout claim matching the tracked tree, is likewise a text correction: `README.md` line 67 states "three tracked files at the root, and no subdirectories" while the tree holds five tracked files and `blitzy/documentation/`, and Section 1.3.2.2 records that no deferred item covers the correction.

### 4.4.3 Process Constructs Not Applicable to This Repository

The following process and flow constructs are standard in a technical specification of this kind and are **absent here**. Each absence was confirmed by direct inspection rather than assumed, and each is listed so that its absence is not mistaken for an omission from this section.

| Construct | Verification of absence |
| --- | --- |
| Business transaction or approval flow | No customer, order, ledger or approval concept; no persistence and no state (Section 1.3.1.2) |
| Authorization or role-based flow | The system "defines no roles, accounts, or permissions of its own"; no authentication or authorization surface exists |
| API request/response flow | No HTTP, RPC or file-based interface; no port bound, no listener started, no network call made |
| Event-driven or message flow | No broker, queue, topic, bus, listener or callback; `Project Guide.md` Appendix B states there is "no service, database, broker or cache in this project" |
| Scheduled or batch job flow | No scheduler, cron entry or job runner; the nearest analogue is the manually invoked verification batch of §4.1.3.4 |
| CI/CD pipeline flow | Existence tests absent for `.github/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.travis.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `.drone.yml`; no such file has ever been tracked in 14 commits |
| Deployment or rollback flow | No packaging, no published coordinates, no deployment descriptor; "Deploying it as a service" is recorded as unsupported |
| Timeout, retry-with-backoff or circuit-breaker policy | No loop, scheduler or retry construct exists; no timing or SLA figure is recorded anywhere |
| Saga or compensating-transaction flow | No transactional resource and no distributed participant |
| Cache population or invalidation flow | No cache at any layer; nothing is resolved at build time and nothing is stateful at run time |
| Database transaction or migration flow | No database and no schema; the whole data domain is one string constant plus the host line separator |
| Session or conversation state flow | Single process, single statement, no state kept between or within runs |
| Concurrency or synchronisation flow | Single-threaded `main`; `Thread` and executor constructs return zero matches |
| Monitoring, alerting or on-call flow | No logging framework, metrics, tracing or log aggregation; stderr is deliberately empty |
| Internationalisation flow | Hard-coded ASCII literal; no resource bundle or locale logic; zero bytes at or above `0x80` in any text file |
| Input validation flow | No input path exists, and validating `args` would itself breach `F-001-RQ-003` |
| Regulatory or data-subject flow | No regulatory regime is named anywhere; no personal data, no input surface, no persistence surface |

# 5. System Architecture

## 5.1 High-Level Architecture

The architecture documented in this section is the entire system. The tracked inventory is five files totalling 925,008 bytes — `Hello.java`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` and `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` — and two directories, `blitzy/` and `blitzy/documentation/`. There is no `src/` tree, no build descriptor, no configuration file, no test directory, no CI descriptor and no infrastructure definition; a direct probe of the worktree confirms the absence of `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle`, `.java-version`, `.sdkmanrc`, `module-info.java`, `.gitignore`, `Makefile`, `Dockerfile` and `.editorconfig`.

Where a conventional architectural element does not exist, this section records it as verified absent rather than approximating it. No service level, latency target, throughput figure, availability objective or capacity plan appears anywhere in the repository, and none is asserted here.

### 5.1.1 System Overview

#### 5.1.1.1 Architecture Style and Rationale

The runtime architecture is a **single-process, single-module, invoke-and-exit console application**. One compilation unit declares one public class in the default package; that class declares one static method; that method performs one write to standard output and returns. Stripping comments from `Hello.java` leaves exactly five lines of executable code — the class declaration, the `main` signature, the single `System.out.println` call and two closing braces — and a keyword census over those five lines returns zero occurrences of `if`, `for`, `while`, `switch`, `try`, `catch`, `throw`, `new`, `import`, `package`, `synchronized`, `System.exit` and `System.err`. There is no tier decomposition, no service boundary, no inter-process communication, no concurrency and no long-running runtime.

The repository nowhere states this style as a design choice, so the rationale below is reconstructed from the constraints the artifacts actually impose:

- **The unit of compilation is the unit of deployment.** With one class in the default package and no `module-info.java`, the smallest shippable thing is the source file itself. Introducing layers would require introducing a build model, and there is none to extend.
- **There is no dependency graph to arrange.** `Hello.java` declares zero `import` statements, so the only library surface is the implicitly available `java.lang`. Styles whose purpose is to govern dependency direction — layered, hexagonal, ports-and-adapters — would have nothing to arrange.
- **There is no state and no I/O beyond one write.** The class Javadoc at `Hello.java` lines 1–5 records that it "has no field, creates no instance"; `README.md` line 12 states the program "reads no input, opens no resource and keeps no state." Styles that exist to coordinate state or distribute work have no subject matter here.
- **Invocation is the whole protocol.** The `args` array is accepted only to satisfy the signature the JVM requires and is never dereferenced (`Hello.java` lines 11–13), and termination is by normal return with no `System.exit` call (`Hello.java` line 18), which makes the operating-system process boundary the only interface contract worth specifying.

A second architecture coexists with the runtime one and is easy to miss because it carries no code: a **source-only, documentation-dominant delivery and governance architecture**. Of the 925,008 tracked bytes, 884,733 are the two Markdown documents under `blitzy/documentation/` and 1,073 are the program; distribution is by Git clone rather than by published artifact, and redistribution is governed by the verbatim GPL v3 text in `LICENSE`. The two architectures are coupled in one direction only: nothing in `Hello.java` reads `README.md`, `LICENSE` or anything under `blitzy/documentation/`, so a documentation change cannot alter runtime behaviour, while a source change invalidates documentation claims.

#### 5.1.1.2 Architectural Principles and Patterns

| Principle | How the repository realises it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Statelessness by construction | No field, no explicit constructor, no instance ever created; `main` is `static`, so nothing is carried between or within runs | `Hello.java` lines 1–6, 15; `README.md` line 12 |
| Single responsibility taken to its limit | One class, one method, one statement, one output sink | `Hello.java` line 17 and its comment at line 16 |
| One output sink, explicitly fixed | The line comment at line 16 makes single-sink behaviour a stated design property: "no other sink is written" | `Hello.java` line 16 |
| Termination by normal return | No `System.exit` anywhere; `README.md` line 63 calls this "a deliberate property of the program rather than an omission" | `Hello.java` line 18; `README.md` line 63 |
| Zero-dependency buildability | No manifest, no lock file, nothing resolved or downloaded at build time; only the implicitly imported `java.lang` is used | `README.md` line 18; `Project Guide.md` §9.3 |
| Configuration-free operation | No environment variable and no secret is read by any tracked file; `JAVA_HOME` is not required | `Project Guide.md` §9.2, Appendix E |
| Determinism as the contract | Output is a compile-time constant, identical across both launch paths and under any argument list | `README.md` lines 46, 57–63 |
| Portability over reproducibility | Toolchain versions are recorded, never enforced; no `--release` or `--source` setting exists anywhere | `README.md` line 18; `Project Guide.md` Appendix D |
| Documentation as the deliverable | The executable behaviour was deliberately left untouched while in-source comments and an eight-section operator guide were added | `README.md` lines 7–8; `Project Guide.md` §5.1 rows 1–3 |
| Command discipline in place of tooling | With no `.gitignore` and no `.gitattributes`, working-tree cleanliness and byte-format stability are maintained by documented commands rather than enforced by configuration | `README.md` line 30; `Project Guide.md` §5.2 item 5 |

Two patterns conventionally expected of a Java system are absent for structural rather than stylistic reasons and are recorded as such: there is no dependency-injection or inversion-of-control arrangement, because no collaborator object exists to inject; and there is no layering or facade, because there is exactly one path through the system.

#### 5.1.1.3 System Boundaries and Major Interfaces

The boundary encloses the five tracked files and nothing else. Everything the system touches at build or run time — the JDK, the operating system, Git and its hosting platform, and every artifact a build produces — sits outside it and is neither vendored nor versioned in the repository. Four interface seams cross that boundary, and they are the complete set.

| Interface | Contract at the seam | Direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **I-1 Compilation interface** | One compilation unit whose file name must match its public class; compiles with no `--release`/`--source` setting and no dependency to resolve; exits 0 with no diagnostics, including under `-Xlint:all -Werror` | Inbound to `javac` |
| **I-2 JVM entry-point interface** | `public static void main(String[] args)` on a default-package class, resolved by the bare name `Hello`; the launcher invokes it exactly once; the argument array is accepted and never read | Inbound from the `java` launcher |
| **I-3 Process and standard-stream interface** | Standard output receives the literal `Hello from Java!` plus one platform line separator; standard error stays empty; exit status is 0 by normal return | Outbound to the operating system |
| **I-4 Distribution and governance interface** | Source-only conveyance by Git clone, branch and merge over HTTPS from `github.com/rjhonsi/BlitzyRepo2_Java`, under the GPL v3 terms carried verbatim in `LICENSE` with a dated modification notice at `README.md` line 5 | Bidirectional with the hosting platform |

Four categories of boundary are absent and verified so: there is no network boundary (`Project Guide.md` Appendix B: the program "binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call"), no persistence boundary, no trust or authentication boundary, and no user-interface boundary — `Project Guide.md` §4 records the implementation as "a console application with no user interface, no hosted page, no bound port and no external integration."
