#### 6.4.1.5 Scope and Verification Environment

Three constraints on the evidence in this sub-section should be stated so its claims can be weighted correctly.

| Constraint | Consequence for this sub-section |
|---|---|
| **No JDK is installed** in the environment used to verify the repository — `java`, `javac`, `javadoc`, `keytool` and `jarsigner` are all absent from `PATH`, `JAVA_HOME` is empty and `/usr/lib/jvm` does not exist | Every runtime security observation quoted here — hostile-argument runs, standard-input and environment probes, class-load counts, filesystem snapshots, unprivileged-account runs and the observed TLS handshake — is attributed to `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` or to the archived specification as **recorded** evidence. None is asserted first-hand, and no keystore or policy experiment could be run |
| **The clone's credential is deliberately not reproduced.** Only its class is recorded: the userinfo username `x-access-token` and a `ghs_`-prefixed token, held in the untracked `.git/config` | This is the one data-handling rule this specification applies to itself, and it matches the archived specification's treatment (Section 6.4.4.4). No push was attempted, so the credential's write capability is **not** asserted here |
| Git and standard POSIX text tooling are present | All repository-state findings — the artifact, source and history censuses, file modes, the signature histogram, configuration keys, object format, `git fsck` integrity and blob-digest reproducibility — were measured directly and are **first-hand** observations |

The one untracked file in the working tree, `tech_spec.md`, is an authoring artifact of the documentation process. It is not tracked, is not a system file, and is excluded from every census and figure above.


### 6.4.2 Authentication Framework

**The application performs no authentication of any kind, and is structurally incapable of it.** There is no credential handling, no identity concept, no session, no token parsing and no `OAuth`, `JWT`, API-key or challenge construct in `Hello.java`. The absence is prior to any configuration choice: because the program reads no input and never dereferences `args`, there is no channel through which a principal could be asserted in the first place. Section 5.4.4 records the same finding from the cross-cutting view, and `Project Guide.md` §1.5, line 49, states the repository-wide position — "no credential, key, network egress, environment variable or secret is used by anything in this project."

Authentication does occur exactly once in the project's lifecycle, and it happens **outside the program, outside the tracked tree, and before or after any run**: the `git` client presents a machine credential to the hosting platform when conveying objects across boundary B-1. That single flow is documented in full below, because it is the only authentication event the system has.

#### 6.4.2.1 Identity Management

No identity store, directory, user registry, account model or provisioning process exists. There is no `IdentityProvider`, no LDAP or SAML configuration, no directory client and — since the repository contains no configuration file of any format — nowhere an identity source could be declared. `Project Guide.md` §1.5, line 55, records the position as a table row: "External services, registries, credentials — Not applicable: no dependency manifest, no network call, no bound port."

Four identities nevertheless exist around the system. Each belongs to a party the repository does not manage, and none is evaluated by any tracked file.

| Identity | Where it is asserted | How it is established |
|---|---|---|
| Commit author and committer | The 14 commit objects in the Git history | **Self-asserted and mostly unverified.** Three commits are authored by `rjhonsi`, ten by `Blitzy Agent` and the merge `2a78292` by `blitzy-qa[bot]`. The signature histogram is 4 commits with status `E` and 10 with status `N` (unsigned), so identity is cryptographically attested for at most four of fourteen (Section 6.4.3.5) |
| Machine identity on the conveyance write path | The userinfo component of `remote.origin.url` in the clone's untracked `.git/config` | A hosting-provider machine token of the `ghs_` class presented with the fixed username `x-access-token`. Evaluated by the platform, never by the repository |
| Operating-system account | The process that runs `javac`, `java` and `git` | Ambient host identity. It governs the POSIX permissions on Z-3 and Z-4 and nothing else; the program requests no privilege and reads no identity |
| Legal identity of the rights holder | Would be the per-file copyright notice the GPL appendix advises | **Not recorded anywhere.** No tracked file names a copyright holder or year, which is precisely why the per-file notice is deferred (ADR-010, requirement F-006-RQ-005) |

The absence of the fourth identity is the only identity-management gap with a consequence inside the repository: Section 2.4.4 records it as an open licensing-compliance item awaiting an owner decision, not a technical vulnerability.

#### 6.4.2.2 Multi-Factor Authentication

**Not applicable, at both layers.** The application has no authentication step to strengthen. On the conveyance path, the credential class in use is a machine token rather than an interactive login, so a second factor has no place in the exchange — and the clone is configured so that an interactive challenge is impossible in any case.

| Dimension | Observed position |
|---|---|
| MFA in the application | Genuinely absent. No login, no principal, no challenge, no enrolment and no recovery path exists or can exist |
| MFA on the conveyance write path | Does not participate. The credential is presented non-interactively as part of the remote URL; `credential.interactive` is set to `false`, `core.askpass` to `echo` and `credential.helper` to the empty value in the clone's local configuration, so no prompt can be raised |
| MFA on the maintainers' platform accounts | Inherited and **not observable from a clone**. Whatever the hosting platform enforces on the human accounts behind commits `c537a19`, `f1847fa` and `0726b1d` is a property of those accounts, is configured by the platform, and is deliberately not asserted here |
| MFA-related artifact in the repository | None. No enrolment record, no recovery code, no authenticator configuration and no policy document exists in any tracked file or in any blob of any commit |

#### 6.4.2.3 Session Management

**No session exists anywhere in the system, in either the application sense or the transport sense.** There is no session identifier, cookie, bearer context, session store, idle timeout, absolute timeout, renewal, fixation defence or logout, because there is nothing that outlives a single operation.

| Session concern | Position at `HEAD` |
|---|---|
| Application session | Genuinely absent. The process lives for the duration of one write: `main` is invoked once, executes one statement and returns, and the JVM then shuts down of its own accord with no `System.exit` call. Nothing is carried between runs because the program declares no field and creates no instance |
| Session store or cache | Genuinely absent. Section 6.2 records that no runtime path reaches durable media, and Section 4.3.1.5 records that no cache of any kind exists |
| Transport session | Inherited and ephemeral. Each `git` invocation opens its own HTTPS connection and closes it; there is no persistent connection, keep-alive tuning or connection pool configured anywhere (Section 6.2.5.3) |
| Timeout, renewal and revocation | Genuinely absent from the repository. No timeout value of any kind is recorded in any tracked file; revocation of the conveyance credential is a platform operation the repository neither performs nor records |
| Concurrency and isolation between sessions | Not applicable, but favourable: each invocation is a separate process with no shared mutable state and no lock, so concurrent runs cannot contend or leak state into one another (Section 6.1.3.5) |

#### 6.4.2.4 Token Handling

Exactly one token exists in the system, it belongs to the clone rather than to the repository, and the program never sees it. No application token — no JWT, OAuth access or refresh token, API key, HMAC signature or nonce — exists anywhere: the fourteen-pattern credential census over every blob of every commit returned no value, and no `eyJ…` or `Bearer …` form occurs in any tracked file.

| Token attribute | Observed value or position |
|---|---|
| Location | The userinfo component of `remote.origin.url` inside the clone's own `.git/config` — a file `git ls-files` confirms is **not tracked**, so it is conveyed by no clone |
| Class | A hosting-provider machine token of the `ghs_` class, presented with the fixed username `x-access-token`. No `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_` or `github_pat_` form is present anywhere. The `ghs_` class is an installation-scoped, short-lived credential class, so the exposure window is inherently bounded |
| Issuance and rotation | Performed entirely by the environment that provisioned this clone. The repository issues nothing, records no rotation interval, and carries no policy on the subject |
| Scope and capability | Not observable from the clone, and **not asserted**. No push was attempted during this verification, so write capability was neither exercised nor confirmed |
| Transmission | Only over the HTTPS conveyance channel of boundary B-1, with server-certificate verification left at the client default (`http.sslVerify` unset) |
| Handling rule in force | Never reproduce the value. This specification records only the username and the class prefix, which is the same treatment the archived specification applies (Section 6.4.4.4) |
| Validation by the system | None. Nothing in the repository parses, verifies, caches or refreshes a token; validation is performed wholly by the hosting platform |

#### 6.4.2.5 Password Policies

**No password exists in this system, so there is no password policy to state — and the only password-related rule in force runs in the opposite direction to a policy.**

| Password concern | Position at `HEAD` |
|---|---|
| Password, passphrase or PIN anywhere in the tracked tree | None. A word-level search across `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE` for `password`, `passphrase`, `secret`, `api_key`, `credential` and `private key` returns exactly **one** hit — `LICENSE` line 340, which is GPL v3 text |
| Password storage, hashing or stretching | Genuinely absent. No `MessageDigest`, `SecureRandom`, `Cipher`, salt, work factor or credential store appears in the source; there is no store in which a credential could be written |
| Password entry | Genuinely absent. No `Console.readPassword`, `Scanner`, `System.in` read or environment read exists, so no secret can be typed into the program even accidentally |
| Interactive credential prompting on the conveyance path | Deliberately disabled: `credential.interactive=false` and `core.askpass=echo` in the clone's local configuration mean no password prompt can be raised for `git` operations |
| The one rule that does apply | GPL v3 §6 at `LICENSE` line 340 requires that Corresponding Source conveyed with an object-code form "must require no special password or key for" unpacking, reading or copying. The only password-related obligation in the entire project therefore **forbids** password-gating the conveyed source rather than mandating a password policy |
| Complexity, expiry, reuse and lockout rules | Not applicable. No authenticator exists to which such rules could attach, and no tracked file records one |

#### 6.4.2.6 Authentication Flow

The flow below is the complete authentication picture for the system. Two of its three paths contain no authentication step at all, and the third is executed by the `git` client on behalf of an operator — never by the program.

**Figure 6.4.2-A — The complete authentication flow: an unauthenticated launch path, an anonymous read path, and the single token-bearing write path at boundary B-1**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Op as Operator shell (Z-2)
    participant Gitc as git client (Z-2)
    participant Hub as Hosting platform (Z-1)
    participant Tool as JDK toolchain (Z-2)
    participant Proc as Hello.main (Z-5)

    Note over Op,Hub: Path 1 — conveyance read. Recorded as anonymous: no credential is required to obtain the source.
    Op->>Gitc: git clone / git fetch
    Gitc->>Hub: HTTPS request, server certificate verified at client default
    Hub-->>Gitc: 5 blobs, 14 commits, 13 trees, 8 refs, 0 tags
    Note right of Hub: Public read recorded in the archived specification.<br/>The tracked tree conveys no credential of any kind.

    Note over Op,Hub: Path 2 — conveyance write. The only authentication event in the whole project.
    Op->>Gitc: git push (branch jr_java1)
    Gitc->>Gitc: Read userinfo from the clone's untracked .git/config
    Note right of Gitc: Username x-access-token plus a ghs_-class machine token.<br/>credential.interactive=false and core.askpass=echo,<br/>so no interactive challenge is possible.
    Gitc->>Hub: Present machine identity over the HTTPS channel
    Hub-->>Gitc: Platform-side authorization decision (Section 6.4.3.3)
    Note over Hub: Evaluated wholly by the platform. The repository defines<br/>no account, role or permission of its own.

    Note over Op,Proc: Path 3 — build and launch. No authentication step exists anywhere on this path.
    Op->>Tool: javac -d "$B" Hello.java, then java -cp "$B" Hello
    Tool->>Proc: Resolve the bare name Hello and invoke main once
    Note right of Proc: No principal is asserted: args is accepted and never<br/>dereferenced, stdin is never read, no environment<br/>variable is consulted and no class is signature-checked.
    Proc-->>Op: Greeting on fd 1, fd 2 empty, wait status 0
```

Two properties of this flow bound the system's entire authentication surface. First, **the authenticated path and the executed path never meet**: the credential is used by a different tool, in a different lifecycle phase, against a different party, and Section 3.4.2 records the program's runtime coupling to the hosting platform as *none*. Second, **the launch path is unauthenticated by construction, not by omission** — with no input channel and no class-signature check, there is no step at which an identity could be introduced without first adding a surface the system does not have. Section 5.4.4 states the architectural consequence: introducing a first input would also introduce the project's first authentication question.


### 6.4.3 Authorization System

**No authorization system exists at any layer of the application.** There is no role, permission, scope, claim, group, policy document or access-control list in the repository, because there is no protected operation to gate and no principal to evaluate. Section 6.3.2.3 reaches the same conclusion for the interface layer and Section 6.2.4.5 for the data layer; Section 5.1.1.3 records that the system has no trust or authentication boundary at all.

What operates instead is a set of **inherited, non-application authorization mechanisms**: the operating system's discretionary access control over files, Git's mode field and content addressing, the hosting platform's ref-update rules, and the GPL v3 grant. All four are documented below, together with the one authorization-relevant mechanism the repository actually selects for itself.

#### 6.4.3.1 Role-Based Access Control

**Genuinely absent.** No role is defined, assumed or referenced anywhere in the tracked tree. There is no role enumeration, no role assignment, no group membership, no scope string, no claim set and no privilege hierarchy — and no configuration file of any format in which one could be declared. Section 3.4.2 records the repository-level position: it "defines no roles, accounts or permissions of its own."

Three coarse subject classes exist around the system, and it is worth naming them so they are not mistaken for roles:

| Subject class | What it can do | Why it is not a role |
|---|---|---|
| Anyone who can reach the hosting platform | Read the source: clone, fetch and view refs and files | Anonymous read was recorded as succeeding without credentials, so this class has no membership to assign and no identity to bind a role to |
| Whoever holds a write-capable credential on the remote | Update refs on the remote, and merge pull requests — the facility visible as `HEAD` = `2a78292`, "Merge pull request #1" | Membership is determined entirely by the platform. No tracked file names a principal, grants a right or records an approval requirement; `CODEOWNERS` is absent |
| The host account that runs the commands | Read the checkout, compile, launch, and write into its own scratch directory | This is POSIX file ownership, not a role: the three POSIX permission classes (owner, group, other) are properties of each inode, not assignable roles in an access model |

#### 6.4.3.2 Permission Management

Permissions in this system are entirely filesystem and Git permissions, and they are managed by convention and umask rather than by any configured policy. Every value below was measured in the checkout.

| Permission surface | Observed state | How it is managed |
|---|---|---|
| Tracked files on disk | All five files mode `644` (`-rw-r--r--`); no setuid, setgid or executable regular file exists anywhere in the worktree | Ambient umask `0022` at checkout time. No `core.fileMode` override is needed and the setting is left at `true` |
| Directories on disk | Root, `blitzy/` and `blitzy/documentation/` at mode `2755` | Created by the clone under the same umask; no special handling is configured or required |
| Git index mode field | All five entries `100644` — no `100755` executable bit, no `120000` symlink and no `160000` gitlink or submodule | Git's own mode field, the only permission datum the repository actually conveys to a consumer. A clone therefore cannot deliver an executable or a symlink |
| Build-output destination | Mode `2700` — owner-only access, verified here by creating a directory with `mktemp -d` under umask `0022` | **The one selected mechanism** (ADR-009). `README.md` line 30 states the reason beside the command |
| Ignore and exclusion rules | `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes` are absent; `.git/info/exclude` exists at 240 bytes with **zero** active patterns, and `git check-ignore -v Hello.class` matches no rule | Unmanaged by design. Section 2.4.1 records that build output is kept out of the tree by command discipline alone |
| Git hooks | `.git/hooks` holds 14 files, **all** `*.sample`; no active hook exists and `core.hooksPath` is unset | No local code executes on commit, push or checkout, so the clone grants the repository no implicit execution privilege |

#### 6.4.3.3 Resource Authorization

Five resources in the project can be acted upon. For each, the decision is made by a party outside the program, and in three of the five cases the decision is not a security decision at all.

| Resource | Who authorises access | Mechanism and observed state |
|---|---|---|
| The five tracked files in the checkout (Z-3) | The operating system, on behalf of the file owner | POSIX discretionary access control at mode `644`. `javac` needs read permission and nothing more; nothing in the tree is executable |
| The per-run build destination (Z-4) | The operating system, on behalf of the creating account | The `mktemp -d` directory at mode `2700`. This is the only place the documented workflows write, and it is deliberately outside the checkout — a fixed, predictable destination "can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it" (`README.md` line 30) |
| Standard output (boundary B-5) | The launching shell, before the process starts | The descriptor is **inherited, not opened**: whether the greeting reaches a terminal, a pipe or a file is decided outside the system boundary. The program performs no check and has no say |
| The Git object store and refs | Locally the filesystem; remotely the hosting platform | Locally, ordinary file permissions plus Git's content addressing — SHA-1 object format, `git fsck` clean with exit 0, and re-hashing `Hello.java` reproduces blob `3fd76ce8…` exactly. Remotely, ref-update rules the platform owns; 8 refs currently sit at 3 distinct commits, with `main` 11 commits behind `jr_java1` |
| The covered work itself | The GPL v3 instrument in `LICENSE` — 674 lines, 35,149 bytes | A **legal** authorization control that grants rather than restricts: it authorises any recipient to run, study, modify and redistribute on stated terms. It is the only authorization control the repository itself carries, and it is enforced by licence rather than by code |

#### 6.4.3.4 Policy Enforcement Points

Six enforcement points act on this system. Not one of them is inside the program, and the JVM's own enforcement point is not merely unused — on the toolchain the repository records as used, it cannot exist.

| Enforcement point | Where it acts | What it decides |
|---|---|---|
| **PEP-1 Kernel discretionary access control** | Every file open on the operator host | Whether `javac` may read the compilation unit and whether the compiler may write its output. The only enforcement point exercised on every documented workflow |
| **PEP-2 Scratch-directory creation** | `mktemp -d`, at build time | Creates the destination with owner-only permissions and an unpredictable name, denying other local accounts both discovery and pre-creation. The system's one **selected** control |
| **PEP-3 JVM class resolution** | The `java` launcher, at boundary B-4 | Resolves the bare name `Hello` on the classpath. This is a *resolution* decision, not a security decision: there is no code-signature verification, no sealed package, no module boundary and no signed jar — `jarsigner` and `keytool` play no part in any documented workflow |
| **PEP-4 Git object integrity** | Every read from the object store | Rejects content that does not hash to its address. Enforces integrity, never access: `git fsck` exits 0 with no error, but the store grants no confidentiality |
| **PEP-5 Platform ref-update authorization** | The hosting remote, at boundary B-1 | Whether a presented identity may advance a ref or merge a pull request. Entirely outside the boundary; not configured by any tracked file, and branch protection is not observable from a clone so none is asserted |
| **PEP-6 The GPL v3 instrument** | Redistribution of the covered work | Whether a downstream act of conveyance is permitted, and on what terms. Enforced in law rather than in code, with the operative clauses anchored in Section 6.4.5.4 |

**The JVM's in-process enforcement point is permanently unavailable on the recorded toolchain.** `Project Guide.md` Appendix D, line 442, records the toolchain actually used as OpenJDK **25.0.3**. From JDK 24 onward the Security Manager is permanently disabled: it cannot be enabled at startup — any `-Djava.security.manager` form is a hard VM-initialisation error that cannot be suppressed or reduced to a warning — nor installed at run time, Security-Manager-specific system and security properties are ignored, and the system policy file `$JAVA_HOME/conf/security/java.policy` has been removed. On that runtime there is therefore no permission model, no `Policy`, no `ProtectionDomain` and no `AccessController` check available even in principle, which is consistent with the source census: the repository references none of those APIs and contains no policy file. Because the repository pins no Java version (ADR-007), an operator on JDK 17–23 could still enable a Security Manager — but nothing in the tracked tree would configure one, so the observable position is unchanged.

Five enforcement points a reviewer might look for are absent, each for a structural reason:

- **No request-path enforcement.** There is no middleware, filter, interceptor, guard or annotation, because there is no request — Section 6.3.2.4 records that work is initiated by an operator rather than arriving.
- **No edge enforcement.** Section 6.3.4.3 records that every gateway, reverse-proxy and ingress descriptor probed is absent, so there is no place to attach an auth plugin, a CORS policy or a rate-limit rule.
- **No admission control.** No container, orchestration or IaC manifest exists anywhere in the history, so there is no admission controller, pod security policy or security group.
- **No pipeline gate.** No CI descriptor has ever been tracked. The project's only automated gate is `javac -Xlint:all -Werror`, which `Project Guide.md` Appendix F names as "the project's static-analysis surface, as no linter is configured" — a code-quality gate, not a security policy, and one that nothing re-runs (ADR-002).
- **No commit-time gate.** All 14 `.git/hooks` entries are `*.sample`, commit signing is unconfigured (`commit.gpgsign`, `tag.gpgsign`, `user.signingkey` and `gpg.format` all unset), and no `CODEOWNERS` or `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists.

**Figure 6.4.3-A — Authorization flow: which enforcement point decides, for each action the project supports, and the enforcement machinery verified absent**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Actor(["An action is attempted<br/>by an operator, a tool or a consumer"])
    Route{"What is the action<br/>performed against?"}

    subgraph HostEnforcement["Host enforcement — PEP-1 and PEP-2, exercised on every workflow"]
        FileCheck{"Does the account hold the<br/>POSIX right on the inode?"}
        ReadOK["Read granted: javac consumes<br/>one 1,073-byte compilation unit"]
        WriteTarget["Write target chosen by -d:<br/>mktemp -d directory, mode 2700, owner-only"]
        DeniedHost["Denied by the kernel;<br/>the workflow stops with a diagnostic"]
        FileCheck -->|"yes"| ReadOK
        FileCheck -->|"yes, into Z-4"| WriteTarget
        FileCheck -->|"no"| DeniedHost
    end

    subgraph RuntimeEnforcement["Runtime — PEP-3: resolution only, no security decision"]
        Resolve{"Is the bare name Hello<br/>resolvable on the classpath?"}
        Invoke["main invoked once; args accepted<br/>and never dereferenced"]
        NotFound["Launch fails before entry — fault E-1;<br/>no partial execution occurs"]
        Resolve -->|"yes"| Invoke
        Resolve -->|"no"| NotFound
    end

    subgraph StoreEnforcement["Git enforcement — PEP-4: integrity, never confidentiality"]

        Corrupt["Rejected as corrupt;<br/>re-clone from any complete replica"]
        HashCheck -->|"yes"| Served
        HashCheck -->|"no"| Corrupt
    end

    subgraph PlatformEnforcement["Platform enforcement — PEP-5, outside the system boundary"]

        RefNo["Rejected by the platform;<br/>no tracked file configures this rule"]
        RefCheck -->|"platform decides"| RefOK
        RefCheck -->|"platform decides"| RefNo
    end

    subgraph LegalEnforcement["Legal enforcement — PEP-6, enforced in law rather than in code"]
        Convey{"Is the act a conveyance<br/>of the covered work?"}
        GrantOK["Permitted on GPL v3 terms:<br/>notices kept, source offered, no further restriction"]
        Terminate["Rights terminate under section 8<br/>until reinstated as that section provides"]
        Convey -->|"terms met"| GrantOK
        Convey -->|"terms breached"| Terminate
    end

    subgraph AbsentEnforcement["Verified absent — no authorization machinery of any kind"]
        NoRbac["No role, scope, claim, group,<br/>ACL or policy document"]
        NoSm["No Security Manager, policy file,<br/>Permission or AccessController check"]
        NoMw["No middleware, filter, interceptor,<br/>guard or gateway auth plugin"]
        NoGate["No CI gate, commit hook, CODEOWNERS<br/>or signing requirement"]
        NoRbac --- NoSm
        NoSm --- NoMw
        NoMw --- NoGate
    end

    Actor --> Route
    Route -->|"a file in the checkout or the build destination"| FileCheck
    Route -->|"launching the program"| Resolve
    Route -->|"an object or ref in the local store"| HashCheck
    Route -->|"a ref on the hosting remote"| RefCheck
    Route -->|"redistributing the work"| Convey
    Invoke -->|"one write to fd 1; no authorization consulted"| Output(["Greeting emitted, fd 2 empty, status 0"])
```

#### 6.4.3.5 Audit Logging

**The application emits no audit record, and no run leaves evidence of itself.** There is no logging framework, no `java.util.logging`, SLF4J or Log4j reference, no audit sink, no correlation identifier and no security event of any kind — the source declares zero imports, and Section 5.4.2 records the single write as "the program's product, not its log." Section 5.3.4 names the accepted tradeoff directly: no run leaves evidence of itself.

The audit trail that does exist is the Git history, and its properties were measured rather than assumed.

| Audit property | Observed state at `HEAD` |
|---|---|
| Event record | 14 commit objects, each carrying author and committer identity with an ISO-8601 timestamp. Three by `rjhonsi` on 2026-09-16, ten by `Blitzy Agent` on 2026-09-16/17, and the merge `2a78292` by `blitzy-qa[bot]` on 2026-09-22 |
| Integrity of the record | Content addressing over SHA-1 objects, verified: `git fsck` exits 0 with no error and re-hashing a tracked file reproduces its stored blob id. Commits are append-only; Section 6.2.3.1 records that no in-place migration step exists |
| Authenticity of the record | **Partial and unenforced.** The signature histogram is 4 commits with status `E` and 10 with status `N` — ten of fourteen commits are unsigned, and no signing configuration exists in the clone. Identity for those ten is therefore self-asserted |
| Replication and durability | Every clone is a complete replica of the trail, and the remote is one replica among them (Section 6.1.4.3). No retention policy exists: no `gc.*` or `pack.*` configuration is set, so Git defaults govern pruning |
| Local, non-conveyed journal | `core.logallrefupdates` is `true` and `.git/logs/HEAD` records ref movements, but the reflog is untracked and conveyed by no clone |
| Run-time audit of executions | **None.** Nothing records that a run occurred: no log file, no exit-status record, no metric and no trace. Section 5.4.1 lists the complete set of observables, all of which are transient stream contents |
| Durable record of verification | `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §3 and §4 — 49 of 49 checks, written by hand. Section 5.4.2 states the consequence: "auditability is documentary, not automatic," and Section 5.4.6 records this prose as the one asset in the system with no mechanical recovery path |

Four audit capabilities that a maintained project would be expected to have are absent, and all four are carried into the residual-risk register in Section 6.4.5.3: there is no tamper-evident log outside the object store, no review or approval record inside the repository (no `CODEOWNERS`, no required-review artifact observable from a clone), no automated audit of changes (nothing re-runs the checks, per ADR-002), and no enforced commit signing — `Project Guide.md` §1.4 records commit-signing infrastructure as deferred and an owner decision.


### 6.4.4 Data Protection

**There is no sensitive datum inside the system to protect.** The program's entire data domain is one public compile-time string constant and one host-supplied line separator; it reads nothing, derives nothing and stores nothing. `Project Guide.md` §6, line 188, records the consequence as a category that does not arise — "no data-at-rest concern" — and Section 6.2 records that no runtime path reaches durable media.

One genuinely sensitive datum does exist in the vicinity of the system, and it is deliberately outside the tracked tree: the machine token in the clone's own `.git/config`. Data protection in this system is therefore almost entirely a statement about inventory and about the two channels that carry bytes anywhere — conveyance and standard output.

#### 6.4.4.1 Data Classification and Inventory

| Datum | Classification | Protection in force |
|---|---|---|
| **D-1** The greeting literal — 16 ASCII characters | Public. Republished verbatim as an operator-facing oracle at `README.md` lines 59–61 | None required. It is a compile-time constant with no interpolation, so there is no format-string or output-injection vector (Section 2.4.4, F-002) |
| **D-2** The platform line separator appended by `println` | Public, host-derived | None required. `README.md` line 63 records that the exact byte count varies by platform while the literal and its single trailing separator do not |
| **D-3** The tracked bytes — 925,008 in five files, of which 1,073 are source and 884,733 are the two documents under `blitzy/documentation/` | Public. Anonymous read of the remote was recorded as succeeding without credentials | Integrity only: SHA-1 content addressing, `git fsck` clean, blob digests reproducible. No confidentiality control exists or is wanted |
| **D-4** The build artifact `Hello.class` — 420 bytes, `main` compiled to four bytecode instructions | Derived and disposable. Zero `.class` blobs have ever been tracked in the 14-commit history | Written only into the owner-only Z-4 directory under the selected mechanism, and removed afterwards. `README.md` line 30: "Do not commit the class file either way" |
| **D-5** The `ghs_`-class machine token presented on the conveyance write path | **Sensitive — the only sensitive datum in the system** | Held in the clone's untracked `.git/config`, so it is conveyed by no clone and appears in no blob of any commit. Transmitted only over the HTTPS channel of boundary B-1 |
| **D-6** Contributor identity metadata in the 14 commit objects — author and committer identity with authored and commit timestamps | Public and **permanent**. Append-only and replicated by every clone | None, and none is possible after the fact. Section 6.2.4 records contributor-identity permanence as one of only two real data-compliance findings in the project |

No personal, payment, health, biometric, location or customer datum is read, derived, stored or transmitted by anything in this system. There is no data subject, no cardholder, no patient record and no user account anywhere in the inventory.

#### 6.4.4.2 Encryption Standards

**The repository implements no cryptography and specifies no cryptographic standard.** The source census found no `javax.crypto`, `java.security`, `Cipher`, `MessageDigest`, `SecureRandom`, `KeyStore`, `SSLContext` or `Base64` reference; the program performs no hashing, signing, encryption, decryption or random generation. No cipher suite, TLS version, certificate, truststore or algorithm choice is configured in any tracked file.

Three cryptographic mechanisms are nevertheless in force, all of them inherited and none of them selected by the repository.

| Mechanism | Purpose it serves here | Observed state |
|---|---|---|
| Git content addressing | Integrity and tamper evidence, not confidentiality | The repository uses Git's default **SHA-1** object format (`git rev-parse --show-object-format`); no SHA-256 object format is configured. `git fsck` exits 0 with no error, and re-hashing `Hello.java` reproduces blob `3fd76ce8…` exactly |
| TLS on the conveyance channel | Confidentiality and server authentication for boundary B-1 | `http.sslVerify` is unset, so certificate verification is at the Git client default. A TLS 1.3 handshake with `ECDHE_RSA_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` and `server certificate verification OK` against subject `CN=github.com` is **recorded** in the archived specification; it was not re-probed here and is not asserted first-hand |
| Commit signatures | Provenance for part of the history | 4 of 14 commits carry a signature (status `E` — present but not verifiable in this environment); the remaining 10 are unsigned. The archived specification records the platform's published web-flow RSA signing key `B5690EEEBB952194` for the earliest commits. Signing is **not** enforced: `commit.gpgsign`, `tag.gpgsign`, `user.signingkey` and `gpg.format` are all unset |

**Encryption at rest is not applicable and is not configured.** All five tracked files are stored as plain text — `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE` are pure 7-bit ASCII, and the two documents under `blitzy/documentation/` are UTF-8 — and Section 3.5.6 records data-at-rest encryption and masking as not applicable because no store exists. Whatever full-disk or volume encryption the operator's host provides is outside the system boundary and is neither required nor recorded.

#### 6.4.4.3 Key Management

**No key management exists, because the repository holds no key.** The recursive search over seventeen key-material filename patterns returned zero files; there is no keystore, truststore, certificate, private key, public key, symmetric key, key-derivation parameter, KMS reference, HSM reference or rotation schedule anywhere in the checkout or in any blob of any commit.

| Key-management concern | Position at `HEAD` |
|---|---|
| Application keys | Genuinely absent. Nothing in the program generates, derives, stores, loads, uses or destroys key material |
| Java keystores and signing tooling | Not used. No `*.jks`, `*.p12` or `*.keystore` file exists, and neither `keytool` nor `jarsigner` appears in any documented workflow — the distribution is source-only, so there is no signed jar to verify (Section 3.6.6) |
| The conveyance credential | Managed entirely by the environment that provisioned the clone. Its class (`ghs_`) is short-lived by construction, which bounds the exposure window, but the repository records no issuance, rotation, expiry or revocation procedure and performs none |
| Commit-signing keys | Managed and published by the hosting platform for its web-flow key; no contributor signing key is configured in this clone, and `.allowed_signers` and `.gitsigners` are absent |
| Transport keys and certificates | Supplied and validated by the Git client and the platform. The repository pins no certificate, configures no truststore and disables no verification |
| Key policy documentation | None. No tracked file states a key-strength, algorithm-agility, escrow or recovery requirement, and none is asserted here |

#### 6.4.4.4 Data Masking Rules

**No data masking is implemented, and no datum in the system requires it.** There is no redaction routine, tokenisation step, pseudonymisation rule, truncation rule or field-level mask — and nowhere for one to act, since the program's output is a fixed constant and there is no log, no store and no response payload.

Two masking-like rules are nevertheless genuinely in force, and both are worth recording because they are the reason no sensitive value appears in the tracked tree or in this document.

| Rule in force | Scope | How it is enforced |
|---|---|---|
| Credential values are never reproduced in documentation | The `ghs_`-class token in the untracked `.git/config` | By authoring discipline, and observably: the archived specification names only the pattern classes `ghp_`, `github_pat_` and `ghs_` without a value, and this specification records only the username `x-access-token` and the class prefix. The fourteen-pattern census over every blob of every commit confirms no value has ever been committed |
| The output channel cannot disclose internal state | Standard output and standard error | Structurally: the payload is a compile-time constant with no interpolation, standard error stays empty on every run, and there is no error path that could surface a stack trace, a path or an environment value (Section 2.4.4, F-002 and F-003) |

One masking-adjacent control is **absent and expected**: nothing prevents a sensitive value from entering the immutable store in future. Section 3.5.6 records the position as "Sensitive content entering the immutable store — Unguarded," because there is no `.gitignore`, no active pattern in `.git/info/exclude`, no secret-scanning configuration and no pre-commit hook. The store is clean today by measurement, not by control; the risk is carried in Section 6.4.5.3.

#### 6.4.4.5 Secure Communication

**The program communicates over no network, so it has no transport security posture of its own.** `Project Guide.md` Appendix B, line 426, records that it "binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call," and Section 6.3.1.2 records that a URI-scheme census over every tracked file found no `http`, `https`, `ws`, `jdbc`, `amqp`, `redis` or `mongodb` endpoint anywhere — the only four URLs in the tracked tree are licence-text references in `LICENSE` at lines 4, 648, 667 and 674, none of which any tracked file resolves.

| Channel | Security properties | Configuration observed |
|---|---|---|
| Git conveyance (B-1) — the only network channel in the system | Encrypted and server-authenticated: HTTPS with certificate verification at the client default. This is also the only channel that ever carries the credential | `remote.origin.url` uses the `https` scheme; `http.sslVerify` is unset; no `url.insteadOf` rewrite is configured; no `.netrc` exists. No `ssh://` or `git://` remote is configured anywhere |
| Process standard streams (B-5) | Unencrypted by nature and appropriately so: the payload is public, the descriptor is inherited from the parent, and the write is fire-and-forget with no reply channel | Nothing to configure. The destination — terminal, pipe or redirect — is chosen outside the system boundary |
| Compilation and launch (B-2, B-4) | Local, offline and air-gapped-capable: zero dependency resolution and zero network egress, so no channel can be intercepted or poisoned at build time | `README.md` line 18: "nothing has to be resolved or downloaded before building." Section 3.6.2.1 records zero network egress for both build paths |

Two consequences follow. First, **every documented workflow after the clone runs entirely offline**, so the system's exposure to network attack is confined to the moments a human runs `git`. Second, because no listener exists anywhere, there is no TLS termination point, no cipher-suite selection, no certificate lifecycle and no mutual-TLS question in this system — Section 6.3.4.3 records the same finding from the gateway perspective.

#### 6.4.4.6 Compliance Controls

The data-protection controls that bear on compliance are few enough to state exhaustively; the full obligation set, with clause-level anchors into `LICENSE`, is tabulated in Section 6.4.5.4.

| Control area | Position at `HEAD` |
|---|---|
| Licence compliance | The one live compliance regime in the project. GPL v3 is carried verbatim (674 lines, unchanged since commit `c537a19`), referenced at `README.md` line 77, and accompanied by the dated modification notice at `README.md` line 5 that §5 of the licence requires. One known gap: no per-file copyright and warranty notice, because no tracked file records a rights holder or year (ADR-010, F-006-RQ-005) |
| Privacy and data-protection regulation | No obligation is recorded in any tracked file, and the data inventory in Section 6.4.4.1 contains no personal datum the program collects, processes or stores. The only personal-adjacent data in the project is the permanent contributor identity metadata in the commit objects, which Section 6.2.4 records as irreversible by construction |
| Data retention and deletion | No retention rule, deletion procedure or expiry policy exists. The Git store is append-only and no `gc.*` or `pack.*` configuration is set, so five superseded blob revisions are retained indefinitely under Git defaults (Section 6.2.3.3) |
| Records of processing, DPIA, DPA | None exist and none is referenced. There is no processing activity to record: no input is read and nothing is stored |
| Export-control and cryptography notices | Not applicable in substance — the repository ships no cryptographic implementation, so there is no encryption functionality to declare |
| Audit evidence for a compliance review | Documentary rather than automatic: the object store supplies an attributable, append-only change history, and `Project Guide.md` §3–§5 supplies the verification and compliance record. Section 6.4.5.5 enumerates exactly what an auditor could obtain and what they could not |


### 6.4.5 Security Control Matrix and Compliance Requirements

This sub-section consolidates the position: what can be attacked, which controls are in force and by whom they are supplied, which risks are carried rather than mitigated, and which compliance obligations actually bind the project.

#### 6.4.5.1 Attack Surface Inventory

The attack surface is unusually small, and the reason is structural rather than defensive: nothing in the program reads anything. Static findings below were measured here; runtime findings are attributed to the repository's own records, because no JDK exists in this verification environment.

| Channel | Reachability | Observed result |
|---|---|---|
| Command-line arguments | Delivered by the launcher, never dereferenced | `args` appears only in the Javadoc at line 11 and the signature at line 15. `Project Guide.md` §4 records that "no arguments, many arguments, and hostile arguments including shell and injection payloads all produce identical output"; the archived specification adds the specific vectors — a shell command separator, command substitution, backticks, `../../../etc/passwd`, `%s%n%s`, a script tag, `' OR 1=1 --`, `{{7*7}}` and NUL bytes — all byte-identical, exit 0, sentinel path never created |
| Standard input | Open at invocation, never read | No `System.in`, `Scanner` or `BufferedReader` reference exists. A piped payload containing a sentinel secret produced identical output with zero sentinel occurrences in either stream (recorded) |
| Environment variables | Present, never consulted | No `System.getenv` or `System.getProperty` reference. `Project Guide.md` Appendix E records that `JAVA_HOME` is not required and "No other variable and no secret is read by any tracked file"; a run under `env -i` with planted credential-shaped values produced identical output (recorded) |
| Configuration and policy files | None exist | Zero configuration files of any format anywhere in the checkout, and none has ever been added on any branch |
| Network — inbound and outbound | None | No port, listener, socket, HTTP client or URI in any tracked file; every documented workflow runs offline after clone |
| Deserialisation, reflection and dynamic loading | Not present | Zero references to `Serializable`, `ObjectInputStream`, `readObject`, `Class.forName`, `setAccessible` or `Method.invoke`. Exactly one class is loaded from the application classpath out of 479 total loads, with no agent, plug-in or service loader (recorded) |
| Native code and process spawning | Not present | No `native` declaration, no JNI reference, and zero matches for `ProcessBuilder` or `Runtime.exec` |
| Filesystem writes by the program | None | The only sink is file descriptor 1. Working-directory, isolated `HOME` and isolated `java.io.tmpdir` snapshots were identical before and after runs, and the program runs unchanged from a mode-555 directory (recorded) |
| Build-time dependency resolution | None | No manifest of any kind exists, so no registry, mirror, lockfile or plug-in participates — there is no dependency-confusion or typosquatting surface |
| Build-time code execution from the repository | None | All 14 `.git/hooks` entries are `*.sample`, `core.hooksPath` is unset, and no wrapper script, `Makefile` or CI descriptor exists |
| Build output destination | The one real local surface | A fixed, predictable destination can be pre-created, replaced or symlink-redirected by another local process; the documented command removes the predictability with `mktemp -d`, verified here to produce a mode `2700` owner-only directory against a world-writable `/tmp` at mode `2777` |
| Distribution channel | Public read, token-gated write | Anonymous read recorded as succeeding; write presents the `ghs_`-class machine token. Consumers pinning a commit SHA obtain content-addressed integrity; consumers tracking a branch inherit whatever the tip becomes, and there are zero tags to pin instead |
| Execution privileges | Ambient, unprivileged | No setuid, setgid or executable regular file exists anywhere in the worktree; the program requests no privilege and runs to completion as an unprivileged account (recorded) |

#### 6.4.5.2 Security Control Matrix

Status values carry precise meanings: **Selected** — the repository chose the mechanism and states the reason; **Inherited** — in force, but supplied by the host, the JVM, the platform or the licence rather than by repository code; **Not applicable** — no corresponding surface exists; **Absent and expected** — a control a maintained project would reasonably carry, and it is missing.

| ID | Control domain | Mechanism observed | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SC-01 | Authentication of application users | None; no input channel through which identity could be asserted | Not applicable |
| SC-02 | Authorization and access model in the application | None; no protected operation and no principal to evaluate | Not applicable |
| SC-03 | Session management | None; the process lives for one write and keeps no state | Not applicable |
| SC-04 | Input validation and output encoding | Attack-surface elimination: `args` never dereferenced, no stdin, no environment read, and a constant output literal with no interpolation | Selected — ADR-006 |
| SC-05 | Secret and credential management | No secret in the tracked tree; the one machine token lives in the untracked `.git/config` and is of a short-lived class | Inherited |
| SC-06 | Interactive credential prompting suppressed | `credential.interactive=false`, `core.askpass=echo` and an empty `credential.helper` in the clone | Inherited |
| SC-07 | Encryption in transit | HTTPS on the only network channel, with certificate verification at the Git client default (`http.sslVerify` unset) | Inherited |
| SC-08 | Encryption at rest | None; no store exists and all tracked bytes are plain text | Not applicable |
| SC-09 | Key management | No key material in the repository; platform-managed signing key and environment-managed token | Inherited |
| SC-10 | Artifact and content integrity | SHA-1 content addressing; `git fsck` exit 0 with no error; blob digest reproducible from the working file | Inherited |
| SC-11 | Commit provenance and signing | 4 of 14 commits signed (status `E`), 10 unsigned; no signing configuration in the clone | Absent and expected |
| SC-12 | Filesystem least privilege | Files mode `644`, directories `2755`, umask `0022`, no setuid/setgid/executable file, no symlink, no submodule | Inherited |
| SC-13 | Build-output isolation | `B="$(mktemp -d)" && javac -d "$B" Hello.java`, producing a uniquely named mode `2700` directory outside the checkout | Selected — ADR-009 |
| SC-14 | Build-output containment in version control | No `.gitignore`, no active `.git/info/exclude` pattern; the control is the documented instruction "Do not commit the class file either way" | Absent and expected |
| SC-15 | Static analysis | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` — recorded clean, and named as the project's entire static-analysis surface because no linter is configured | Selected — ADR-002 |
| SC-16 | Supply-chain control | Zero dependencies, zero imports beyond `java.lang`, no manifest, no lock file, nothing downloaded at build time | Selected — ADR-003 |
| SC-17 | SBOM and dependency scanning | No SBOM, no `dependabot.yml`, no `.snyk`, `.semgrep.yml`, `.trivyignore` or `sonar-project.properties` | Absent and expected (no dependency to scan) |
| SC-18 | Toolchain and runtime patch management | Unpinned, host-supplied JDK; versions recorded, never enforced | Absent and expected — ADR-007 |
| SC-19 | Secret scanning and pre-commit control | None; no `.gitleaks.toml`, `.secrets.baseline` or `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and no active hook | Absent and expected |
| SC-20 | Code review and ownership gate | None expressed in the repository; `CODEOWNERS` absent and branch protection not observable from a clone | Absent and expected |
| SC-21 | Audit trail of changes | 14 commit objects with author identity and timestamps in an append-only, content-addressed, fully replicated store | Inherited |
| SC-22 | Audit trail of executions and application logging | None; no logger, no log sink, and no run leaves evidence of itself | Not applicable |
| SC-23 | Monitoring, alerting and incident detection | None; no metrics endpoint, health probe, agent, dashboard or alerting rule exists (Section 5.4.1) | Absent and expected |
| SC-24 | Vulnerability disclosure path | None; no `SECURITY.md`, no `.well-known/security.txt` and no contact address in any tracked file | Absent and expected |
| SC-25 | Network perimeter controls — firewall, WAF, rate limiting | None, and no admission point at which any could act (Sections 6.3.2.4, 6.3.4.3) | Not applicable |
| SC-26 | In-JVM sandbox and policy enforcement | None; permanently unavailable on the recorded OpenJDK 25.0.3 toolchain, and no policy file exists in the repository | Not applicable |
| SC-27 | Container, orchestration and host hardening | None; no `Dockerfile`, compose file, Kubernetes manifest or IaC has ever been tracked | Not applicable |
| SC-28 | Licence and redistribution control | Verbatim GPL v3 at the root, referenced from the guide, with a dated modification notice | Selected — ADR-010 |

#### 6.4.5.3 Residual Risks and Compensating Controls

Each risk below is carried rather than eliminated. Severity and probability are quoted as the repository itself records them in `Project Guide.md` §6 where a rating exists; where no rating exists, none is invented.

| Residual risk | Recorded rating and status | Compensating control in force |
|---|---|---|
| A future edit reintroduces a fixed, predictable compiler-output path, restoring the local pre-creation and symlink exposure | Security; Low severity, Low probability; **Mitigated** | The threat rationale is written beside the command at `README.md` line 30, where the next editor will see it. The control is documentary, not enforced (Section 5.3.6) |
| With no ignore rule, an in-place compile leaves an untracked class file that can be committed by accident, ending source-only distribution | Operational; Low severity, Medium probability; **Open** | The documented `mktemp -d` build path and the instruction "Do not commit the class file either way"; `git status --short` is part of the documented verification routine |
| A sensitive value could enter the immutable, append-only store in future and could not be removed from history | Not rated in the repository; Section 3.5.6 records the position as "Unguarded" | Measurement only: the fourteen-pattern census confirms the store is clean today. No secret scanning, ignore rule or pre-commit hook exists to keep it so |
| Ten of fourteen commits are unsigned, so authorship for most of the history is self-asserted | `Project Guide.md` §1.4 records commit-signing infrastructure as **Deferred**, an owner decision | Content addressing still makes tampering detectable, and 4 commits carry a platform signature. Nothing prevents a forged author identity on a new commit |
| The JDK is host-supplied and unpinned, so runtime CVE exposure is entirely a property of the operator's build | Technical; Low severity, Low probability; **Open** | None inside the repository. Section 5.3.6 records the exposure as accepted in exchange for compiling on any JDK; `Project Guide.md` Appendix D records the version used without enforcing it |
| No automated gate exists, so no security or quality check is re-run on future changes | Operational; Medium severity, Medium probability; **Open** | Manual re-run of `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` after any source edit, as Section 2.4.5 requires. The 49 recorded checks are a point-in-time observation |
| No vulnerability-disclosure path exists, so a finder has no documented channel | Not rated in the repository | None. The hosting platform's own issue and advisory facilities are outside the boundary and are not referenced by any tracked file |
| Contributor identity metadata in the commit objects is permanent, public and replicated by every clone | Not rated; recorded as irreversible in Section 6.2.4 | None possible after the fact; rewriting history would change every commit id |
| Consumers who track a branch rather than pin a commit inherit whatever the tip becomes; zero tags exist to pin instead | Not rated | Content addressing lets a consumer pin a SHA. `main` currently sits 11 commits behind `jr_java1`, which is itself the open delivery item in Section 5.4.6 |
| The credential in the clone's untracked `.git/config` is a real secret in the operator's environment | Not rated | Its class is short-lived, it is conveyed by no clone, interactive prompting is disabled, and it is transmitted only over the HTTPS channel |

#### 6.4.5.4 Compliance Requirements

**GPL v3 is the only compliance regime that actually binds this project**, and it binds it in full: `LICENSE` carries the licence verbatim — 674 lines, 35,149 bytes, unchanged since the initial commit `c537a19`. Each obligation below is anchored to the clause line in `LICENSE`.

| Obligation | Clause and line anchor | Status at `HEAD` |
|---|---|---|
| Convey verbatim copies with the licence and notices intact | §4, `LICENSE` line 195 | **Met.** The licence travels with every clone as one of five tracked files; `README.md` line 77 states the terms and links to it |
| Mark modified versions and date the change | §5, line 208 | **Met.** `README.md` line 5 carries the dated notice "*Modified 2026-09-16.*", recorded against requirement F-006-RQ-003 |
| Impose no further restriction on downstream recipients | §7 line 343 and §10 line 446 | **Met.** No additional term, EULA, CLA or usage restriction exists in any tracked file; there is no `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `NOTICE` imposing terms |
| Do not invoke anti-circumvention law against users exercising licensed rights | §3, line 179 | **Met by construction.** The work contains no technological protection measure of any kind |
| Display Appropriate Legal Notices in an interactive interface | Defined at line 103; required at lines 231–232 | **Not applicable.** The program has no interactive user interface — it writes one line and exits — so the condition in §5(d) does not arise |
| Corresponding Source must require no special password or key to unpack, read or copy | §6, line 340 | **Met.** The source is plain text, conveyed by anonymous clone, with no archive, password or key involved. This is also the only password-related rule anywhere in the project (Section 6.4.2.5) |
| Patent provisions — no discriminatory patent licensing, automatic downstream patent grant | §11, line 471 | **No conflicting obligation observed.** No patent grant, licence exception or third-party term exists in the tracked tree |
| Termination on violation, with the stated reinstatement path | §8, line 407 | **Recorded as the enforcement mechanism** for PEP-6 (Section 6.4.3.4). No violation is asserted or known |
| Warranty disclaimed, liability limited, and both interpreted per the licence | §15 line 589, §16 line 600, §17 line 612 | **Met by conveyance.** These are the project's entire warranty and liability position; no separate warranty, support or service-level statement exists anywhere (Section 5.4.5) |
| Per-file copyright and warranty notice as the licence appendix advises | Template at line 635 | **Not met — deferred.** No tracked file records a copyright holder or year, and `Hello.java` carries no copyright line. ADR-010 and Section 2.4.4 record this as an open owner decision, a licensing-compliance gap rather than a technical vulnerability |
| Combination with the GNU Affero GPL | §13, line 552 | **Not exercised.** No AGPL-covered component is combined; there is no dependency of any kind |

**Regulatory and privacy scope.** No tracked file records a regulatory, privacy, sectoral or contractual security obligation, and none is asserted here. The data inventory in Section 6.4.4.1 contains no datum the program collects from a person: there is no user account, no data subject, no cardholder data, no health record, no biometric or location datum, and no telemetry — the program reads no input and stores nothing. The only personal-adjacent data in the project is the contributor identity metadata permanently embedded in the 14 commit objects, which Section 6.2.4 records as irreversible by construction. Because the repository ships no cryptographic implementation, there is likewise no encryption functionality to declare.

#### 6.4.5.5 Evidence Available for a Compliance Audit

| Evidence an auditor can obtain | What it substantiates | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| The complete object store from any clone — 5 tracked blobs, 14 commits, 13 trees, 8 refs, 0 tags | Authorship, chronology and content of every change, verifiable by re-hashing | Ten of fourteen commits are unsigned, so author identity is self-asserted for most of the history |
| `LICENSE`, verbatim and unchanged since `c537a19` | The licence position and the full warranty and liability terms | No per-file notice and no recorded rights holder (Section 6.4.5.4) |
| `README.md` — the dated modification notice at line 5, the output oracle at lines 59–61, the hardening rationale at line 30 | Compliance with §5's marking requirement, and the operator-facing contract as published | Its Project Layout claim at line 67 is stale: it describes three tracked files and no subdirectories against a five-file tree |
| `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §3–§6 | The verification record (49 of 49 checks on OpenJDK 25.0.3), the 12-row compliance matrix, and the risk register with severities and statuses | Prose written by hand, not machine output. Nothing re-runs the checks, so it is a point-in-time record and, per Section 5.4.6, the one asset with no mechanical recovery path |
| Direct measurement of the checkout — file modes, object format, `git fsck`, configuration keys, signature histogram, censuses | The static security posture at `HEAD`, reproducible by any reader with Git and POSIX text tools | Runtime behaviour cannot be re-derived without a JDK, which this verification environment lacks |
| The absence findings themselves — 32 governance-artifact probes, 17 key-material patterns, the 14-pattern credential census over every blob | That no security control, key or credential was removed, stubbed or hidden | Absence at `HEAD` says nothing about a future commit, and no gate exists to preserve it |


### 6.4.6 Reassessment Triggers and Cross-Section References

The determination in Section 6.4.1 is a statement about the repository at commit `2a78292` on branch `jr_java1`, not a permanent property of the project. This sub-section records the specific, observable changes that would invalidate it, so a future reader can test the verdict rather than re-derive it, and then maps the related material elsewhere in this specification.

#### 6.4.6.1 Changes That Would Make a Security Architecture Applicable

Each trigger maps to one of the six failed preconditions in Section 6.4.1.1. Any single one occurring would require this sub-section to be rewritten as a substantive security architecture rather than amended.

| Trigger | Failed precondition it would satisfy | Sub-sections that would need content |
|---|---|---|
| The program begins to **read anything** — `args` dereferenced, a `System.in` or `Scanner` read, a file read, `System.getenv` or `System.getProperty`, or an accepted connection | P1 — a principal whose identity the system can receive | 6.4.2 in full; 6.4.3.3 resource authorization; 6.4.5.1 attack surface. Section 5.4.4 records that the first input is also the project's first authentication question |
| A **protected resource** appears — a file written outside the scratch directory, a bound port, a datastore, or any operation with a privileged effect | P2 — a resource an authorization decision could govern | 6.4.3.1 through 6.4.3.4; 6.4.4.1 data inventory; 6.4.5.2 control matrix |
| A **credential, key or keystore** enters the tracked tree, or any tracked file begins reading an environment variable or secret | P3 — a secret the system must hold or present | 6.4.2.4 token handling; 6.4.4.3 key management; 6.4.4.4 masking rules; 6.4.5.3 residual risks |
| A **personal, payment, health or otherwise regulated datum** enters the data domain | P4 — a confidential or regulated datum | 6.4.4.1, 6.4.4.2 and 6.4.4.4; 6.4.5.4 compliance requirements, which would acquire its first regulatory row |
| Any **configuration, policy or governance file** appears — `*.properties`, `*.yml`, `*.json`, `*.xml`, a Java policy file, `SECURITY.md` or `CODEOWNERS` | P5 — a place in which a security policy could be expressed | 6.4.3.1 RBAC; 6.4.3.2 permission management; 6.4.3.4 enforcement points; 6.4.5.2 |

Four further changes would **not** make a bespoke security architecture applicable, but would each close a control this sub-section currently records as absent and expected:

- **A `.gitignore` or `.gitattributes`** would convert the build-output containment control (SC-14) and the line-ending position from command and editor discipline into enforced policy; both are open owner decisions in Section 2.4.1.
- **A `SECURITY.md` or `.well-known/security.txt`** would create the vulnerability-disclosure path whose absence is recorded in Section 6.4.5.3 and as SC-24.
- **Enforced commit signing** (`commit.gpgsign` with a configured key, or a platform requirement) would move SC-11 from absent to inherited and make authorship cryptographically attested rather than self-asserted for new commits.
- **A recorded copyright holder and year** would allow the per-file notice the licence appendix advises, closing the one open obligation in Section 6.4.5.4 and requirement F-006-RQ-005.

## 6.5 Monitoring and Observability

### 6.5.1 Applicability Determination

**Detailed Monitoring Architecture is not applicable for this system.**

At commit `2a78292` on branch `jr_java1` the repository tracks five files, of which exactly one is executable: `Hello.java`, 20 lines and 1,073 bytes, whose only member is `main(String[] args)` and whose entire behaviour is the single statement at line 17 — `System.out.println("Hello from Java!")`. A process that exists for the duration of one write has no steady state to sample, no request to trace, no queue to measure and no availability window to compute. `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` §4, line 130, records the shape of the thing being monitored: it is "a console application with no user interface, no hosted page, no bound port and no external integration," and Appendix B, line 426, adds that it "binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call; there is no service, database, broker or cache in this project."

The determination is corroborated at three independent levels, each measured against the checkout rather than assumed. A **64-marker observability census** over `Hello.java` — covering logging APIs (`Logger`, `getLogger`, `java.util.logging`, `slf4j`, `log4j`, `logback`), metric instruments (`MeterRegistry`, `Counter`, `Timer`, `Gauge`, `Histogram`, `Prometheus`, `CollectorRegistry`), tracing types (`OpenTelemetry`, `Tracer`, `Span`, `TraceId`, `SpanId`, `Baggage`), platform introspection (`ManagementFactory`, `MXBean`, `MBeanServer`, `JMX`, `jdk.jfr`, `FlightRecorder`), timing calls (`System.nanoTime`, `System.currentTimeMillis`, `Instant.now`, `Duration.`), probe vocabulary (`health`, `healthz`, `readiness`, `liveness`, `heartbeat`) and diagnostic sinks (`System.err`, `printStackTrace`, `addShutdownHook`) — returns **exactly one hit**: the payload write at line 17, matched only because it is a `println`. Section 5.4.2 fixes the interpretation: "the program's single write is its product, not its log." `System.err` occurs zero times, and the line comment at line 16 makes single-sink behaviour a stated design property — "no other sink is written."

**109 existence probes** across six monitoring-artifact categories return zero present files, a recursive search for telemetry data files (`*.log`, `*.jfr`, `*.hprof`, `*.prom`, `*.tsdb`) returns zero files, and `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` confirms that only the five known paths have ever been added on any branch. No monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, dashboard or runbook artifact has ever existed in this repository's recorded history — nothing was removed, stubbed out or deferred.

Section 5.4.1 states the same verdict from the cross-cutting view — "No monitoring exists, and no component capable of monitoring is present" — and Section 6.4.5.2 carries it as control row SC-23, "Monitoring, alerting and incident detection … Absent and expected."

Declaring non-applicability does not discharge the areas this section must address. Sections 6.5.2 through 6.5.4 take each in turn — metrics collection, log aggregation, distributed tracing, alert management, dashboard design, health checks, performance and business metrics, SLA monitoring, capacity tracking, alert routing, escalation, runbooks, post-mortems and improvement tracking — and label each as exactly one of:

- **Genuinely absent** — no corresponding surface exists, so the capability cannot be applied and its absence is structural rather than an omission.
- **Inherited** — the capability is in force but supplied by the host, the JDK, Git or the hosting platform, not implemented by anything in the repository.
- **Selected** — the repository itself chose the mechanism and states the reason.
- **Absent and expected** — a capability a maintained project would reasonably carry, and it is missing; each is carried as a recorded risk.

#### 6.5.1.1 Preconditions Tested

Seven preconditions must hold before a monitoring architecture has anything to describe. All seven fail, and each was tested against the checkout.

| # | Precondition | Verified result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | A resident process with a steady state to observe | **Fails.** `main` is invoked once, executes one statement and returns; `Project Guide.md` §9.5 records "There is no service to start — the program writes one line and exits." Section 5.4.1 states the consequence: the process "lives for the duration of one write, so there is no steady state to observe" |
| M2 | A telemetry emission point in the code — logger, meter, span, probe endpoint or timing call | **Fails.** The 64-marker census yields one hit, the payload `println` at line 17. Zero `System.err` writes, zero timing calls, zero shutdown hooks, zero `assert` statements, and the source declares no `import` at all |
| M3 | A destination in which collected telemetry could be stored | **Fails.** No log file, metric store, trace backend or file sink exists; the recursive telemetry-data search returns zero files, and Section 6.2 records that no runtime path reaches durable media |
| M4 | A notification channel on which an alert could be raised | **Fails.** Section 4.3.2.6 records the absence of a notification channel of any kind; the eighteen alerting, paging and status-page probes in Section 6.5.6.2 are all absent. The operator's terminal is the only signal channel in the system |
| M5 | A declared target — SLA, SLO, threshold or error budget — to compare an observation against | **Fails.** A strict census for `latency`, `throughput`, `availability`, `uptime`, percentile notation, `error budget`, `service level`, `SLA`, `SLO`, `RTO`, `RPO`, `MTTR`, `MTBF`, `response time`, `milliseconds` and `benchmark` returns **zero hits** in `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`, and one hit in `Project Guide.md` — the word "Benchmark" in a table header at line 149. Section 5.4.5 states the position directly: the repository "states no performance requirement, no service-level objective and no service-level agreement" |
| M6 | A place in which monitoring configuration could be expressed | **Fails.** Section 6.1.1.2 records a recursive configuration census across the whole checkout for `*.yml`, `*.yaml`, `*.xml`, `*.properties`, `*.json`, `*.toml`, `*.ini`, `*.conf`, `*.sh`, `*.jar` and `*.class` returning **zero files**. There is no descriptor anywhere capable of holding a scrape target, a log route, a sampling rate, an alert rule or a dashboard definition |
| M7 | An automated executor able to run a check without a human | **Fails.** No CI descriptor, `Makefile`, wrapper script, cron entry, systemd unit or timer exists, and all 14 `.git/hooks` entries are `*.sample`. ADR-002 records the position; `Project Guide.md` §6 carries "No build descriptor, test suite or CI workflow, so nothing re-runs the documentation checks" as an Open operational risk at Medium severity and Medium probability |

#### 6.5.1.3 Basic Monitoring Practices Followed Instead

In place of a monitoring stack the project relies on a small set of deterministic, operator-run checks. Every one of them is a comparison against a published expectation rather than a measurement of a trend, which is what makes them adequate for a program whose entire contract is three values. Each command below is documented in the repository; none is executed automatically.

| Practice in force | Check and expected signal | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Three-value process observation | `java Hello; echo "exit=$?"` — the literal `Hello from Java!` plus one platform line separator on standard output, an empty standard error, and `exit=0`. `Project Guide.md` §9.7 records exactly that transcript | Selected — the system's primary health check (Section 6.5.3.1) |
| Output-oracle byte comparison | Compare captured standard output against the fenced oracle at `README.md` lines 59–61; `Project Guide.md` §4 records the comparison as byte-identical, with the payload observed at 17 bytes on an LF host | Selected |
| Static-analysis gate at compile time | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror -d "$B" Hello.java` — exit 0 with an empty error stream. `Project Guide.md` Appendix F names this "the project's static-analysis surface, as no linter is configured" | Selected — ADR-002 |
| Documentation-coverage check | `javadoc -d "$B/jd" -quiet Hello.java` — exit 0 with exactly one warning, for the implicit default constructor at `Hello.java:6`, which cannot carry a doc comment | Selected |
| Behaviour-parity check against a baseline | Compile revision `0726b1d`, run both builds, and `cmp` the captured standard output and standard error of each — `Project Guide.md` §9.6 expects "behaviour identical" | Selected |
| Repository-hygiene check | `git status --short` expecting no output, and `git ls-files` expecting the tracked inventory; run after every build and verification step | Selected |
| Stored-byte-format census | `Hello.java` expected at `lf=20 cr=20 crlf=20`; `README.md` expected at `cr=0` with a trailing newline — the compensating control where no `.gitattributes` exists | Selected |
| Change-history and integrity record | 14 commit objects with author identity and timestamps in an append-only, content-addressed store; `git fsck` clean and blob digests reproducible (Section 6.4.3.5) | Inherited — the only durable event log in the system |
| Point-in-time evidence record | `Project Guide.md` §3 and §4 — 49 checks executed, 49 passed, 0 failed on OpenJDK 25.0.3, across nine acceptance groups V1–V9 plus 12 direct toolchain checks | Inherited — prose, written by hand |

Three limitations of this arrangement are recorded rather than mitigated, and they are the honest cost of having no monitoring infrastructure. **Nothing re-runs any of these checks**, so the 49 recorded results are a point-in-time observation whose only durable record is `Project Guide.md` §3 and §4. **No run leaves evidence of itself** — Section 6.4.3.5 records that nothing captures that an execution occurred: no log file, no exit-status record, no metric and no trace. And **there is no channel on which a failure could be announced**: Section 4.3.2.6 records the absence of a notification channel, so detection depends entirely on a human reading a terminal at the moment of the run.

#### 6.5.1.4 Applicability Decision Path

**Figure 6.5.1-A — The applicability test, precondition by precondition, and the practices that stand in for a monitoring stack**
