##### 6.6.1.1.4 Scope and Verification Environment

Three constraints on the evidence in this section should be stated so its claims can be weighted correctly. The convention follows Sections 6.4.1.5 and 6.5.1.5.

| Constraint | Consequence for this section |
|---|---|
| **No JDK is installed** in the environment used to verify the repository — `java`, `javac` and `javadoc` are all absent from `PATH` and every invocation exits **127** | No compile, launch, `javadoc` or cross-release check could be re-executed first-hand. Every result attributed to the check suite — the 49-of-49 tally, the zero-diagnostic compile, the single `javadoc` warning, the byte-identical parity and the release-target outcomes — is quoted from `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` as **recorded** evidence on OpenJDK 25.0.3. The failure mode is itself evidence: a JDK on `PATH` is the one non-negotiable prerequisite of the entire procedure |
| Git and standard POSIX text tooling are present | All repository-state and toolchain-independent findings are **first-hand**: the 127 artifact probes, the 68-marker source census, the recursive test-filename search, the history check across every branch, the hook-state check, the line-ending and byte-format censuses, the guide-structure and summary-budget checks, the two-link check, the secret census and the resolvability of baseline revision `0726b1d` |
| No coverage threshold, pass-rate target, performance budget or test-quality figure exists in any tracked file | This section defines none. Where the prompt calls for coverage targets, success-rate requirements or performance thresholds, what is documented is the **expectation the repository actually publishes** and the **absence** of any target, never an invented number (Sections 6.6.3.1 through 6.6.3.3) |

The one untracked file in the working tree, `tech_spec.md`, is an authoring artifact of the documentation process. It is not tracked, is not a system file, and is excluded from every census and figure above.

#### 6.6.1.2 Unit Testing

**No unit test exists, and the program offers nothing a unit test could isolate.** What follows documents the basic verification approach actually in force, concern by concern, and states precisely what a unit test would have to do if one were ever introduced — because the shape of `Hello.java` constrains that answer to two options.

##### 6.6.1.2.1 Testing Frameworks and Tools

No test framework, assertion library, mocking library or runner is configured or resolvable: JUnit, TestNG, Spock, Cucumber, Mockito, AssertJ, Hamcrest and Truth are absent from the 68-marker source census, and with no manifest (precondition T6) none could be declared. The instruments that do the verification work are the JDK toolchain, Git and POSIX text utilities, and `Project Guide.md` Appendix F names each one's role.

| Instrument | Role in the verification approach | Expected signal |
|---|---|---|
| `javac` (OpenJDK 25.0.3) | Compiles the single unit; `-Xlint:all -Werror` is, per Appendix F, "the project's static-analysis surface, as no linter is configured" | Exit 0, no diagnostics, empty error stream |
| `java` launcher | Executes the unit under test as a process in three documented forms | `Hello from Java!` plus one platform separator, empty standard error, exit status 0 |
| `javadoc` | Measures documentation coverage; `-Xdoclint:all` validates doc-comment syntax and tag usage, and its HTML output "is never committed" | Exit 0 with exactly one warning, for the implicit default constructor at `Hello.java:6` |
| `git` (2.51.0 recorded; 2.43.0 observed here) | Supplies the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` used as the reference implementation for behaviour-parity and change-shape comparisons | `git show 0726b1d:Hello.java` resolves; `git status --short` prints nothing |
| GNU `grep`, `awk`, `diff`, `tr`, `od`, `cmp`, `iconv` | Assert file structure and stored byte format directly against the source, so "verification needs no renderer and no extra runtime" | Exact literal counts, enumerated per check in `Project Guide.md` §9.6 |
| `mktemp -d` | Generates the per-run build and scratch directories, "keeping class output out of the checkout" | A uniquely named, owner-readable-only directory per run |

##### 6.6.1.2.2 Test Organization Structure

There is no `src/test/java`, no parallel test tree and no test resource directory — all 21 conventional layout probes are absent, and the repository is flat apart from `blitzy/documentation/`. The checks are instead organised as **nine acceptance groups plus a set of direct toolchain checks, held outside the checkout by design**. `Project Guide.md` §9.6 states the placement rule and the invocation:

```bash
S="$(mktemp -d)"     # paste the suite into "$S/verify.sh"
bash "$S/verify.sh" "$PWD" "$PWD/Hello.java" "$PWD/README.md" "$(date -u +%F)"
```

| Group | What it asserts | Recorded result |
|---|---|---|
| Compilation and static diagnostics | The annotated source compiles with zero diagnostics, including under `-Xlint:all -Werror` | 2 of 2 passed; coverage 1 of 1 compilation unit |
| V2 — runtime behaviour and parity | Output, error stream and exit status are byte-identical to a build of the pre-comment source, and arguments never alter the result | 6 of 6 passed; both documented launch paths |
| V3 — comment structure and placement | The change adds exactly four comments, each attached to the construct it documents, and alters no code line | 7 of 7 passed; 4 of 4 functionalities |
| V4 — stored byte format | `Hello.java` keeps CRLF on every line, pure ASCII and no tabs; the guide stays LF-only, UTF-8 and newline-terminated | 7 of 7 passed; both changed files |
| V5 — comment coverage | The class and entry point are documented; only the implicit constructor, which can carry no doc comment, is not | 2 of 2 passed; 2 of 3 documentable members |
| V6–V7 — guide structure and highlighting | The change summary is the guide's first content block, sections run in the required order, and italics mark the two changed files and nothing else | 8 of 8 passed; 8 of 8 sections |
| V8–V9 — links, literals and citations | Both relative links resolve on disk, every mandated operator literal is present, and sources are cited by stable symbol with no line-number locators | 10 of 10 passed; 2 of 2 links, 2 of 2 citations |
| Cross-release compilation | The compile-then-run path carries no recent-JDK floor, as the guide's Requirements section claims | 7 of 7 passed; release targets 11, 17 and 21 |

The suite's own structure carries one recorded defect of organisation rather than of code. Its comment-census group takes a baseline revision as an argument and the plan named the current commit; at `HEAD` that comparison is empty, so four assertions fail vacuously against a correct tree and "the suite's own tally on a correct tree is 33 of 37." Supplying the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` "restores the intent … and the suite then passes 37 of 37." `Project Guide.md` §5.2 records the remedy as the invocation rather than a code change, "since the script is provisioned outside the repository and committing a test file is out of scope."

##### 6.6.1.2.3 Mocking Strategy

**Genuinely absent — and nothing in the program is mockable.** The 68-marker census returns zero Mockito, EasyMock and PowerMock references; `Hello.java` declares no `interface`, `abstract`, `implements` or `extends`, so there is no polymorphic seam; it declares no field and no constructor, so there is no injection point; and it declares no `import`, so its only collaborator is `java.lang.System`, reached through the static field `System.out`. Substituting that would require a test to install a replacement `PrintStream`, and the census confirms zero `System.setOut`, `setErr`, `PrintStream` and `ByteArrayOutputStream` references anywhere in the source — no capture seam exists in the code.

Two substitution techniques *are* used, and they operate on the process and the revision rather than on objects.

| Technique in use | What it substitutes | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Baseline revision as reference implementation** (Selected) | The pre-comment source at `0726b1d`, compiled into a scratch directory and executed alongside the current build, stands in for an expected-value fixture. Both captured streams and the exit status are compared with `cmp`, and "suppressing debug information makes the two class files identical" | `Project Guide.md` §9.6, §4 |
| **Per-run scratch directories as environment isolation** (Selected) | `mktemp -d` supplies `$B` for build output, `$O` for the parity comparison and `$S` for the suite, so no run observes another run's artifacts and the checkout is never written to | `Project Guide.md` §9.4, §9.6; `README.md` line 30 |

If a unit test were ever introduced, the absence of a seam leaves exactly two observation strategies, and the repository has already chosen the second for its own checks:

```java
// NOT PRESENT IN THIS REPOSITORY — illustrative only: in-process capture
System.setOut(new PrintStream(buffer));   // the only way to intercept line 17 in-process
Hello.main(new String[0]);                // assert buffer against the README oracle
```

The alternative is **process-level capture** — launch `Hello` as a subprocess and compare its captured standard output, standard error and exit status against the published oracle. That is precisely what `Project Guide.md` §9.6 does, it requires no test file, and it is why the project's verification is black-box rather than unit-level.

##### 6.6.1.2.4 Code Coverage Requirements

**No coverage tool is configured and no coverage threshold is declared anywhere** — JaCoCo, Cobertura, Clover, `lcov`, Codecov and PIT mutation testing are all absent from the 23 coverage and quality probes, and no manifest exists in which a `check` or `verify` goal could bind one. No coverage percentage for executable code is therefore reported, and none is invented here.

Three coverage-adjacent figures are measured or recorded, and their bases differ:

| Coverage dimension | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Compilation-unit coverage | **1 of 1** — the single unit is compiled by every check that compiles anything | `Project Guide.md` §3, compilation row |
| Statement coverage achieved per run | **All five executable lines are traversed by any successful run.** The program contains no branch and no loop, so its single straight-line path is the whole program; this is a structural property of the source, not an instrumented measurement, and no tool records it | Executable-line census of `Hello.java` (lines 6, 15, 17, 19, 20) |
| Documentation coverage | **2 of 3 documentable members**, with exactly one accepted `javadoc` warning at `Hello.java:6`. The third member is the implicit default constructor, which "can carry no doc comment, and declaring one is a structural change the comment-only constraint forbids" | `Project Guide.md` §3, §5.2 divergence 4, §9.6 |

The documentation-coverage figure is the project's substitute for a code-coverage gate: it is the one coverage number the toolchain can produce without a test framework, it has a published expected value, and a deviation from exactly one warning is treated as a signal in both directions — "0 or ≥2 means comment coverage changed."

##### 6.6.1.2.5 Test Naming Conventions

No test method, class or display name exists, so no test-naming convention is in force. Three naming systems do carry the identity of checks and findings, and they are the vocabulary a reader should expect:

| Identifier family | Form and meaning | Where defined |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance groups | `V1` … `V9`, one per assertion group, referenced by the per-area rows of the results table | `Project Guide.md` §3 |
| Requirement anchors | `F-nnn-RQ-nnn`, each traced to an artifact anchor and a verification method of *static*, *recorded* or *open* | Section 2.5.1 |
| Fault identifiers | `E-1` … `E-7`, one per symptom in the troubleshooting table that serves as the project's runbook | `Project Guide.md` §9.8; Section 4.3.2.2 |

One naming rule is imposed by the language rather than by convention, and the verification procedure has to obey it: a public class must live in a file of the same name, so the baseline export in §9.6 writes into a directory **as `Hello.java`** — the comment on that line reads "the file name must match the public class." Getting it wrong produces fault E-2, `error: class Hello is public, should be declared in a file named Hello.java`.

##### 6.6.1.2.6 Test Data Management

**There is no test data to manage in the conventional sense** — no fixture, factory, builder, seed script, snapshot or golden-file directory exists, and the 21 layout probes confirm no `testdata/`, `test-data/`, `fixtures/`, `__files/` or `cassettes/` directory. The program reads no input, so there is no input data at all; every datum in the verification approach is an *expected* value.

| Datum | Source and form | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|
| Output oracle | The fenced `text` block at `README.md` lines 59–61 containing exactly `Hello from Java!`. Verified with `cat -A` as LF-terminated with no CR; the literal is **16 bytes**, so 17 bytes with a single LF separator | Version-controlled with the guide; compared byte for byte per run |
| Stream and status expectations | `README.md` line 63 — "Standard error stays empty and the process exits with status 0" | Version-controlled; asserted per run |
| Reference implementation | Blob of `Hello.java` at revision `0726b1d`, extracted with `git show` into a scratch directory. The revision is resolvable in the checkout, and `git diff 0726b1d HEAD --stat` confirms `Hello.java` at **+15 additions and no deletions** | Materialised per run into `$O`, discarded afterwards |
| Structural expectations | Literal counts published in `Project Guide.md` §9.6 — `added=15 /**=2 */=2 //=2`, `Hello.java lf=20 cr=20 crlf=20`, `README.md cr=0` with a trailing newline, eight ordered sections, a 55-word summary against a 70-word limit, exactly two relative links. Every one of these was re-verified first-hand and matched | Published in prose; asserted by shell census |
| Argument inputs | Supplied on the command line and never consumed — `args[` occurs **zero times** in the source, so the array is never indexed. Runs "with no arguments, many arguments, and hostile arguments including shell and injection payloads all produce identical output" | Constructed ad hoc per run; no fixture file |

The test data is, in short, **a 16-byte literal, an empty stream, an exit status and a Git revision**. None of it needs seeding, none of it needs cleanup, and none of it is stored outside the two documentation files and the object store.

#### 6.6.1.3 Integration Testing

**No service integration exists to test.** Precondition T4 fails on a zero-hit egress census and on Appendix B's statement that the program "binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call." What the approach does integration-test is the program **against its toolchain, its host and its own documentation** — the only three things it actually meets.

##### 6.6.1.3.1 Service Integration Test Approach

| Integration concern | Position at `HEAD` |
|---|---|
| Service-to-service integration | **Genuinely absent.** One process, one frame, one write; no second component and no second compilation unit. Section 2.4.3 notes that adding one "would immediately create the build-ordering and manifest concerns the project currently has none of" |
| Program-to-toolchain integration (Selected) | The real integration surface: `javac` compiles the unit, the `java` launcher resolves and runs it in three documented forms, and `javadoc` parses its doc comments. Every check in §9.6 exercises one of these three couplings |
| Launch-path equivalence (Selected) | `java -cp "$B" Hello`, `java Hello` and `java Hello.java` must agree. `README.md` line 46 publishes the contract — "Both paths produce byte-identical standard output" — and the runtime-parity group records **6 of 6** checks passed across both documented paths |
| Cross-release integration (Selected) | Compilation at `--release` targets 11, 17 and 21, plus `java --source 11`, corroborating the guide's claim that the compile-then-run path carries no recent-JDK floor: **7 of 7** checks passed |
| Contract-to-documentation integration (Selected) | The fenced expected-output block is compared byte for byte against real standard output, and both relative links are resolved on disk — the guide is treated as a consumer of the program's contract and tested as such |

##### 6.6.1.3.2 API Testing Strategy

There is no HTTP, RPC or library API: the program publishes no endpoint, and `Project Guide.md` Appendix B records that no port is bound. The only interface it offers is the **JVM entry-point contract and the command line**, and that contract is tested in three parts.

| Contract clause | How it is tested | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| Entry point reachable by the bare class name | Launch as `java Hello` from the directory holding the class, and as `java -cp "$B" Hello` from outside it. The class is in the default package, "so the bare name is correct" | `Hello from Java!` from both |
| Argument insensitivity | Launch with no arguments, with many arguments, and with hostile arguments "including shell and injection payloads"; compare outputs | Identical output in every case; the parameter is never dereferenced |
| Termination contract | `java Hello; echo "exit=$?"` | `exit=0`, produced by normal return from `main` with no `System.exit` |

##### 6.6.1.3.3 Database Integration Testing

**Genuinely absent.** No database, broker or cache exists — Appendix B and §9.1 both state it, and Section 6.2 records that no runtime path reaches durable media. There is no schema to migrate, no transaction to roll back, no seeded dataset and no in-memory substitute to configure; the 20 test-environment probes confirm no Testcontainers, Compose or `.env.test` descriptor through which one could be provisioned.

The only persistent store the procedure touches is the **Git object store, read-only**, to materialise the baseline revision. Its integrity is inherited rather than tested: 14 commits in an append-only, content-addressed store, with `git status --short` used after every build and verification step as the store-state assertion.

##### 6.6.1.3.4 External Service Mocking

**Genuinely absent and unnecessary.** With zero imports, zero network markers and no dependency manifest, there is no external call to intercept and no stub server to stand up — WireMock, MockServer, VCR-style cassettes and recorded-response directories are all absent from the census. `Project Guide.md` §6 disposes of the category in one line: the program "reads no input, dereferences no argument, opens no resource, binds no port, makes no network call and has no dependency manifest." The baseline-revision technique of Section 6.6.1.2.3 is the only substitution in use.

##### 6.6.1.3.5 Test Environment Management

Environment management is **per-run, directory-scoped and self-cleaning**, and it is the one area where the procedure is deliberately more careful than a minimal project would be.

| Environment element | Mechanism | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Build output | `B="$(mktemp -d)"`, then `javac -Xlint:all -d "$B" Hello.java` | Exit 0 and no output at all; the working tree is untouched |
| Parity workspace | `O="$(mktemp -d)"; mkdir -p "$O/base"`, holding the exported baseline source, two builds and four captured stream files | `cmp` reports both stream pairs identical — "behaviour identical" |
| Suite workspace | `S="$(mktemp -d)"`, holding `verify.sh`, which is never committed | 49 of 49 checks pass when given baseline `0726b1d` |
| Teardown | `rm -rf "$B" "$O" "$S" && git status --short` | No output. For an in-place Path A compile, `rm -f Hello.class && git status --short` |
| Checkout state | `git status --short` and `git ls-files` before and after | No output from the first; the tracked inventory from the second |

The choice of `mktemp -d` over a fixed path is a **security control on the test environment**, not a convenience. `README.md` line 30 records the reason: `mktemp -d` "returns a uniquely named one readable only by its owner, whereas a fixed, predictable destination can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it." `Project Guide.md` §6 carries the reintroduction of a predictable output path as a Security-category risk, and records it as the register's only **Mitigated** entry.

#### 6.6.1.4 End-to-End Testing

End-to-end here means **the whole documented operator journey**, because that journey is the system: a clone, a compile, a launch, three observations and a clean tree. `Project Guide.md` §4 defines the scope exactly — "runtime validation means driving the compiler, the launcher, the documentation tool and every command the guide tells an operator to type."

##### 6.6.1.4.1 End-to-End Scenarios

| Scenario | Path exercised | Recorded outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Compile in place, launch, clean up | `javac Hello.java` → `java Hello` → `rm -f Hello.class` → `git status --short` | Exit 0 and no diagnostics; correct payload; clean tree. "Compiling inside a throwaway clone leaves the class file untracked and unignored, exactly as the Build section states" |
| Compile out of tree, launch from the classpath | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror -d "$B"` → `java -cp "$B" Hello` | Compile exits 0 with an empty error stream; the launch prints the payload "followed by one newline (17 bytes on this host), with an empty error stream and exit status 0" |
| Direct source launch | `java Hello.java` | Same payload, and "leaves no class file behind" |
| Argument-bearing launch | `java Hello.java one two three`, plus many and hostile arguments | Identical output in every case |
| Behaviour parity against the baseline | Build `0726b1d` and `HEAD`, run both, `cmp` both stream pairs | Both streams and the exit status "compare byte-identical against a build of the pre-comment source" |
| Documentation-tool journey | `javadoc -quiet` over the unit, then inspect the generated HTML | Exit 0 with exactly one warning; "the generated HTML carries both comment blocks and the parameter table" |
| Guide-guidance journey | Execute the guide's own alternate build destination end to end | "A freshly generated owner-only directory, compiles and launches clean end to end" |

##### 6.6.1.4.2 UI Automation Approach

**Genuinely absent — there is no UI to automate.** `Project Guide.md` §4 records "no user interface, no hosted page, no bound port"; the E2E and browser probes (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, WebDriver, Karma, TestCafe, Puppeteer) are all absent; and the program writes to a file descriptor it inherits rather than to any rendered surface.

One view-like artifact remains, and the project is explicit that it was never driven: the Markdown documentation. §3 lists "The guide's rendered appearance" among the things not covered — "Emphasis, the two tables, the four fenced blocks and both relative links were asserted against the Markdown source, never against a rendered page. Open the guide once on the hosting platform before release." §4 repeats it as the single "Never exercised at runtime" item. The corresponding structural assertions are the shell checks of Section 6.6.1.2.6, all of which were re-verified first-hand against the source text.

##### 6.6.1.4.3 Test Data Setup and Teardown

Setup and teardown are three commands and a comparison, and they are symmetrical by construction.

```bash
B="$(mktemp -d)"; O="$(mktemp -d)"; S="$(mktemp -d)"   # setup: per-run, owner-only
git show 0726b1d:Hello.java > "$O/base/Hello.java"     # materialise the reference implementation
rm -rf "$B" "$O" "$S" && git status --short            # teardown: expect no output
```

The program itself needs neither: it reads no input, keeps no state and persists nothing, so there is no database to reset, no cache to flush and no file to remove other than a `Hello.class` produced by an in-place compile. `README.md` line 30 instructs "Do not commit the class file either way," and the absence of an ignore rule is what makes the teardown assertion necessary at all — fault E-3 exists solely because of it.

##### 6.6.1.4.4 Performance Testing Requirements

**No performance test exists and no performance requirement is declared anywhere in the repository.** Section 5.4.5 records the absence of any latency target, throughput figure, availability objective, capacity plan, error budget or timing measurement, and the strict census reported in Section 6.5.1.1 returns zero hits for that vocabulary across `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`. JMH, Gatling, JMeter, k6 and Locust are all absent from the harness probes, and no benchmark has ever been committed.

What exists is a small set of **structural baselines** — quantities about the artifact, not thresholds for a run:

| Baseline | Recorded value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Work per invocation | 4 bytecode instructions in `main` | Section 5.4.5 |
| Output volume | 16 ASCII characters plus one platform separator — 17 bytes on an LF host, 18 on a CRLF host | `Project Guide.md` §4; `README.md` lines 57–63 |
| Error-stream volume | 0 bytes on every run | `README.md` line 63 |
| Compiled artifact size | 420 bytes | Section 5.4.5 |
| Dependency-resolution cost | 0 artifacts fetched; nothing is downloaded at build time | `README.md` line 18; §9.3 |
| Wall-clock runtime, CPU and memory | **Not measured anywhere**, and not measurable in this verification environment — no JDK and no `/usr/bin/time` are installed | Section 6.5.3.2 |

##### 6.6.1.4.5 Cross-Browser Testing Strategy

**Not applicable — there is no browser surface.** The equivalent portability axis for a console program is the **toolchain release and the host platform**, and that axis *is* tested. Two dimensions are exercised and one is only partially covered:

| Portability dimension | Coverage | Status |
|---|---|---|
| JDK release targets | `--release` 11, 17 and 21 exercised for the compile-then-run path, 7 checks, all passed | Covered; confirms the guide's "no recent-JDK floor" claim |
| Single-file source launch floor | Corroborated only by compiling at targets 11, 17 and 21 and by `java --source 11` on a JDK 25 toolchain | **Partial.** "The `JDK 11 or later` floor … has not been run on a JDK 11 runtime; only JDK 25 was available." Carried as requirement F-004-RQ-004 and as a Low/Low Integration risk |
| Host line separator | The contract is stated as "the literal plus a separator rather than a fixed byte count," so the payload is 17 bytes on an LF host and 18 on a CRLF host | Covered by contract; only the LF host was observed |
| Rendered Markdown platform | Not exercised on any renderer | **Absent and expected.** §3 recommends opening the guide once on the hosting platform before release |

### 6.6.2 Test Automation

**Nothing in this repository is automated.** Every check described in Section 6.6.1 is typed by a person, evaluated by eye against a published expectation, and recorded by hand. This sub-section documents that arrangement against each automation concern the specification calls for, and states what is verifiably absent rather than merely unconfigured.

#### 6.6.2.1 CI/CD Integration

**Absent and expected.** Nineteen CI-executor probes return absent — `.github/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.travis.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `.drone.yml`, `.teamcity/`, `appveyor.yml`, `cloudbuild.yaml`, `Taskfile.yml`, `justfile`, `Rakefile`, `tox.ini`, `noxfile.py`, `act.yml` and `.buildkite/` — and `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` confirms that no such descriptor has **ever** been added on any branch across 14 commits. `README.md` line 18 records the same absence from the version-pinning angle: the repository carries no "CI descriptor … in which a version could be recorded."

The scope position is explicit rather than incidental. `Project Guide.md` §9.6 instructs that the suite be run from a scratch directory and "never commit it, since build, test and CI files are out of scope for this repository," and §5.2 divergence 5 records that "No ignore rule and no build, test or CI descriptor was added" among five deliberately deferred hygiene items.

| Pipeline stage a CI system would provide | State in this repository |
|---|---|
| Checkout and toolchain provisioning | **Inherited from the operator's host.** §9.1 requires only a JDK, `git` and a POSIX shell with GNU `grep`, `diff`, `awk` and `coreutils`; there is "no package manager step, no virtual environment, no container, no database, no broker and no bound port" |
| Dependency resolution and caching | **Genuinely absent and vacuous.** Zero artifacts are fetched; §9.3 records no manifest or lock file of any kind |
| Build step | **Manual.** A single `javac` invocation, in one of two documented paths |
| Test step | **Manual.** The V1–V9 suite, invoked from a `mktemp -d` directory outside the checkout |
| Quality gate and merge blocking | **Absent.** Nothing blocks a merge on a check result; Section 3.6.3 records the structural gap as "Nothing re-runs any of these gates" |
| Artifact publication | **Genuinely absent.** No jar, archive or published coordinate exists, and `git tag` returns zero tags across 14 commits |
| Deployment | **Genuinely absent.** There is no deployment mechanism; the program is consumed as source from a clone |

The one automation-adjacent facility actually in use belongs to the hosting platform, not to the repository: `HEAD` is the merge commit `2a78292`, "Merge pull request #1" — a human or bot workflow step rather than a pipeline. ADR-002 records the decision to rely on the compiler's own `-Xlint:all -Werror` as the project's static gate instead of adopting a pipeline, and adopting one is carried as a `[Deferred]` owner decision in `Project Guide.md` §1.4 and as the constraint Section 2.6.2 records as K-3.

#### 6.6.2.2 Automated Test Triggers

**No trigger of any kind exists.** All **14 entries in `.git/hooks` end in `.sample`**, so no `pre-commit`, `pre-push`, `commit-msg` or `pre-receive` hook is active; no `crontab`, `.cron`, systemd unit or timer file is present; and with no CI descriptor there is no push, pull-request, tag, schedule or manual-dispatch event to bind a job to.

The triggers actually in force are human, and each is documented as an instruction rather than a configuration.

| Event | Documented obligation | Where recorded |
|---|---|---|
| Any edit to `Hello.java` | Re-run `javac -Xlint:all -Werror`; the compiler is the only static gate the project has | Section 2.4.5 F-004; `Project Guide.md` §1.6 |
| Any edit that could rewrite stored bytes | Re-run the line-ending census — "Edit in byte mode, re-emit CRLF on added lines, and re-run the line-ending census after any edit" | `Project Guide.md` §6, CRLF risk row |
| Any change intended to be comment-only | Re-run the additions-only comment census against the pre-comment revision `0726b1d`, expecting `added=15 /**=2 */=2 //=2` | `Project Guide.md` §9.6, §5.2 divergence 2 |
| Before publishing the change | Open the guide once on the hosting platform, because the rendered appearance is asserted against the Markdown source and never against a rendered page | `Project Guide.md` §3, "Not Covered" |
| After any build | `git status --short` expecting no output, and `rm -f Hello.class` if Path A was used | `Project Guide.md` §9.4 |

The consequence is recorded plainly in `Project Guide.md` §1.4 — "Nothing re-runs the documentation checks on future changes" — and it is the mechanism behind the register's Medium/Medium Open risk that "guide claims can drift from the source as the program changes."

#### 6.6.2.3 Parallel Test Execution

**No parallel runner is configured, and none is needed.** The 49 checks execute sequentially in a single shell session; there is no fork count, no thread-per-class setting, no shard index and no `junit-platform.properties` in which parallelism could be enabled — that file is among the absent probes.

Two properties of the work do bear on parallelism, and both are established from the code rather than assumed:

| Property | Evidence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Checks are mutually independent | Each stage allocates its own `mktemp -d` workspace (`$B`, `$O`, `$S`) and the checkout is only ever read, so no stage observes another's artifacts | The suite could be parallelised without redesign, but nothing in the repository does so |
| Invocations share nothing | Each launch is an independent JVM process that reads no input, writes no file and binds no port; the program allocates nothing and creates no thread | Section 6.1.3.1 records horizontal capacity as unbounded in principle and entirely manual in practice, with the ceiling set by host capacity the repository never measures |
| Sequential cost is trivially small | One compilation unit of 1,073 bytes, zero dependency resolution and a 4-instruction `main` | There is no runtime pressure that would motivate parallel execution, and no timing has ever been measured to quantify one |

#### 6.6.2.4 Test Reporting Requirements

**No machine-readable report is produced or retained.** There is no JUnit XML, no `surefire-reports/`, no `failsafe-reports/`, no coverage report and no test-result upload — the 23 coverage and reporting probes are all absent, and Section 6.1.1.2 records that a recursive configuration census across the whole checkout for `*.yml`, `*.yaml`, `*.xml`, `*.properties`, `*.json`, `*.toml`, `*.ini`, `*.conf`, `*.sh`, `*.jar` and `*.class` returns **zero files**. There is consequently no format, schema, publisher or dashboard to specify.

The reporting that does exist is **prose in a version-controlled Markdown file**, and it is the project's only durable test record.

| Report artifact | Content | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Result tally by area | Eight rows pairing each check group with its framework, its executed/passed/failed counts, its coverage denominator and what it proves — 49 executed, 49 passed, 0 failed on OpenJDK 25.0.3 | `Project Guide.md` §3 |
| Explicit "Not Covered" statement | Five items: no unit or integration tests exist; the rendered guide was never viewed; the JDK 11 floor was not exercised on a JDK 11 runtime; comment and prose wording is not machine-checkable; the comment census fails vacuously under its default baseline | `Project Guide.md` §3 |
| Runtime validation checklist | Ten items marked Operational or Partial, each naming the command run and the signal observed | `Project Guide.md` §4 |
| Compliance and divergence review | A twelve-row compliance matrix with evidence anchors, plus five divergence entries each with cause, impact and remediation | `Project Guide.md` §5.1, §5.2 |
| Risk register | Eight forward-looking risks with category, severity, probability, mitigation and status | `Project Guide.md` §6 |

Three properties of this reporting should be read alongside it. It is **hand-written**, so it records what an operator observed rather than what a tool emitted. It is **point-in-time**: the 49-of-49 tally is an observation on OpenJDK 25.0.3 and ages the moment the source changes. And it is **the only record that survives a run** — Section 6.4.3.5 records that nothing captures that an execution occurred, so no log, exit-status record, metric or trace exists to reconstruct a past result from.

#### 6.6.2.5 Failed Test Handling

Failure handling is **synchronous, human and fully documented**. There is no retry policy, no automatic re-run, no bisect automation and no notification — Section 4.3.2.6 records the absence of a notification channel of any kind, so detection depends on a person reading the terminal at the moment of the run. What the repository provides instead is a complete fault catalogue with a resolution for every entry: the seven-row troubleshooting table at `Project Guide.md` §9.8, which serves as the project's runbook and maps one-to-one onto faults `E-1` through `E-7` of Section 4.3.2.2.

| Failing check | Fault | Documented resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Launch fails with `Could not find or load main class Hello` | E-1 | No compiled class on the classpath, or the wrong directory. Compile first, or launch with `java -cp <build dir> Hello`; the bare name is correct because the class is in the default package |
| Baseline compile fails with `class Hello is public, should be declared in a file named Hello.java` | E-2 | The source was exported under another name. Export into the scratch directory **as `Hello.java`**, as §9.6 does |
| `git status --short` prints a line after a build | E-3 | An in-place compile left `Hello.class` and no ignore rule covers it. Delete it, or compile to a directory outside the checkout with `-d` |
| Comment census reports `block census wrong: /**=0 */=0 //=0` | E-4 | The census was given the current commit as its baseline. Re-run with the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` |
| Byte-format census reports mixed line endings or `final terminator not CRLF` | E-5 | An editor normalised `Hello.java` to LF on save. Restore the file and re-apply the edit in byte mode, re-emitting CRLF on every line |
| `javadoc` reports one warning | E-6 | **Expected — no action.** The implicit default constructor can carry no doc comment; documenting it would require declaring a constructor, which is out of scope |
| Direct source launch fails on an older JDK | E-7 | Single-file source launch needs JDK 11 or later. Use the compile-then-run path, which has no such floor |

Re-running after a fix is safe, and the reasons are structural rather than conventional: the command is deterministic, the payload is a compile-time constant, no dependency is resolved, and each attempt gets a fresh `mktemp -d` directory. Where a row does not match, or where the fix is a policy decision rather than a correction, escalation is a documentary act — the item is written into `Project Guide.md` §1.4 with an owner and an ETA, and carried in the §6 register. Section 6.5.4.2 documents that three-level model (operator in session, maintainer out of session, owner decision) in full, and records that **there is no notification step at any level**.

#### 6.6.2.6 Flaky Test Management

**No flake tracking, quarantine list, retry-on-failure setting or test-stability history exists**, and the program itself supplies no source of nondeterminism to track: it reads no input, consults no clock, generates no random value, creates no thread, opens no resource and makes no network call, so a run's three observables are fixed by a compile-time constant. `README.md` line 46 states the resulting property — "Both paths produce byte-identical standard output."

Three *environment- or invocation-dependent* results do exist, and they are the honest analogue of flakiness in this project: each produces a different outcome from an unchanged tree, each has a documented cause, and each has a deterministic remedy rather than a retry.

| Condition | Why the result changes | Documented remedy |
|---|---|---|
| Comment census run with the default baseline | The check diffs the working source against a named revision; at `HEAD` the comments are already committed, so the diff is empty and four assertions fail vacuously — "a correct tree scores 33 of 37 checks when the baseline is not supplied" | Pass the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` as the baseline argument. The suite then passes 37 of 37. Carried as a Medium/High Open risk because "a contributor could read that as a broken deliverable" |
| Line endings rewritten by an editor | `Hello.java` is stored CRLF on all 20 lines with no `.gitattributes` and no line-ending policy file, so a tool that writes LF rewrites all five code lines and changes the file's content digest | Edit in byte mode, re-emit CRLF on added lines, and re-run the census. Status: "Open — accepted by design" |
| Host-dependent byte count of the payload | The program appends the platform line separator, so the payload is 17 bytes on an LF host and 18 on a CRLF host | The published contract asserts "the literal and its single trailing separator," never a fixed byte count — which is why the oracle comparison is stable across hosts while a byte-count assertion would not be |

One further result is **permanently non-zero by design and must not be treated as a failure**: the single `javadoc` warning for the implicit default constructor. Section 6.5.3.6 records it as the system's only standing "firing" condition, documented as requiring no action.

#### 6.6.2.7 Test Environment Architecture

The architecture below is the complete automation and environment picture. Every actor in it is either the operator, the JDK toolchain, the Git object store or a directory that exists for the duration of one run.

**Figure 6.6.2-A — Test environment architecture: the operator-driven toolchain, the per-run workspaces, the read-only sources of truth, and the automation infrastructure verified absent**

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Op["Operator shell session on a Linux host —<br/>the only runner, evaluator, reporter and<br/>responder in the system"]

    subgraph Prereq["Host prerequisites — all inherited, none provisioned by the repository"]
        P1["JDK on PATH: javac, java, javadoc.<br/>Recorded at OpenJDK 25.0.3; no version pinned"]
        P2["git, for the baseline comparisons.<br/>2.51.0 recorded, 2.43.0 observed here"]
        P3["POSIX shell with GNU grep, diff, awk,<br/>tr, od, cmp and coreutils"]
    end

    subgraph Sources["Read-only sources of truth — the checkout is never written to"]
        SRC["Hello.java — the unit under test:<br/>20 lines, 1073 bytes, 5 executable lines"]
        ORA["README.md lines 59-61 — the fenced<br/>output oracle, plus the stream and<br/>exit-status contract at line 63"]
        BASE["Git object store — revision 0726b1d<br/>supplies the reference implementation;<br/>14 commits, append-only"]
    end

    subgraph Workspaces["Per-run workspaces — mktemp -d, owner-readable only, discarded at teardown"]
        WB["B — build output: the 420-byte class file,<br/>kept outside the checkout so no<br/>untracked artifact appears"]
        WO["O — parity workspace: exported baseline source,<br/>two builds, four captured stream files"]

    end

    end

    subgraph Record["Durable record — hand-written Markdown, version-controlled"]
        E1["Project Guide sections 3 and 4:<br/>49 executed, 49 passed, 0 failed"]
        E2["Project Guide sections 5 and 6:<br/>compliance matrix, divergences, risk register"]
        E1 --> E2
    end

    subgraph Absent["Verified absent — no automation infrastructure exists or ever has"]
        NA1["No CI runner, workflow, job or agent;<br/>19 executor probes absent"]
        NA2["No active git hook; all 14 entries are samples.<br/>No cron, timer or scheduler"]
        NA3["No container, Compose file or devcontainer<br/>for a test environment"]
        NA4["No service virtualisation, stub server<br/>or recorded-response store"]

    end

    Op --> P1
    Op --> P2
    Op --> P3
    P1 -->|"compiles and launches"| WB
    P2 -->|"git show exports the baseline into"| WO
    P3 -->|"runs the suite from"| WS
    SRC -->|"read by javac and javadoc"| WB
    BASE -->|"reference implementation"| WO
    WB --> G1
    WB --> G2
    WB --> G3
    WO --> G4
    WS --> G4
    Sources --> G5
    G1 -->|"compared against the expected result"| Op
    G2 -->|"compared byte for byte against"| ORA
    G3 -->|"expected exactly one warning"| Op

```

Two properties of this architecture are worth stating plainly. First, **the runner and the assertion engine are the same human** — there is no process between the signal and the judgement, which is why every check is a comparison against a published literal rather than an executable assertion. Second, **the environment is created and destroyed per run**: nothing persists between executions except the checkout, the Git object store and the hand-written record, so there is no test database to reset, no cache to invalidate and no accumulated state that could make one run's result depend on another's.


### 6.6.3 Quality Metrics and Test Environment Requirements

Every quality figure in this sub-section is either **measured first-hand in the checkout** or **quoted as recorded** from `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md`. No coverage percentage, pass-rate target, latency budget or capacity figure exists in any tracked file, and none is invented here; where the prompt calls for a target, what is documented is the exact expectation the repository publishes and the absence of any threshold beyond it.

#### 6.6.3.1 Code Coverage Targets

**No coverage tool is configured and no coverage target is declared anywhere in the repository.** JaCoCo, Cobertura, Clover, `lcov`, Codecov and PIT are absent from the 23 coverage and quality probes, no manifest exists that could bind a coverage goal, and `Project Guide.md` §3 states outright that "there is no unit- or integration-test coverage figure to report."

Three coverage denominators are nonetheless published with exact expected values, and they are what the project measures in place of executed-line coverage.

| Coverage measure | Published expectation | Status at `HEAD` |
|---|---|---|
| Compilation-unit coverage | 1 of 1 unit compiled by every check that compiles | **Met** — 2 of 2 compilation checks passed |
| Documentable-member coverage | 2 of 3 members documented, with exactly **one** accepted `javadoc` warning at `Hello.java:6` | **Met, capped by design** — the implicit default constructor can carry no doc comment, and declaring one is a structural change the comment-only constraint forbids |
| Written-functionality comment coverage | 4 of 4 functionalities carry exactly one explanatory comment — class declaration, entry-point signature and parameter, output statement, termination path | **Met** — 7 of 7 comment-structure checks passed |
| Executable-line traversal | All five executable lines (6, 15, 17, 19, 20) lie on the program's single straight-line path, so any successful run traverses every one | **Structural, not instrumented** — no tool records it, and the figure is a property of a source with no branch and no loop |

#### 6.6.3.2 Test Success Rate Requirements

The success requirement in force is **total and exact**: every check has a literal expected value, there is no warning band and no partial credit, and Section 6.1.4.5 records that the architecture admits no degraded mode — either the full contract is met or the workflow never reached the program.

| Requirement | Recorded outcome |
|---|---|
| All acceptance and toolchain checks pass | **49 executed, 49 passed, 0 failed** on OpenJDK 25.0.3 — 37 acceptance assertions plus 12 direct toolchain checks |
| The acceptance suite passes in full when correctly invoked | **37 of 37** with the pre-comment revision `0726b1d` as the baseline; **33 of 37** on the same correct tree if the baseline argument is omitted |
| Zero-tolerance signals | Compiler diagnostics exactly 0 under `-Xlint:all -Werror`; standard-error volume exactly 0 bytes; exit status exactly 0 |
| The one permitted non-zero signal | Exactly **1** `javadoc` warning. Section 6.5.3.6 records that 0 or 2-or-more both indicate that comment coverage changed |
| Requirement-level satisfaction | Section 2.5.3 rolls up **45 requirements: 40 fully satisfied, 3 open, 2 partial**, and reconciles that against `Project Guide.md` §1.4's "No defect is open in the delivered code" — every unmet requirement corresponds to a recorded open item or owner decision rather than a defect |

Compliance is **binary per invocation** rather than aggregated over a window, and it is **unmeasured over time**: with nothing re-running any check and no execution history recorded, the 49-of-49 tally is a point-in-time observation rather than a trend.

#### 6.6.3.3 Performance Test Thresholds

**No performance threshold exists to test against.** Section 5.4.5 records that no latency target, throughput figure, availability objective, capacity plan, error budget or timing measurement appears in any tracked file, and the strict census reported in Section 6.5.1.1 returns zero hits for that vocabulary in `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE`. No load, soak, stress or benchmark harness is present, and no timing could be taken in this verification environment — neither a JDK nor `/usr/bin/time` is installed.

The exact quantities that function as thresholds are size and volume figures, not durations. They are tabulated with their sources in Section 6.6.1.4.4; the ones that carry a pass/fail meaning are the payload of 16 characters plus one platform separator, the standard-error volume of 0 bytes, the exit status of 0, and a dependency-resolution cost of 0 artifacts fetched.

#### 6.6.3.4 Quality Gates

Nine gates are documented, each with a command and a literal pass condition. **None is enforced mechanically**: no gate blocks a commit, a push or a merge, because no hook, pipeline or build task exists to evaluate one. Section 3.6.3 tabulates the same gates from the development-tooling perspective and records the structural gap as "Nothing re-runs any of these gates."

| Gate | Command | Pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| Compile | `javac Hello.java` | Exit 0, no diagnostics |
| Strict static analysis | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror -d "$B" Hello.java` | Exit 0, empty error stream. Appendix F names this "the project's static-analysis surface, as no linter is configured" |
| Documentation coverage | `javadoc -d "$B/jd" -quiet Hello.java` | Exit 0 with exactly one warning, for the implicit default constructor |
| Output contract | Capture standard output and compare against `README.md` lines 59–61 | Byte-identical to the fenced oracle; 17 bytes on an LF host |
| Behaviour parity | Build `0726b1d` and `HEAD`, run both, `cmp` both stream pairs | "behaviour identical" — standard output, standard error and exit status all match |
| Change shape | `diff` against the baseline, then count added lines and blocks | No deletions or modifications; `added=15 /**=2 */=2 //=2` |
| Stored byte format | Line-ending and terminator censuses | `Hello.java lf=20 cr=20 crlf=20`; `README.md cr=0` with a trailing newline. **Re-verified first-hand and matched** |
| Guide structure | `grep '^## '`, the summary word count, and the link census | Eight sections in the required order with Summary of Changes first; 55 words against a 70-word limit; exactly two relative links. **Re-verified first-hand and matched** |
| Clean tree | `git status --short` and `git ls-files` | No output from the first; the tracked inventory from the second |

#### 6.6.3.5 Security Testing Requirements

The security testing surface is shaped by what the program does not do. `Project Guide.md` §6 disposes of whole categories in a single sentence: the program "reads no input, dereferences no argument, opens no resource, binds no port, makes no network call and has no dependency manifest, so there is no injection surface, no supply-chain exposure, no authentication or authorisation surface and no data-at-rest concern." Five security checks are nonetheless in force, and three practices are absent and expected.

| Security check | What it establishes | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Abuse-case execution** | Runs "with no arguments, many arguments, and hostile arguments including shell and injection payloads all produce identical output; the parameter is never dereferenced." A first-hand census confirms `args[` occurs **zero times** in the source, so the array is never indexed | **Selected** — recorded in `Project Guide.md` §4 |
| **Input and egress surface census** | A 16-marker census over `Hello.java` for `Runtime`, `exec`, `ProcessBuilder`, `Socket`, `URL`, `http`, `File`, `Files`, `Reader`, `Writer`, `System.getenv`, `System.getProperty`, `Class.forName`, `reflect` and `serial` returns **zero hits** — there is no injection, deserialisation, path-traversal or request-forgery surface to test | **Selected** — measured first-hand |
| **Dependency and supply-chain scanning** | Vacuous by construction: §9.3 records no manifest or lock file of any kind and nothing downloaded at build time, so there is no transitive dependency to scan and no lockfile to audit | **Genuinely absent** — nothing to scan |
| **Secret scanning** | A 15-pattern census over `Hello.java` and `README.md` (`password`, `secret`, `token`, `api_key`, `AKIA`, `BEGIN RSA`, `BEGIN PRIVATE`, `credential`, `Authorization`, `Bearer`, `ssh-rsa`, `client_secret`, `private_key` and variants) returns **zero matches**. §9.2 records "No environment variable or secret is read by any tracked file" | **Selected** — measured first-hand |
| **Test-environment hardening** | The build destination must be a freshly generated owner-only directory. `README.md` line 30 states the threat: a fixed, predictable destination "can be pre-created, replaced or redirected through a symbolic link by another local process before the compiler writes into it" | **Selected and mitigated** — the register's only **Mitigated** risk, in the Security category |
| Static application security testing | No SAST tool is configured — `spotbugs.xml`, `pmd.xml`, `checkstyle.xml` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` are absent. The compiler's `-Xlint:all -Werror` is the substitute and the whole of it | **Absent and expected** (ADR-002) |
| Automated re-scanning | Nothing re-runs any of the above, so a future change that introduces an input surface would not be detected by any mechanism | **Absent and expected** — the Medium/Medium Open gate risk |
| Vulnerability disclosure path | No `SECURITY.md`, `SUPPORT.md` or contact address exists in any tracked file, so there is no route by which a finding could be reported | **Absent and expected** — Section 6.4.5.3 carries it as a residual risk with no compensating control |

One licence-compliance check belongs in this list because it is asserted mechanically alongside the others: the GPLv3 dated-modification notice at `README.md:5` is verified as present (compliance matrix row 8), and `LICENSE` is verified untouched at 674 lines and 35,149 bytes.

#### 6.6.3.6 Conditions That Would Make a Detailed Testing Strategy Applicable

The determination in Section 6.6.1.1 is a statement about the repository at commit `2a78292` on branch `jr_java1`, not a permanent property. Each change below satisfies one of the failed preconditions T1–T7 and would oblige this section to be rewritten as a substantive testing strategy rather than amended.

| Repository change | Precondition it would satisfy | Sub-sections that would need content |
|---|---|---|
| A second method, class or compilation unit | T1 — a unit to isolate | 6.6.1.2 in full; a test source tree would have to be chosen |
| Any `interface`, `abstract` type, field or constructor parameter | T2 — a substitutable seam | 6.6.1.2.3 mocking strategy, which is currently vacuous |
| A return value, thrown exception or mutated state | T3 — something to assert on | 6.6.1.2 assertions; 6.6.3.1 would gain a real coverage denominator |
| Any input path — `args[…]`, `System.in`, a file read, an environment variable | T3 and the security surface | 6.6.1.2.6 test data would gain inputs; 6.6.3.5 would need injection, traversal and fuzz testing |
| A second component, socket, HTTP call, broker or datastore | T4 — an integration boundary | 6.6.1.3 in full; 6.6.1.3.4 external service mocking; a test-environment provisioning model |
| A UI, hosted page or bound port | T5 — a surface to drive | 6.6.1.4.2 UI automation; 6.6.1.4.5 would become a genuine cross-browser matrix |
| Any manifest — `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `package.json` | T6 — a place to declare a test dependency and a test task | 6.6.1.2.1 frameworks; 6.6.3.1 coverage tooling; 6.6.3.4 gates would become enforceable |
| A CI descriptor, active Git hook, cron entry or systemd timer | T7 — an automated executor | 6.6.2 in full — triggers, parallelism, reporting and flake management all become real concerns; ADR-002 would be superseded |
| A declared performance budget, SLO or benchmark | A threshold to test against | 6.6.1.4.4 and 6.6.3.3, which currently record baselines but no target |
| A pinned JDK version or `.gitattributes` | — | Would close two recorded risks rather than create a new test obligation: the unpinned-toolchain risk and the CRLF-normalisation risk that makes the byte-format gate necessary |

Two further changes would **not** make a testing strategy applicable but would each close a limitation this section records. **Committing the V1–V9 suite together with an executor** would turn the point-in-time 49-of-49 record into a repeatable signal; it is the `[Deferred]` item in `Project Guide.md` §1.4 and the Medium/Medium Open risk in §6, which §8 calls "the one recommendation that outlives this change." **Adding a `.gitignore`** would remove the standing false-positive source behind fault E-3, which exists only because an in-place compile leaves an untracked class file that no ignore rule covers.

#### 6.6.3.7 Test Environment and Resource Requirements

The environment requirement is a **single-host, single-process, offline one**, and its whole surface is enumerated in `Project Guide.md` §9.1–§9.3.

| Resource | Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Toolchain | A JDK on `PATH` — `javac`, `java`, `javadoc`. No version is pinned; the checks were recorded on OpenJDK 25.0.3, and the compile-then-run path was exercised at release targets 11, 17 and 21 | §9.1, Appendix D |
| Version control | `git`, required not only to clone but to supply the baseline revision `0726b1d` used by the parity and change-shape gates | §9.1, §9.6 |
| Shell utilities | A POSIX shell with GNU `grep`, `diff`, `awk`, `tr`, `od`, `cmp`, `iconv` and `coreutils` — needed for the structural censuses, which "assert the guide's structure and both files' stored byte format directly against the source, so verification needs no renderer and no extra runtime" | §9.1, Appendix F |
| Network | **None.** Nothing is downloaded at build time and the program makes no network call, so the entire procedure runs offline | §9.3; `README.md` line 18 |
| Infrastructure | **None.** "No package manager step, no virtual environment, no container, no database, no broker and no bound port" | §9.1, Appendix B |
| Configuration and credentials | **None.** "Nothing to configure. No environment variable or secret is read by any tracked file," and `JAVA_HOME` is not required | §9.2, Appendix E |
| Compute per run | One JVM process per launch; one written file descriptor; zero threads created by the program; a 4-instruction `main` | Section 6.5.3.5; `Hello.java` lines 15–19 |
| Disk per run | One 420-byte class file plus generated `javadoc` HTML, in `mktemp -d` directories removed at teardown. Zero bytes are persisted by the program | Section 5.4.5; §9.6 |
| Environment tiers | **None.** "No environment-specific configuration exists to differentiate dev, test and production" — any host with a JDK and a POSIX shell is the test environment | Section 3.6.6 |

The one hard dependency was demonstrated by its absence: in the environment used to verify this section `java`, `javac` and `javadoc` are not installed and every invocation exits **127**, which blocks every JDK-dependent gate while leaving all Git- and shell-based gates fully executable — and those were re-run and matched their published expectations.

#### 6.6.3.8 Documentation Requirements

Because the checks are not committed, **the documentation *is* the test artifact**, and the repository imposes requirements on it that a test suite would normally encode in code.

| Requirement | Obligation | Where satisfied |
|---|---|---|
| Every command carries its expected result | Nine command rows, each with the exact signal an operator should see | `Project Guide.md` Appendix A |
| Every verification step carries its expected value | Literal counts and outcomes inline with each command — warning count, `cmp` verdict, census tallies, structure counts | `Project Guide.md` §9.6 |
| Uncovered areas are stated explicitly | A five-item "Not Covered" list, including the absence of any unit or integration test and the unexercised JDK 11 runtime | `Project Guide.md` §3 |
| Every fault has a documented resolution | A seven-row symptom / cause / resolution table serving as the runbook | `Project Guide.md` §9.8 |
| Verification tooling is documented but never committed | The suite is reproduced in the project specification and must be saved to a scratch file outside the checkout | `Project Guide.md` §9.6 |
| Toolchain provenance is recorded | The versions every recorded result was observed on, and the statement that no version is pinned | `Project Guide.md` Appendix D |
| Source is cited by stable symbol, never by line number | Because inserting comments shifts every line below them, citations take the form `Source: Hello.java (Hello.main)`. Recorded as **Partial** — 2 of 2 required references present, but only 2 of 7 body sections carry one | `README.md:14`, `:53`; compliance row 11 |
| The documentation itself is gated | Eight ordered sections, a 55-word summary against a 70-word limit, italics on exactly the two changed files and nowhere else, exactly two resolvable relative links, and a dated GPLv3 modification notice | `Project Guide.md` §3 (V6–V9), §5.1 rows 5–9 |

One documentation defect is recorded as open rather than fixed, and it is a reminder of why the gate matters: `README.md` line 67 still describes the repository as "three tracked files at the root, and no subdirectories," which `git ls-files` contradicts at `HEAD` with five tracked files and a `blitzy/documentation/` subtree. Section 2.5.3 carries it as the open requirement F-007-RQ-006 — a claim that drifted precisely because nothing re-runs the structural checks.

#### 6.6.3.9 Test Data Flow

**Figure 6.6.3-A — Test data flow: where each expected value comes from, what each run produces, and the single comparison that turns the two into a result**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Expected["Expected-value sources — version-controlled, read-only"]
        X1["README.md lines 59-61:<br/>fenced oracle, the 16-byte literal"]
        X2["README.md line 63: stderr empty,<br/>exit status 0, no System.exit"]
        X3["Project Guide section 9.6:<br/>published literals — added=15, blocks 2 and 2,<br/>lf=20 cr=20 crlf=20, 8 sections, 55 words, 2 links"]
        X4["Git object store at 0726b1d:<br/>the pre-comment Hello.java blob"]
    end

    subgraph Produced["Produced per run — transient, discarded at teardown"]
        Y1["Compiled class in B<br/>plus javac exit status and error stream"]
        Y2["Captured stdout and stderr files in O,<br/>for both the current and baseline builds"]
        Y3["javadoc warning count<br/>and generated HTML in B/jd"]
        Y4["Shell census counts over<br/>Hello.java and README.md"]
        Y5["git status --short and git ls-files output"]
    end

    subgraph Compare["Comparison — performed by the operator, no assertion engine exists"]
        Z1{"cmp: stdout and stderr byte-identical<br/>to the baseline build?"}
        Z2{"stdout byte-identical to the oracle,<br/>stderr empty, exit status 0?"}
        Z3{"Census counts equal to the<br/>published literals?"}
        Z4{"Exactly one javadoc warning,<br/>and a clean working tree?"}
    end

    Result(["Result: pass or fail, per check.<br/>49 of 49 recorded on OpenJDK 25.0.3"])
    Written["Hand-written into Project Guide<br/>sections 3, 4, 5 and 6 — the only<br/>record that survives the run"]
    Lost["Not recorded anywhere: that a run occurred,<br/>when, on what host, or with what timing"]
    Teardown["rm -rf B O S, then<br/>git status --short expecting no output"]

    X4 -->|"git show exports into O/base"| Y2
    X1 --> Z2
    X2 --> Z2
    X3 --> Z3
    Y1 --> Z4
    Y2 --> Z1
    Y2 --> Z2
    Y3 --> Z4
    Y4 --> Z3
    Y5 --> Z4
    Z1 --> Result
    Z2 --> Result
    Z3 --> Result
    Z4 --> Result
    Result --> Written
    Result -.->|"everything else about the run"| Lost
    Produced -.-> Teardown
```

Two properties of this flow are worth stating plainly. **Every expected value is a literal held in a tracked Markdown file**, not in code — which is why the documentation is gated as tightly as the source. And **the flow is one-way and lossy**: the produced side is deleted at teardown and only the pass/fail judgement is transcribed, so no run can be re-examined after the fact.

# 7. User Interface Design

## 7.1 User Interface Assessment

**No user interface required.**

This project defines no user interface, so there is nothing in this section to specify. Across the five tracked files — `Hello.java`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` and `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` — and the single subdirectory `blitzy/documentation/`, there is no screen, view, page, template, markup asset, stylesheet, icon, font, window, widget, form, menu or interactive prompt, and no such artifact has existed at any point in the repository's history on any branch. The entire human-facing surface of the system is one fixed line of text written to standard output by the single statement `System.out.println("Hello from Java!")` at `Hello.java` line 17.

The repository states the same conclusion in its own records. `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` line 130 opens its runtime-validation section with "The program is a console application with no user interface, no hosted page, no bound port and no external integration," and line 143 adds that "There is no UI and no hosted page, and the guide's structure was asserted against its Markdown source rather than a rendered page, so nothing here was verified through a browser." Section 1.3.2.1 reaches the same verdict from the scope side, listing "User interface of any kind" among the explicitly excluded capabilities with the note "Console output only; no UI, hosted page, or port."

The sub-sections below record the evidence for that determination, describe the console surface that exists in place of a user interface, dispose of each topic this section would otherwise have covered, separate documentation rendering from an application UI, and state the conditions under which this section would have to be written for real.

### 7.1.1 Basis for the Determination

Every precondition for a user interface was probed against the working tree rather than assumed absent. Each row names what was looked for and what established its absence.

| UI precondition probed | Observed | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screen, view or page source | None | A file-extension census over the whole worktree excluding `.git` returned **zero** files for each of 45 UI-bearing extensions, including `.html`, `.htm`, `.xhtml`, `.jsp`, `.jsx`, `.tsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.fxml`, `.qml`, `.xaml`, `.storyboard`, `.mustache`, `.hbs`, `.ftl`, `.twig`, `.ejs` and `.pug`. The tracked extension census is one `.java`, three `.md` and one extension-less `LICENSE` |
| UI asset directory | None | Existence tests for 30 conventional UI directories — `src`, `resources`, `static`, `public`, `assets`, `templates`, `views`, `layouts`, `webapp`, `www`, `ui`, `frontend`, `client`, `pages`, `components`, `styles`, `images`, `fonts`, `locales`, `i18n`, `node_modules`, `.storybook` among them — all reported absent. The only directories in the repository are `blitzy/` and `blitzy/documentation/`, which hold two Markdown documents and no assets |
| Desktop GUI toolkit | None | `Hello.java` contains zero occurrences of `javax.swing`, `java.awt`, `javafx`, `java.applet`, `JFrame`, `JPanel`, `Scene`, `Stage`, `Canvas`, `Toolkit`, `Desktop` and `JOptionPane`. The file declares no `import` and no `package` at all, so the only types it can name are those of `java.lang`; Section 3.2.2 records the complete API surface as `System.out`, `println(String)` and `String` |
| Web front end | None | Zero `servlet`, `jsp`, `springframework`, `thymeleaf`, `freemarker`, `velocity`, `react`, `vue`, `angular`, `svelte`, `jquery`, `bootstrap`, `tailwind`, `electron`, `document.`, `window.`, `addEventListener`, `innerHTML`, `<html`, `<div` or `<body` tokens in the source or the operator guide; no `package.json`, lockfile or bundler configuration exists. Section 3.2.1 records the same null result for every framework channel |
| Mobile UI | None | No Android manifest, layout resource, `.xib`/`.storyboard`/`.plist` file or mobile project structure; no `android`, `xcode` or `storyboard` token anywhere in the source or guide |
| Interactive console prompt | None | Zero `System.in`, `Scanner`, `BufferedReader`, `readLine`, `Console` and `System.console` tokens. `README.md` line 12 states the program "reads no input, opens no resource and keeps no state," and Section 1.3.1.2 records the input surface as "None — no stdin read, no file read, no arguments consulted" |
| Command-line presentation logic | None | `args` appears only in the `@param` tag at `Hello.java` lines 11–13 and in the signature at line 15, never in an executable statement, so there is no flag, sub-command, `--help` text or usage screen. No CLI framework token — `picocli`, `commons-cli`, `jline`, `jansi`, `getopt`, `curses`, `ncurses` — appears anywhere |
| Terminal styling or layout control | None | `Hello.java` holds no ANSI escape byte and no non-printable byte outside CR/LF, and its only string literal is the 16-character ASCII `Hello from Java!`, so no colour, bold, cursor positioning, spinner, progress bar or table layout can be produced |
| Image, icon or font asset | None | Zero `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.ico`, `.webp`, `.ttf`, `.woff`, `.woff2` or `.eot` files anywhere in the tree; no `favicon.ico` and no `manifest.json` |
| Network-served interface | None | No port is bound and no listener is started, so no interface could be served: `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix B records "Not applicable. The program binds no port, starts no listener and makes no network call," and §9.1 confirms "no bound port" among the prerequisites. `Hello.java` contains zero `ServerSocket`, `Socket`, `HttpServer` and `@WebServlet` tokens |
| UI artifact in project history | None | `git log --all --name-only` over every ref shows the only paths ever committed are the five tracked today. No UI artifact was added and later removed on any branch |
| Indexed UI content | None | A semantic file search for user-interface screens, views, pages and rendered templates returned no results, and a folder search for frontend components, static web assets and stylesheets returned none |

Two artifacts that appear outside the tracked set are also not user interfaces: the untracked `tech_spec.md` at the root is a documentation authoring artifact, and the `Hello.class` produced by a build is compiled bytecode that `README.md` line 30 instructs must not be committed.
