### 9.3.4 Closing Order

The items are not independent. Four of them determine whether the most valuable one would produce a sound result, and three others only become enforceable once it exists.

**Figure 9.3.4-A — Prerequisite order among the open items: the four on the left must be settled before an automated gate would return a trustworthy verdict**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    OI3["OI-3 pin the toolchain"] --> Gate
    OI1["OI-1 close the<br/>silent-loss gap"] --> Gate
    OI13["OI-13 fix the census<br/>baseline invocation"] --> Gate
    OI5["OI-5 add build-output<br/>hygiene"] --> Gate
    Gate["OI-6 commit an automated gate<br/>cold suite recorded at 779 ms"]
    Gate --> OI2["OI-2 licence-header check<br/>becomes enforceable"]
    Gate --> OI7["OI-7 documentation-coverage check<br/>becomes enforceable"]
    Gate --> OI8["OI-8 release identity gives<br/>per-release runs meaning"]
    Indep["Independent of the gate:<br/>OI-4 line-ending policy,<br/>OI-10 disclosure path,<br/>OI-11 signing policy"]
```

The ordering is measured rather than conventional. Automating a gate before OI-13 is settled would automate a false failure, because a correct tree scores 33 of 37 under the default baseline; automating it before OI-3 is settled would make the verdict a property of whichever JDK the runner happens to install, since Section 9.1.3 records that a single release-target difference changes the artifact's digest. The cost argument points the other way: the archived specification measured the whole cold sequence — compile, static gate, run — at 779 ms, so a gate for this repository is bounded by well under two seconds of compute. As `Project Guide.md` §8 puts it, the absent gate is "the one recommendation that outlives this change."

### 9.3.5 Absence of an In-Repository Register

None of these items is recorded as an item anywhere in the tracked tree. A marker census over `Hello.java`, `README.md` and `LICENSE` returns **zero** occurrences of `TODO`, `FIXME`, `XXX`, `HACK` or `BUG` — the only tracked file matching any of those words is the archived specification, and there only in prose about the census itself — and no `CHANGELOG`, `TODO`, `ROADMAP`, `ISSUES` or `BACKLOG` file exists at any name tested. Both facts were measured here at `HEAD`.

The consequence is procedural rather than technical. `Project Guide.md` §1.4 and this register are the only places the items exist, so a change made without reference to one of them can reopen a closed item — or close one — without anything recording that it did. That is the same structural gap OI-6 describes, viewed from the bookkeeping side rather than the verification side.


## 9.4 Glossary

These are the terms this specification uses in a sense that is specific to this repository, or that a reader of a normal Java project specification would not expect to carry the meaning it carries here. Each entry gives the general definition and then what the term denotes concretely at commit `2a78292`. The three evidence and status vocabularies — *static* / *recorded* / *open*, *Stated* / *Recorded* / *Reconstructed*, and *Genuinely absent* / *Selected* / *Inherited* / *Absent and expected* — are defined in Section 9.2.5 and are not repeated here.

### 9.4.1 Java Platform and Toolchain Terms

| Term | Definition | Concretely, in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry point | The `public static void main(String[])` method a JVM launcher invokes to start a program | `Hello.java` line 15; interface seam I-2; feature F-001 |
| Compilation unit | One `.java` source file presented to the compiler | `Hello.java`, the only one that has ever existed; 1,073 bytes, 20 lines, 5 of them executable |
| Default (unnamed) package | The package a compilation unit belongs to when it declares none | The reason the class launches as `java Hello` rather than by a qualified name, and the reason it cannot be imported by packaged code; ADR-001 |
| Class file | The compiled binary representation of one Java type | `Hello.class`, 420 bytes (recorded), produced per run and never tracked; zero `*.class` blobs exist in the history |
| Class-file major version | The two-byte field naming the format level a class file targets | Recorded as 65 at target 21; targets 8, 11, 17 and 21 differ in exactly one byte (Section 9.1.3) |
| Constant pool | The table of literals and symbolic references carried inside a class file | 28 entries, of which one `String` entry holds `Hello from Java!` — the whole of the system's data at rest |
| Bytecode instruction | A single operation in the JVM instruction set | 4 in `main` (`getstatic`, `ldc`, `invokevirtual`, `return`) and 3 in the implicit constructor |
| Implicit default constructor | The no-argument constructor the language supplies because the class declares none | The third documentable member; it can carry no doc comment, which is why exactly one `javadoc` warning stands by design and coverage is capped at 2 of 3 |
| Documentable member | A construct `javadoc` expects a doc comment on | Three exist: the class, `main`, and the implicit constructor |
| Single-file source launch | Running `java Hello.java` with no separate compile step, available from JDK 11 onward | Workflow W-3; leaves no class file; the one version floor the repository states, and the one it has never exercised on a JDK 11 runtime |
| Platform line separator | The newline sequence the host defines, appended by `println` | Why the contract is stated as the literal plus one separator rather than a byte count: 17 bytes under LF, 18 under CRLF, 36 under a UTF-16 sink (Section 9.1.4) |
| Classpath | The search path the launcher uses to resolve a class | Supplied explicitly only in the out-of-tree path, as `java -cp "$B" Hello`; omitted in the in-place path because the class sits in the working directory |
| Implicit `java.lang` import | The package every compilation unit imports without declaring it | The entire library surface of this program; `System`, `PrintStream`, `String` and `Object` are the only types bound, and `jdeps` reports `java.base` as the only module requirement |
| Release target | The `--release` or `--source` setting that fixes the language and API level | **None is declared anywhere in the repository.** `Project Guide.md` Appendix D records the language level as "None declared" |
| Static-analysis surface | The set of automated checks applied to the source | `javac -Xlint:all -Werror` and nothing else; no linter, formatter or SAST tool is configured (ADR-002) |
| Doc-comment lint | `javadoc -Xdoclint:all`, which validates doc-comment syntax and tag usage | The project's comment-coverage gate; its HTML output is never committed |

### 9.4.2 Repository, Version-Control and Distribution Terms

| Term | Definition | Concretely, in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blob, tree, commit | The three content-addressed object types Git stores | 10 blobs, 13 trees and 14 commits at `HEAD` — 37 objects, 947,449 raw bytes, one pack of 307,997 bytes |
| Content addressing | Naming an object by the hash of its contents | The system's only integrity mechanism; the object format is SHA-1, and `git hash-object` reproduces each tracked blob's name |
| Packfile and delta chain | The compressed object store and the chains of differences inside it | One pack: 24 objects stored whole, 10 at chain length 1, 3 at chain length 2 |
| Baseline revision | A named commit used as the reference implementation for a comparison | `0726b1d`, the pre-comment revision; supplies both the behaviour-parity build and the additions-only census, and its omission is OI-13 |
| Reflog | The clone-local journal of ref movements | `.git/logs/HEAD`, 599 bytes, untracked — conveyed by no clone |
| Ancestor and fast-forward | A commit reachable from another, and the merge that needs no new commit | `main` is an ancestor of `HEAD`, 11 commits behind; the delivery gap F-005-RQ-005 records |
| Merge commit | A commit with more than one parent | `2a78292`, parents `0726b1d` and `b4a1188`, committer `GitHub` — and, uniquely here, a merge whose tree is identical to one parent's |
| Signature status | Git's `%G?` verdict on a commit signature | `E` on 4 commits (a signature is present but unverifiable without the signer's key) and `N` on 10 (unsigned); `commit.gpgsign` is unset |
| Untracked artifact | A file present in the working tree that Git does not track | Two kinds occur: `Hello.class` from an in-place compile (fault E-3), and `tech_spec.md`, an authoring artifact excluded from every census |
| Source-only distribution | Delivery as source from a clone, with no built artifact published | No packaging step, no coordinates, zero tags across 14 commits; every version reference is a commit SHA |
| Per-run scratch directory | A directory created fresh for one invocation and removed afterwards | `B="$(mktemp -d)"` and its siblings `$O` and `$S`; measured mode 2700 inside a mode-2777 `/tmp`, which is the whole of ADR-009's threat model |
| Stored byte format | The exact bytes a file occupies in the tree, including line terminators | `Hello.java` is CRLF on all 20 lines and pure ASCII; the other text files are LF-only; nothing normalises either, so the format is load-bearing rather than incidental |

### 9.4.3 Licensing Terms

| Term | Definition | Concretely, in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copyleft | A licence condition requiring derivative works to carry the same terms | GPL v3, dated 29 June 2007, verbatim in `LICENSE`; ADR-010 |
| Conveying | The licence's term for transferring a copy to another party | Here, a clone or fetch from the hosting remote — the only conveyance mechanism the project uses |
| Corresponding Source | The source form the licence requires to accompany a non-source conveyance | Never at issue: nothing non-source is ever conveyed, because no compiled or packaged artifact is tracked |
| Appropriate Legal Notices | The copyright and warranty notices the licence expects a work to display | The subject of the one licence gap: no per-file notice exists because no rights holder or year is recorded (OI-2, F-006-RQ-005) |
| Dated modification notice | A statement that a covered work was changed, and when | `README.md` line 5, "*Modified 2026-09-16.*" — the mechanism chosen in place of per-file notices |
| Verbatim copy | A conveyed copy whose text is unaltered | `LICENSE` at 674 lines and 35,149 bytes, unchanged since `c537a19` and confirmed by digest across both specification generations (Section 9.1.1) |
| Warranty disclaimer and liability limitation | GPL v3 §§15–17 | The project's entire warranty position; no other undertaking, SLA or guarantee exists in any tracked file |

### 9.4.4 Architecture, Verification and Operations Terms

| Term | Definition | Concretely, in this system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Written functionality | A construct actually present in the source that takes exactly one explanatory comment | Four exist — the class declaration, the entry-point signature and its parameter, the output statement, the termination path — and all four are commented (`Project Guide.md` Appendix G) |
| Stable-symbol citation | A source reference written as a symbol rather than a line number, because inserting comments shifts every line below them | `Source: Hello.java (Hello.main)` at `README.md` line 53 and its companion at line 14; coverage is 2 of 7 body sections, which is why F-007-RQ-004 is partial |
| Comment-only, additions-only edit | A change in which every added line is a comment and no existing line is deleted or modified | The delivered change: 15 lines added, none removed, with the 5 executable lines occupying byte-for-byte the 127 bytes of the original file (ADR-008, Section 9.1.2) |
| Behaviour parity | Byte-identical standard output, standard error and exit status between two builds | Established by `cmp` against a build of `0726b1d`, with debug information suppressed so the class files themselves compare identical |
| Output oracle | The published expected value a run is compared against | The fenced `text` block at `README.md` lines 59–61 — a 16-byte literal held in a Markdown file, not in code |
| Acceptance group | One of the repository's own check groups | `V1` … `V9`, run from a scratch directory outside the checkout and never committed; 37 assertions plus 12 toolchain checks |
| Quality gate | A check with a command and a literal pass condition | Nine are documented in Section 6.6.3.4; **none is enforced**, because no hook, pipeline or build task exists to evaluate one |
| Fault and runbook | A catalogued failure mode and the document that resolves it | `E-1` … `E-7`, one per row of the seven-row troubleshooting table in `Project Guide.md` §9.8 |
| Applicability determination | The verdict-first pattern by which a section records that a standard concern does not apply, then addresses each of its parts anyway | Used in Sections 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.5, 6.6, 7.1 and 8.1, each with a tested precondition set |
| Attack-surface elimination | Achieving a security posture by removing the surface rather than by adding a control | Section 5.3.6's position: one positive mechanism is selected — the owner-only build destination — and every other category is absent rather than mitigated |
| Statelessness by construction | Holding no state because the code declares none, rather than as a policy | No field, no instance, no persistence; nothing can be carried between runs even if a later requirement wanted it (ADR-004) |
| Invoke-and-exit | An execution model in which the process exists only for the duration of one unit of work | One process, one thread of control, one statement of work; there is no resident instance to probe, scale or monitor |
| Silent-loss gap | A failure that produces a success status | OI-1: a rejected write to standard output still yields exit status 0 with an empty error stream, because the source queries no stream error state |
| Frozen tree | A tracked tree that later commits do not change | Tree `a837de2a` has been the tracked content since `297792f`; five subsequent commits, including `HEAD`, alter nothing (Section 9.1.7) |

### 9.4.5 Relationship to the Repository's Own Glossary

`blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` Appendix G defines seven terms of its own: written functionality, stable-symbol citation, default package, single-file source launch, platform line separator, comment-only edit and implicit default constructor. All seven appear above, with the same meaning and with the repository's definition preserved; the entries here add the measured or `HEAD`-accurate detail that the Appendix G table does not carry. Where the two differ in wording only, the repository's wording governs, since it is the tracked artifact.

### 9.6.6 Verification Notes

Three limits on this appendix's evidence should be read alongside it.

**No JDK is present in the environment used to produce it.** Every figure describing the compiled artifact, the JVM's behaviour, an encoding sensitivity, a runtime footprint or a timing is therefore labelled *recorded* and attributed to the tracked artifact that observed it — `blitzy/documentation/Project Guide.md` on OpenJDK 25.0.3, or the archived `blitzy/documentation/Technical Specifications.md` on a `javac`/`java` 21.0.12 host. None was re-derived here, and Sections 9.1.3 and 9.1.5 name the two respects in which the archived figures pertain to a different toolchain and a different revision of the source.

**The archived measurements are observations, not requirements.** Section 9.1.5 reproduces timing and memory figures that exist nowhere else in this document precisely because Sections 5.4.5, 6.5.3.2 and 6.6.1.4.4 are correct that the repository declares no performance target. A one-off measurement and a threshold are different objects, and nothing in this appendix converts one into the other.

**One file in the working tree is excluded from every census.** `tech_spec.md` is untracked, is an authoring artifact of the documentation process, and is byte-identical to the committed archive — as the shared MD5 in Section 9.1.1 demonstrates. It is not a system file and appears in no count, digest table or diagram above. The credential embedded in the clone's own `.git/config` is likewise never reproduced, in this appendix or anywhere else in this specification.
